Sesagāthāsu heṭṭhā vuttanayattā uttānatthamevāti.

83. Recalling his past deed, and by way of joy revealing the Apadāna of his former conduct, he spoke the words beginning, 'When the Lord of the World had attained Nibbāna.' Therein, 'attained Nibbāna' (`nibbute`) means: when the Teacher had attained Parinibbāna by way of the Parinibbāna of the aggregates. The meaning is: while the body of Vipassī, the Fully Enlightened One, was being placed upon the constructed pyre, 'I took a fully bloomed lotus cluster, placed it on the pyre, and worshipped it.' In the remaining verses, because the method has been explained previously and because the meaning is plain, it is easily understood.

Padumacchadaniyattheraapadānavaṇṇanā samattā.

The commentary on the Apadāna of the Elder Padumacchadaniya is complete.

7. Sayanadāyakattheraapadānavaṇṇanā

7. Commentary on the Apadāna of the Elder Sayanadāyaka

Siddhatthassa bhagavatotiādikaṃ āyasmato sayanadāyakattherassa apadānaṃ. Ayampi purimabuddhesu katādhikāro tattha tattha bhave vivaṭṭūpanissayāni puññāni upacinanto siddhatthassa bhagavato kāle [P 0.0373] aññatarasmiṃ kule nibbatto viññutaṃ patto satthari pasīditvā hatthidaṇḍasuvaṇṇādīhi sayanatthāya mañcaṃ kāretvā anagghehi vicittattharaṇehi attharitvā bhagavantaṃ pūjesi. So bhagavā tassānukampāya paṭiggahetvā anubhavi. So tena puññakammena dibbamanussasampattiyo anubhavitvā imasmiṃ buddhuppāde ekasmiṃ kulagehe nibbatto viññutaṃ patvā satthu sāsane pasanno pabbajitvā vipassanaṃ ārabhitvā nacirasseva arahā ahosi. Pubbe katapuññanāmena sayanadāyakattheroti pākaṭo.

The words beginning, 'Of the Blessed One Siddhattha,' are the Apadāna of the Venerable Sayanadāyaka Thera. He too, having made a foundation under former Buddhas and accumulating merits that are a supporting condition for turning away from the round of rebirths in various existences, was born into a certain family during the time of the Blessed One Siddhattha. Having reached maturity and gained faith in the Teacher, he had a couch made for the purpose of reclining, with ivory, gold, and so forth. Having spread it with priceless, variegated coverings, he worshipped the Blessed One. That Blessed One, out of compassion for him, accepted and used it. He, through that meritorious deed, experienced divine and human prosperities. In this Buddha-era, he was born into a certain family, reached maturity, gained faith in the Teacher's Dispensation, went forth, and having undertaken insight, became an Arahant before long. By the name of the merit performed in the past, he became known as Sayanadāyaka Thera.

88. So [V 2.0066] ekadivasaṃ attano pubbakammaṃ saritvā somanassajāto pubbacaritāpadānaṃ pakāsento siddhatthassa bhagavatotiādimāha. Taṃ sabbaṃ pāḷinayānusārena suviññeyyamevāti.

88. One day, he, recollecting his past deed, and with joy arisen, revealed the Apadāna of his former conduct, speaking the words beginning, 'Of the Blessed One Siddhattha.' All of that is easily understood in accordance with the method of the Pāli text.

Sayanadāyakattheraapadānavaṇṇanā samattā.

The commentary on the Apadāna of the Elder Sayanadāyaka is complete.

8. Caṅkamanadāyakattheraapadānavaṇṇanā

8. Commentary on the Apadāna of the Elder Caṅkamanadāyaka

Atthadassissa [M 2.0073] muninotiādikaṃ āyasmato caṅkamanadāyakattherassa apadānaṃ. Ayampāyasmā purimabuddhesu katādhikāro tesu tesu bhavesu vivaṭṭūpanissayāni puññāni upacinanto atthadassissa bhagavato kāle ekasmiṃ kulagehe nibbatto viññutaṃ patto satthari pasīditvā uccavatthukaṃ sudhāparikammakataṃ rajatarāsisadisaṃ sobhamānaṃ caṅkamaṃ kāretvā muttadalasadisaṃ setapulinaṃ attharitvā bhagavato adāsi. Paṭiggahesi bhagavā, caṅkamaṃ paṭiggahetvā ca pana sukhaṃ kāyacittasamādhiṃ appetvā “ayaṃ anāgate gotamassa bhagavato sāsane sāvako bhavissatī”ti byākāsi. So tena puññakammena devamanussesu aparāparaṃ saṃsaranto dve sampattiyo anubhavitvā imasmiṃ buddhuppāde ekasmiṃ kulagehe nibbatto vuddhippatto saddhāsampanno sāsane pabbajitvā nacirasseva arahattaṃ patvā katapuññanāmena caṅkamanadāyakattheroti pākaṭo ahosi.

This is the Apadāna of the Venerable Elder Caṅkamanadāyaka, beginning with 'Atthadassissa munino'. This venerable one, having made a resolution under previous Buddhas, accumulated merits in various existences that served as a supporting condition for turning away from saṃsāra. During the time of the Blessed One Atthadassī, he was born into a certain family, and having attained discernment, he gained faith in the Teacher. He had a walking path constructed on high ground, plastered with stucco, shining like a heap of silver; and having spread white sand like a layer of pearls, he gave it to the Blessed One. The Blessed One accepted it. Having accepted the walkway, he entered into a pleasant concentration of body and mind and made this prediction: 'In the future, this one will be a disciple in the Dispensation of the Blessed One Gotama.' Through that meritorious deed, he wandered from life to life among devas and humans, experiencing divine and human prosperity. In this Buddha-era, he was born into a certain family, and upon reaching maturity, being endowed with faith, he went forth in the Dispensation. Before long, he attained arahantship and became known as the Elder Caṅkamanadāyaka, by the name of the meritorious deed he had performed.

93. So ekadivasaṃ attanā pubbe katapuññakammaṃ saritvā somanassajāto pubbacaritāpadānaṃ pakāsento atthadassissa muninotiādimāha. Tattha atthadassissāti atthaṃ payojanaṃ vuddhiṃ virūḷhiṃ nibbānaṃ dakkhati passatīti atthadassī, atha vā atthaṃ nibbānaṃ dassanasīlo jānanasīloti atthadassī, tassa atthadassissa munino monena ñāṇena samannāgatassa bhagavato manoramaṃ manallīnaṃ bhāvanīyaṃ manasi kātabbaṃ caṅkamaṃ kāresinti sambandho. Sesaṃ vuttanayānusāreneva suviññeyyamevāti.

93. One day, recalling the meritorious deed he had formerly performed, he became filled with joy and, proclaiming the Apadāna of his past conduct, spoke the verse beginning 'Atthadassissa munino'. Therein, 'Atthadassī' means one who sees (dassī) the goal (attha)—that is, the purpose, growth, development, and Nibbāna. Or else, 'Atthadassī' means one whose nature it is to see (dassanasīlo) and to know (jānanasīlo) the goal (attha), Nibbāna. The connection is as follows: 'I had a walking path made—delightful to the mind, mind-absorbing, worthy of development, to be kept in mind—for that Blessed One Atthadassī, the sage endowed with sagely knowledge.' The rest is easily understood according to the method already stated.

Caṅkamanadāyakattheraapadānavaṇṇanā samattā.

The commentary on the Apadāna of the Elder Caṅkamanadāyaka is complete.

9. Subhaddattheraapadānavaṇṇanā

9. Commentary on the Apadāna of the Elder Subhadda.

Padumuttaro [P 0.0374] lokavidūtiādikaṃ āyasmato subhaddattherassa apadānaṃ. Ayampi purimabuddhesu katādhikāro [V 2.0067] tattha tattha bhave nibbānādhigamanatthāya puññāni upacinanto padumuttarassa bhagavato kāle vibhavasampanne [M 2.0074] saddhāsampanne ekasmiṃ kulagehe nibbato viññutaṃ patvā gharabandhanena baddho ratanattaye pasanno parinibbānamañce nipannaṃ padumuttaraṃ bhagavantaṃ disvā sannipatitā dasasahassacakkavāḷadevatāyo ca disvā pasannamānaso nigguṇḍikeṭakanīlakāsokāsitādianekehi sugandhapupphehi pūjesi. So tena puññakammena yāvatāyukaṃ ṭhatvā tato cavitvā tusitādīsu dibbasampattiyo anubhavitvā tato manussesu manussasampattiyo anubhavitvā nibbattanibbattaṭṭhānesu ca sugandhehi pupphehi pūjito ahosi. Imasmiṃ pana buddhuppāde ekasmiṃ vibhavasampanne kule nibbattitvā viññutaṃ patto kāmesu ādīnavaṃ disvāpi yāva buddhassa bhagavato parinibbānakālo tāva aladdhabuddhadassano bhagavato parinibbānamañce nipannakāleyeva pabbajitvā arahattaṃ pāpuṇi. Pubbe katapuññanāmena subhaddoti pākaṭo ahosi.

This is the Apadāna of the Venerable Elder Subhadda, beginning with 'Padumuttaro lokavidū'. He too, having made a resolution under previous Buddhas and accumulating merits in various existences for the sake of attaining Nibbāna, was born into a family endowed with wealth and faith during the time of the Blessed One Padumuttara. Having attained discernment, though bound by household ties, he became confident in the Triple Gem. Seeing the Blessed One Padumuttara lying on the couch of final Nibbāna, and also seeing the assembled deities of the ten-thousand world-systems, his mind became serene. He worshipped with many fragrant flowers such as nigguṇḍi, keṭaka, blue aśoka, and dark aśoka. Through that meritorious deed, having lived out his lifespan, he passed away from there and experienced divine prosperity in the Tusita realm and others. Thereafter, he experienced human prosperity among humans, and in whatever place he was reborn, he was honored with fragrant flowers. In this present Buddha-era, however, he was born into a family endowed with wealth, and having attained discernment, although he saw the danger in sensual pleasures, he did not get to see the Buddha until the time of the Blessed One's final Nibbāna. Only at the time when the Blessed One was lying on the couch of final Nibbāna did he go forth and attain arahantship. He became known as Subhadda because of the meritorious deed he had formerly performed.

101. So attano pubbakammaṃ saritvā somanassavasena pubbacaritāpadānaṃ pakāsento padumuttaro lokavidūtiādimāha. Taṃ uttānatthameva. Suṇātha mama bhāsato…pe… nibbāyissatināsavoti idaṃ parinibbānamañce nipannova padumuttaro bhagavā byākāsi.

101. Recalling his former deed, out of joy he proclaimed the Apadāna of his past conduct, speaking the verse beginning 'Padumuttaro lokavidū'. Its meaning is self-evident. The Blessed One Padumuttara made this prediction while lying on the couch of final Nibbāna: 'Listen to me as I speak… he will attain Nibbāna, free from taints.'

Pañcamabhāṇavāravaṇṇanā samattā.

The commentary on the fifth recital section is complete.

115. So attano paṭipattiṃ dassento pubbakammena saṃyuttotiādimāha. Ekaggoti ekaggacitto. Susamāhitoti suṭṭhu samāhito, santakāyacittoti attho. Buddhassa oraso puttoti buddhassa urasā hadayena niggataovādānusāsaniṃ sutvā pattaarahattaphaloti attho. Dhammajomhi sunimmitoti dhammato kammaṭṭhānadhammato jāto ariyāya jātiyā sunimmito suṭṭhu nipphāditasabbakicco amhi bhavāmīti attho.

115. Showing his own practice, he spoke the verse beginning 'Pubbakammena saṃyutto'. 'Ekaggo' means 'with a one-pointed mind'. 'Susamāhito' means 'well-composed'; the meaning is 'with a calmed body and mind'. 'Buddhassa oraso putto' means 'a legitimate son of the Buddha'; the meaning is 'one who has attained the fruit of arahantship by hearing the advice and instruction that issued from the Buddha’s heart'. 'Dhammajo’mhi sunimmito' means 'I am born of the Dhamma, well-fashioned'; the meaning is 'I am one born from the Dhamma—from the Dhamma of the meditation subject—born with a noble birth, well-fashioned, having perfectly accomplished all duties'.

116. Dhammarājaṃ upagammāti dhammena sabbasattānaṃ rājānaṃ issarabhūtaṃ bhagavantaṃ upagantvā samīpaṃ gantvāti attho. Apucchiṃ pañhamuttamanti uttamaṃ khandhāyatanadhātusaccasamuppādādipaṭisaṃyuttaṃ pañhaṃ apucchinti attho. Kathayanto [P 0.0375] ca me pañhanti eso amhākaṃ bhagavā me mayhaṃ pañhaṃ kathayanto byākaronto. Dhammasotaṃ upānayīti anupādisesanibbānadhātusaṅkhātaṃ dhammasotaṃ dhammapavāhaṃ upānayi pāvisīti attho.

116. 'Dhammarājaṃ upagamma' means 'having approached the Blessed One, who is the king and lord of all beings through the Dhamma; that is, having gone near him'. 'Apucchiṃ pañhamuttamaṃ' means 'I asked the supreme question, one connected with the aggregates, sense bases, elements, truths, dependent origination, and so on'. 'Kathayanto ca me pañhaṃ' means 'while our Blessed One was speaking on and explaining my question'. 'Dhammasotaṃ upānayī' means 'he entered the stream of Dhamma, the flow of Dhamma, which is known as the Nibbāna-element without residue; that is, he entered it'.

118. Jalajuttamanāyakoti [M 2.0075] padumuttaranāmako ma-kārassa ya-kāraṃ katvā katavohāro. Nibbāyi [V 2.0068] anupādānoti upādāne pañcakkhandhe aggahetvā nibbāyi na paññāyi adassanaṃ agamāsi, manussalokādīsu katthacipi apatiṭṭhitoti attho. Dīpova telasaṅkhayāti vaṭṭitelānaṃ saṅkhayā abhāvā padīpo iva nibbāyīti sambandho.

118. 'Jalajuttamanāyako' (the leader, highest of lotuses) is a designation for the one named Padumuttara, a term formed by changing the letter 'm' to 'y'. 'Nibbāyi anupādāno' (extinguished without clinging) means: without grasping the five aggregates, which are the basis for clinging, he was extinguished, was no longer perceived, passed into invisibility; the meaning is that he was not established anywhere in the worlds of humans and so on. 'Dīpova telasaṅkhayā' (like a lamp when the fuel is exhausted): the connection is that just as a lamp is extinguished due to the exhaustion and absence of wick and oil, so was he extinguished.

119. Sattayojanikaṃ āsīti tassa parinibbutassa padumuttarassa bhagavato ratanamayaṃ thūpaṃ sattayojanubbedhaṃ āsi ahosīti attho. Dhajaṃ tattha apūjesinti tattha tasmiṃ cetiye sabbabhaddaṃ sabbato bhaddaṃ sabbaso manoramaṃ dhajaṃ pūjesinti attho.

119. 'Sattayojanikaṃ āsi' (it was seven yojanas) means: the jeweled stūpa of that Blessed One Padumuttara, who had attained final Nibbāna, was seven yojanas high. 'Dhajaṃ tattha apūjesiṃ' (I worshipped a banner there) means: at that shrine, I worshipped a banner that was auspicious in every way, beautiful from every side, and completely delightful.

120. Kassapassa ca buddhassāti padumuttarassa bhagavato kālato paṭṭhāya āgatassa devamanussesu saṃsarato me mayhaṃ oraso putto tisso nāma kassapassa sammāsambuddhassa aggasāvako jinasāsane buddhasāsane dāyādo āsi ahosīti sambandho.

120. The connection is that 'Kassapassa ca buddhassa' means: from the time of the Blessed One Padumuttara, as I was wandering among devas and humans, my own son, named Tissa, became the chief disciple of the Perfectly Self-Enlightened One Kassapa, an heir in the Dispensation of the Conqueror, the Buddha’s Dispensation.

121. Tassa hīnena manasāti tassa mama puttassa tissassa aggasāvakassa hīnena lāmakena manasā cittena abhaddakaṃ asundaraṃ ayuttakaṃ “antako pacchimo”ti vācaṃ vacanaṃ abhāsiṃ kathesinti attho. Tena kammavipākenāti tena arahantabhakkhānasaṅkhātassa akusalakammassa vipākena. Pacchime addasaṃ jinanti pacchime pariyosāne parinibbānakāle mallānaṃ upavattane sālavane parinibbānamañce nipannaṃ jinaṃ jitasabbamāraṃ amhākaṃ gotamasammāsambuddhaṃ addasaṃ ahanti attho. “Pacchā me āsi bhaddaka”ntipi pāṭho. Tassa pacchā tassa bhagavato avasānakāle nibbānāsannakāle me mayhaṃ bhaddakaṃ sundaraṃ catusaccapaṭivijjhanaṃ āsi ahosīti attho.

121. 'Tassa hīnena manasā' means: with a low, base mind, with an unwholesome consciousness, I spoke harsh, unbecoming, and unsuitable words to that son of mine, Tissa, the chief disciple, saying, 'The end-maker is the last'; this is the meaning. 'Tena kammavipākena' means: due to the result of that unwholesome deed, namely disparaging an arahant. 'Pacchime addasaṃ jinaṃ' means: in my final period, at the time of final Nibbāna, in the Sāla grove of the Mallas at Upavattana, I saw the Conqueror, our Gotama the Perfectly Self-Enlightened One who had conquered all Māras, lying on the couch of final Nibbāna; this is the meaning. There is also a reading, 'Pacchā me āsi bhaddakaṃ'. Its meaning is: at the end, at the time of the Blessed One's cessation, near the time of Nibbāna, the beautiful penetration of the four truths occurred for me.

122. Pabbājesi mahāvīroti mahāvīriyo sabbasattahito karuṇāyutto jitamāro muni mallānaṃ upavattane sālavane pacchime sayane parinibbānamañce sayitova maṃ pabbājesīti sambandho.

122. The connection is that 'Pabbājesi mahāvīro' means: the Great Hero—one of great energy, devoted to the welfare of all beings, endowed with compassion, the conqueror of Māra, the sage—ordained me while he was lying on his final couch, the couch of final Nibbāna, in the Sāla grove at the Mallas’ Upavattana.

123. Ajjeva [M 2.0076] dāni pabbajjāti ajja eva bhagavato parinibbānadivaseyeva mama pabbajjā, tathā ajja eva upasampadā, ajja eva dvipaduttamassa sammukhā parinibbānaṃ ahosīti sambandho. Sesaṃ suviññeyyamevāti.

123. “Today is truly the going forth”—the connection is: on this very day, the day of the Blessed One’s Parinibbāna, was my going forth; likewise, on this very day, the higher ordination; on this very day, in the presence of the Supreme Among Two-footed Beings, his Parinibbāna occurred. The rest is easily understood.

Subhaddattheraapadānavaṇṇanā samattā.

The commentary on the Apadāna of the Elder Subhadda is complete.

10. Cundattheraapadānavaṇṇanā

10. The Commentary on the Apadāna of the Elder Cunda

Siddhatthassa [P 0.0376][V 2.0069] bhagavatotiādikaṃ āyasmato cundattherassa apadānaṃ. Ayampi purimabuddhesu katapuññasambhāro tattha tattha bhave vivaṭṭūpanissayāni puññāni upacinanto siddhatthassa bhagavato kāle vibhavasampanne kule nibbatto viññutaṃ patvā satthari pasīditvā sattaratanamayaṃ suvaṇṇagghiyaṃ kāretvā sumanapupphehi chādetvā bhagavantaṃ pūjesi. Tāni pupphāni ākāsaṃ samuggantvā vitānākārena aṭṭhaṃsu. Atha naṃ bhagavā “anāgate gotamassa nāma bhagavato sāsane cundo nāma sāvako bhavissatī”ti byākāsi. So tena puññakammena tato cuto devaloke upapanno kamena chasu kāmāvacaradevesu sukhaṃ anubhavitvā manussesu cakkavattiādisampattiyo ca anubhavitvā imasmiṃ buddhuppāde brāhmaṇakule rūpasāriyā putto sāriputtattherassa kaniṭṭho hutvā nibbatti. Tassa viññutaṃ pattassa ārohapariṇāharūpavayānaṃ sundaratāya sakārassa cakāraṃ katvā cundoti nāmaṃ kariṃsu. So vayappatto gharāvāse ādīnavaṃ pabbajjāya ca ānisaṃsaṃ disvā bhātuttherassa santike pabbajitvā vipassanaṃ vaḍḍhetvā nacirasseva arahattaṃ pāpuṇi.

The Apadāna of Venerable Cunda begins with “Of the Blessed One Siddhattha.” He too, having accumulated a store of merit in the presence of previous Buddhas, gathered wholesome deeds as supportive conditions for liberation in various existences. In the time of the Blessed One Siddhattha, he was born into a wealthy family, attained understanding, developed faith in the Teacher, and had a golden offering vessel made of the seven jewels, covered with jasmine flowers, and offered it to the Blessed One. Those flowers rose into the sky and remained as a canopy. Then the Blessed One declared, “In the future, in the dispensation of the Blessed One named Gotama, there will be a disciple named Cunda.” By that meritorious deed, after passing away from there, he was reborn in the deva realm. In due course, he experienced happiness in the six sensuous deva realms, and among humans experienced the fortunes of a wheel-turning monarch and so forth. In this Buddha’s dispensation, he was born into a brahmin family as the son of Rūpasārī, the younger brother of Elder Sāriputta. When he reached maturity, because of the beauty of his height, build, form, and age, they changed the sound ‘sa’ to ‘ca’ and gave him the name Cunda. Having come of age, seeing the danger in household life and the benefit in renunciation, he went forth in the presence of his elder brother, developed insight, and in no long time attained Arahantship.

125. So pattaarahattaphalo ekadivasaṃ attano pubbakammaṃ saritvā somanassajāto pubbacaritāpadānaṃ pakāsento siddhatthassa bhagavatotiādimāha. Taṃ heṭṭhā vuttatthameva. Agghiyantiādayopi uttānatthāyeva.

125. Having attained the fruit of Arahantship, one day, recollecting his past deeds and filled with joy, he proclaimed the Apadāna of his former conduct, beginning with “Of the Blessed One Siddhattha.” The meaning of that is as stated below. “Agghiya,” etc., are also of obvious meaning.

128. Vitiṇṇakaṅkho sambuddhoti visesena maggādhigamena vicikicchāya khepitattā vitiṇṇakaṅkho asaṃsayo sambuddho. Tiṇṇoghehi purakkhatoti kāmoghādīnaṃ catunnaṃ oghānaṃ tiṇṇattā atikkantattā oghatiṇṇehi [M 2.0077] khīṇāsavehi purakkhato parivāritoti attho. Byākaraṇagāthā uttānatthāyeva.

128. “The doubt-crossed, the Awakened One”—because through the special attainment of the path he has destroyed doubt, he is doubt-crossed, without uncertainty, a Perfectly Enlightened One. “Accompanied by those who have crossed the floods”—meaning, he is accompanied and surrounded by those who have crossed the floods, the taintless ones, because the four floods of sensuality and so forth have been crossed and gone beyond. The verses of declaration are of obvious meaning.

139. Upaṭṭhahiṃ mahāvīranti uttamatthassa nibbānassa pattiyā pāpuṇanatthāya kappasatasahassādhikesu caturāsaṅkhyeyyesu kappesu pāramiyo pūrentena katavīriyattā mahāvīraṃ buddhaṃ upaṭṭhahiṃ upaṭṭhānaṃ akāsinti attho. Aññe ca pesale bahūti na kevalameva buddhaṃ upaṭṭhahiṃ, pesale piyasīle sīlavante aññe ca bahuaggappatte sāvake, me mayhaṃ bhātaraṃ sāriputtattherañca upaṭṭhahinti sambandho.

139. “I attended upon the Great Hero”—meaning that I attended upon the Great Hero, the Buddha, so-called because of the effort he made while fulfilling the perfections over four incalculable and one hundred thousand aeons for the sake of attaining the supreme goal of Nibbāna. “And many other virtuous ones”—the connection is that not only did I attend upon the Buddha, but I also attended upon many other virtuous, amiable, and well-conducted disciples who had reached the highest attainment, as well as my brother, the Elder Sāriputta.

140. Bhātaraṃ [V 2.0070] me upaṭṭhahitvāti mayhaṃ bhātaraṃ upaṭṭhahitvā vattapaṭivattaṃ katvā tassa parinibbutakāle bhagavato paṭhamaṃ parinibbutattā tassa dhātuyo gahetvā pattamhi okiritvā lokajeṭṭhassa [P 0.0377] narānaṃ āsabhassa buddhassa upanāmesiṃ adāsinti attho.

140. “Having attended upon my brother”—meaning: having attended upon my brother and performed all requisite duties for him, at the time of his Parinibbāna—since he attained Parinibbāna before the Blessed One—I collected his relics, placed them in a bowl, and presented them to the Buddha, the foremost of the world, the Bull among men.

141. Ubho hatthehi paggayhāti taṃ mahā dinnaṃ dhātuṃ so bhagavā attano ubhohi hatthehi pakārena gahetvā taṃ dhātuṃ saṃsuṭṭhu dassayanto aggasāvakaṃ sāriputtattheraṃ kittayi pakāsesīti attho. Sesaṃ uttānatthamevāti.

141. “Raising it with both hands”—meaning: that Blessed One, taking the relic given by me with both his hands, and displaying that relic very well, praised and proclaimed the chief disciple, the Elder Sāriputta. The rest is of obvious meaning.

Cundattheraapadānavaṇṇanā samattā.

The Commentary on the Apadāna of the Elder Cunda is complete.

Pañcamavaggavaṇṇanā samattā.

The commentary on the fifth section is complete.

6. Bījanivaggo

6. The Seed Chapter

1. Vidhūpanadāyakattheraapadānavaṇṇanā

1. Commentary on the Apadāna of the Elder Vidhūpanadāyaka

Padumuttarabuddhassātiādikaṃ [V 2.0071] āyasmato vidhūpanadāyakattherassa apadānaṃ. Ayampi purimajinavaresu pūritapuññasambhāro tattha tattha bhave vivaṭṭūpanissayāni puññāni upacinanto padumuttarassa bhagavato kāle ekasmiṃ kulagehe nibbatto viññutaṃ patto vibhavasampanno saddhājāto bhagavati pasanno gimhakāle suvaṇṇarajatamuttāmaṇimayaṃ bījaniṃ kāretvā bhagavato adāsi. So tena puññakammena devesu ca manussesu ca saṃsaranto [M 2.0078] dve sampattiyo anubhavitvā imassa amhākaṃ sammāsambuddhassa uppannakāle ekasmiṃ kulagehe nibbatto gharabandhanena bandhitvā gharāvāse ādīnavaṃ disvā pabbajjāya ca ānisaṃsaṃ disvā saddhāsampanno sāsane pabbajitvā vipassanaṃ vaḍḍhetvā nacirasseva arahā ahosi.

The Apadāna of the Venerable Vidhūpanadāyaka begins with the words, 'Of the Buddha Padumuttara.' He too, having fulfilled his store of merit under former Conquerors and accumulating, in various existences, meritorious deeds that serve as a basis for liberation, was born in a certain family home in the time of the Blessed One Padumuttara. Having reached maturity, being endowed with wealth, with faith having arisen, and being devoted to the Blessed One, during the hot season he had a fan made of gold, silver, pearls, and gems, and gave it to the Blessed One. Through that meritorious action, while wandering among gods and humans and experiencing two kinds of prosperity, at the time of the arising of this our Perfectly Enlightened Buddha, he was born in a certain family home. Bound by the fetters of the household, seeing the peril in the household life and the benefit in renunciation, endowed with faith, he went forth into the Dispensation, developed insight, and not long after became an Arahant.

1. So “kena mayā puññakammena ayaṃ lokuttarasampatti laddhā”ti attano pubbakammaṃ anussaranto taṃ paccakkhato ñatvā pubbacaritāpadānaṃ pakāsento padumuttarabuddhassātiādimāha. Taṃ heṭṭhā vuttatthameva. Bījanikā mayā dinnāti visesena santāpayantānaṃ sattānaṃ santāpaṃ nibbāpenti sītalaṃ vātaṃ janetīti bījanī, bījanīyeva bījanikā, sā sattaratanamayā vijjotamānā bījanikā mayā kārāpetvā dinnāti attho.

1. He, reflecting on his own past deeds, 'By what meritorious action was this supramundane attainment gained by me?', and having known it directly, while proclaiming the Apadāna of his past conduct, spoke the words beginning with, 'Of the Buddha Padumuttara.' That has the meaning already stated previously. As for 'A fan was given by me': because it extinguishes the torment of beings who are especially tormented and generates a cool wind, it is a 'bījanī' (fan). A 'bījanī' is a 'bījanikā'. The meaning is: that radiant fan, made of the seven kinds of precious materials, was caused to be made by me and was given.

Vidhūpanadāyakattheraapadānavaṇṇanā samattā.

The commentary on the Apadāna of the Elder Vidhūpanadāyaka is complete.

2. Sataraṃsittheraapadānavaṇṇanā

2. Commentary on the Apadāna of the Elder Sataraṃsi

Ucciyaṃ selamāruyhātiādikaṃ āyasmato sataraṃsittherassa apadānaṃ. Ayampi purimabuddhesu katādhikāro tattha tattha bhave vivaṭṭūpanissayāni puññāni upacinanto padumuttarassa bhagavato kāle brāhmaṇakule nibbatto viññutaṃ patto sakkaṭabyākaraṇe vedattaye ca pāraṅgato gharāvāsaṃ [V 2.0072] pahāya araññaṃ pavisitvā isipabbajjaṃ pabbajitvā himavante vāsaṃ kappesi. Tasmiṃ [P 0.0378] samaye padumuttaro bhagavā vivekakāmatāya uccaṃ ekaṃ pabbataṃ āruyha jalitaggikkhanto viya nisīdi. Taṃ tathānisinnaṃ bhagavantaṃ disvā tāpaso somanassajāto añjaliṃ paggayha anekehi kāraṇehi thomesi. So tena puññakammena tato cuto chasu kāmāvacaradevesu dibbasampattiṃ anubhavitvā tato manussaloke sataraṃsī nāma cakkavattī rājā hutvā nibbatti. Tampi sampattiṃ anekakkhattuṃ anubhavitvā imasmiṃ buddhuppāde ekasmiṃ kulagehe nibbatto pubbapuññasambhāravasena ñāṇassa paripakkattā sattavassikova pabbajitvā arahattaṃ pāpuṇi.

The Apadāna of the Venerable Sataraṃsi begins with the words, 'Ascending the high rocky mountain...' He too, having made his aspiration in the presence of previous Buddhas and accumulating, in various existences, meritorious deeds that serve as a basis for liberation, was born into a brahmin family in the time of the Blessed One Padumuttara. Having reached maturity, he became a master of Sanskrit grammar and the three Vedas. Abandoning the household life, he entered the forest, undertook the going-forth of an ascetic, and took up residence in the Himalayas. At that time, the Blessed One Padumuttara, desiring seclusion, ascended a high mountain and sat like a blazing mass of fire. Seeing the Blessed One seated thus, the ascetic, with joy arisen, raised his joined hands in reverence and praised him for many reasons. Through that meritorious deed, having passed away from there, he experienced divine fortune in the six sense-sphere heavens. Then, in the human world, he was reborn as a wheel-turning monarch named Sataraṃsi. Having experienced that fortune many times, during this Buddha-dispensation, he was born into a certain family home. By the power of his store of past merit and due to the maturity of his knowledge, at the age of seven he went forth and attained arahantship.

8-9. So [M 2.0079] “ahaṃ kena kammena sattavassikova santipadaṃ anuppattosmī”ti saramāno pubbakammaṃ ñāṇena paccakkhato disvā somanassajāto pubbacaritāpadānaṃ udānavasena pakāsento ucciyaṃ selamāruyhātiādimāha. Tattha ucciyanti uccaṃ selamayaṃ pabbataṃ āruyha nisīdi padumuttaroti sambandho. Pabbatassāvidūramhīti bhagavato nisinnassa pabbatassa āsannaṭṭhāneti attho. Brāhmaṇo mantapāragūti mantasaṅkhātassa vedattayassa pāraṃ pariyosānaṃ koṭiṃ gato eko brāhmaṇoti attho, aññaṃ viya attānaṃ niddisati ayaṃ mantapāragūti. Upaviṭṭhaṃ mahāvīranti tasmiṃ pabbate nisinnaṃ vīravantaṃ jinaṃ, kiṃ visiṭṭhaṃ? Devadevaṃ sakalachakāmāvacarabrahmadevānaṃ atidevaṃ narāsabhaṃ narānaṃ āsataṃ seṭṭhaṃ lokanāyakaṃ sakalasattalokaṃ nayantaṃ nibbānaṃ pāpentaṃ ahaṃ añjaliṃ dasanakhasamodhānañjalipuṭaṃ sirasi muddhani paggahetvāna patiṭṭhapetvā santhaviṃ suṭṭhuṃ thomesinti sambandho.

8-9. He, remembering, 'By what action have I, at only seven years of age, attained the state of peace?', and seeing his past action directly with his knowledge, became joyful. Proclaiming the Apadāna of his past conduct by way of an inspired utterance, he spoke the words beginning with, 'Ascending a high rocky mountain...' Therein, the connection for 'ascending' is: having ascended a high, rocky mountain, Padumuttara sat down. The meaning of 'not far from the mountain' is: in a place near the mountain where the Blessed One was seated. The meaning of 'a brahmin, a master of mantras' is: a brahmin who has gone to the further shore, the final end, the summit of the three Vedas, which are known as mantras. He refers to himself as if he were another, saying, 'this master of mantras.' 'The great hero seated' refers to the heroic Conqueror seated on that mountain. What are his special qualities? He is the god of gods, the supreme god over all the gods of the six sense-spheres and the Brahmā gods; the bull among men, the best of men; the leader of the world, who guides the entire world of beings, leading them to Nibbāna. The connection is: 'I praised' means, 'I, having raised the cupped hands of reverence—the ten fingernails brought together—and placed them upon my head, upon the crown, praised him well, extolled him.'

12. Abhāsathāti “yenāyaṃ añjalī dinno…pe… arahā so bhavissatī”ti byākāsi. Sesaṃ uttānatthamevāti.

12. 'He spoke' means he made the prediction, 'By this gesture of reverence that was given... (etc.)... he will become an arahant.' The rest has a clear meaning.

Sataraṃsittheraapadānavaṇṇanā samattā.

The commentary on the Apadāna of the Elder Sataraṃsi is complete.

3. Sayanadāyakattheraapadānavaṇṇanā

3. Commentary on the Apadāna of the Elder Sayanadāyaka

Padumuttarabuddhassātiādikaṃ āyasmato sayanadāyakattherassa apadānaṃ. Ayampi purimabuddhesu katādhikāro tattha tattha bhave vivaṭṭūpanissayāni puññāni upacinanto padumuttarassa bhagavato [V 2.0073] kāle ekasmiṃ kulagehe nibbatto viññutaṃ patto gharāvāsaṃ saṇṭhapetvā sukhamanubhavanto satthu dhammadesanaṃ sutvā satthari pasanno dantasuvaṇṇarajatamuttamaṇimayaṃ mahārahaṃ mañcaṃ kārāpetvā cīnapaṭṭakambalādīni attharitvā sayanatthāya bhagavato adāsi. Bhagavā tassa anuggahaṃ karonto tattha sayi[P 0.0379]. So tena puññakammena devamanussesu saṃsaranto tadanurūpaṃ ākāsagamanasukhaseyyādisukhaṃ anubhavitvā imasmiṃ buddhuppāde vibhavasampanne ekasmiṃ kule nibbattitvā viññutaṃ pāpuṇitvā satthu dhammadesanaṃ sutvā pasannamānaso pabbajitvā vipassanto nacirasseva arahā ahosi.

The Apadāna of the Venerable Sayanadāyaka begins with the words, 'Of the Buddha Padumuttara...' He too, having made his aspiration in the presence of past Buddhas and accumulating, in various existences, meritorious deeds that serve as a basis for liberation, was born into a certain family home in the time of the Blessed One Padumuttara. Having reached maturity, he established a household and experienced happiness. Hearing the Teacher’s Dhamma discourse, he became devoted to the Teacher. He had a valuable couch made of ivory, gold, silver, pearls, and gems, and having spread it with Chinese silks, woolen blankets, and the like, he gave it to the Blessed One for the purpose of reclining. The Blessed One, showing him compassion, lay down upon it. Through that meritorious deed, while wandering among gods and humans, he experienced corresponding happiness, such as traveling through the sky and having comfortable beds. During this Buddha-dispensation, he was born into a certain family endowed with wealth. Having reached maturity and heard the Teacher’s Dhamma discourse, with a devoted mind he went forth, and while developing insight, not long after became an arahant.

20. So [M 2.0080] attano pubbakammaṃ saritvā somanassajāto pubbacaritāpadānaṃ pakāsento padumuttarabuddhassātiādimāha. Taṃ heṭṭhā vuttatthameva.

20. He, remembering his own past deed, with joy arisen, and proclaiming the Apadāna of his past conduct, spoke the words beginning with, 'Of the Buddha Padumuttara...' That has the meaning already stated previously.

21. Sukhette bījasampadāti yathā tiṇakacavararahite kaddamādisampanne sukhette vuttabījāni sāduphalāni nipphādenti, evameva rāgadosādidiyaḍḍhasahassakilesasaṅkhātatiṇakacavararahite suddhasantāne puññakkhette vuttadānāni appānipi samānāni mahapphalāni hontīti attho. Sesaṃ suviññeyyamevāti.

21. The phrase 'the excellence of seeds in a fertile field' means that just as seeds sown in a fertile field—free from grass and refuse, rich in mud and other nutrients—produce sweet fruits, so too do even small acts of generosity, when performed in the pure continuum, the field of merit, free from the grass and refuse of the fifteen hundred defilements such as greed and hatred, bear great fruit. The rest is easily understood.

Sayanadāyakattheraapadānavaṇṇanā samattā.

The commentary on the Apadāna of the Sayanadāyaka Thera is complete.

4. Gandhodakiyattheraapadānavaṇṇanā

4. Commentary on the Apadāna of Gandhodakiya Thera

Padumuttarabuddhassātiādikaṃ āyasmato gandhodakiyattherassa apadānaṃ. Ayampi purimamunivaresu katādhikāro tattha tattha bhave vivaṭṭūpanissayāni puññāni upacinanto padumuttarassa bhagavato kāle kulagehe nibbatto parinibbute bhagavati nagaravāsino bodhipūjaṃ kurumāne disvā vicittaghaṭe candanakappurāgaruādimissakasugandhodakena pūretvā bodhirukkhaṃ abhisiñci. Tasmiṃ khaṇe devo mahādhārāhi pavassi. Tadā so asanivegena kālaṃ kato. Teneva puññakammena devaloke nibbatti, tattheva ṭhito “aho buddho, aho dhammo”tiādigāthāyo abhāsi. Evaṃ so devamanussesu sampattiyo anubhavitvā sabbapariḷāhavippamutto nibbattanibbattaṭṭhāne sītibhāvamupagato sukhito imasmiṃ buddhuppāde kulagehe [V 2.0074] nibbatto viññutaṃ patto satthari pasanno pabbajitvā kammaṭṭhānaṃ ārabhitvā vipassanto nacirasseva arahattaṃ pāpuṇi. Pubbe katapuññena gandhodakiyattheroti pākaṭo ahosi.

The Apadāna of the Venerable Gandhodakiya Thera, beginning with 'Padumuttarabuddhassa,' and so forth. This one, too, having made aspirations under previous great sages, accumulating merits in various existences that are a basis for liberation, was born into a family in the time of the Blessed One Padumuttara. After the Blessed One had attained final Nibbāna, seeing the city dwellers worshipping the Bodhi tree, he filled a variegated pot with fragrant water mixed with sandalwood, camphor, agarwood, and so forth, and sprinkled it over the Bodhi tree. At that moment, rain fell in great streams. Then he passed away, struck by a thunderbolt. By that very meritorious deed, he was reborn in the deva world, and while remaining there, he recited verses such as, 'Ah, the Buddha! Ah, the Dhamma!' Thus, experiencing prosperity among devas and humans, freed from all feverishness, he attained coolness and was happy in every place of rebirth. In this Buddha-era, he was born into a family, attained maturity, became faithful to the Teacher, went forth, took up a meditation subject, developed insight, and soon attained arahantship. Due to merit made in the past, he became known as the Gandhodakiya Thera.

25. So ekadivasaṃ attano pubbakammaṃ saritvā somanassajāto pubbacaritāpadānaṃ pakāsento padumutarassātiādimāha. Taṃ vuttatthameva. Mahābodhimaho ahūti mahābodhirukkhassa pūjā ahosīti attho. Vicittaṃ ghaṭamādāyāti anekehi cittakammasuvaṇṇakammehi vicittaṃ sobhamānaṃ gandhodakapuṇṇaṃ ghaṭaṃ gahetvāti attho[M 2.0081]. Gandhodakamadāsahanti gandhodakaṃ adāsiṃ, ahaṃ gandhodakena abhisiñcinti attho.

25. One day, recalling his past deed, he was filled with joy and, revealing his Apadāna of past conduct, he began with 'Padumuttarassa,' and so forth. That has the meaning already stated. 'Mahābodhimaho ahū' means: there was worship of the great Bodhi tree. 'Vicittaṃ ghaṭamādāya' means: taking a variegated and beautiful pot, adorned with various artistic and golden designs, filled with fragrant water. 'Gandhodakamadāsahaṃ' means: 'I gave fragrant water'; the meaning is, 'I sprinkled with fragrant water.'

26. Nhānakāle [P 0.0380] ca bodhiyāti bodhiyā pūjākaraṇasamayeti attho. Sesaṃ uttānatthamevāti.

26. 'Nhānakāle ca bodhiyā' means at the time of worshipping the Bodhi tree. The rest is clear in meaning.

Gandhodakiyattheraapadānavaṇṇanā samattā.

The commentary on the Apadāna of Gandhodakiya Thera is complete.

5. Opavayhattheraapadānavaṇṇanā

5. Commentary on the Apadāna of Opavayha Thera

Padumuttarabuddhassātiādikaṃ āyasmato opavayhattherassa apadānaṃ. Ayampi purimabuddhesu katādhikāro tattha tattha bhave vivaṭṭūpanissayāni puññāni upacinanto padumuttarajinādicce loke pātubhūte ekasmiṃ vibhavasampannakule nibbatto vuddhimanvāya mahaddhano mahābhogo gharāvāsaṃ vasamāno sāsane pasanno satthari pasādabahumāno ājānīyena sindhavena pūjaṃ akāsi, pūjetvā ca pana “buddhādīnaṃ samaṇānaṃ hatthiassādayo na kappanti, kappiyabhaṇḍaṃ dassāmī”ti cintetvā taṃ agghāpetvā tadagghanakena kahāpaṇena kappiyaṃ kappāsikakambalakojavādikaṃ cīvaraṃ kappūratakkolādikaṃ bhesajjaparikkhārañca adāsi. So tena puññakammena yāvatāyukaṃ ṭhatvā tato cuto devesu ca manussesu ca hatthiassādianekavāhanasampanno sukhaṃ anubhavitvā imasmiṃ buddhuppāde ekasmiṃ kulagehe nibbatto viññutaṃ patto saddhāsampanno sāsane pabbajitvā kammaṭṭhānaṃ gahetvā vipassanaṃ vaḍḍhetvā maggapaṭipāṭiyā arahatte patiṭṭhāsi, pubbe katapuññasambhāravasena opavayhattheroti pākaṭo ahosi.

The Apadāna of the Venerable Opavayha Thera, beginning with 'Padumuttarabuddhassa,' and so forth. This one, too, having made aspirations under former Buddhas, accumulating merits in various existences that are a basis for liberation, when the Victorious Sun Padumuttara appeared in the world, was born into a prosperous family. Having reached maturity, possessing great wealth and great abundance, living the household life, having faith in the Dispensation and great devotion to the Teacher, he made an offering with a thoroughbred Sindhu steed. After making the offering, he thought, 'Elephants, horses, and so forth are not suitable for ascetics such as the Buddha. I shall give suitable requisites.' Having its value assessed, with the kahāpaṇas of that value he gave suitable robes such as those of cotton, wool, and rugs, and medicinal requisites such as camphor and cubeb. By that meritorious deed, having lived for his full lifespan, and having passed away from there, he experienced happiness among devas and humans, endowed with numerous vehicles like elephants and horses. In this Buddha-era, he was born into a family, attained maturity, became endowed with faith, and went forth into the Dispensation. Taking up a meditation subject, he developed insight, and by the sequence of paths, he became established in arahantship. Due to the accumulation of past meritorious deeds, he became known as the Opavayha Thera.

33. So “kena nu kho kāraṇena idaṃ mayā santipadaṃ adhigata”nti upadhārento pubbakammaṃ [V 2.0075] ñāṇena paccakkhato ñatvā somanassajāto pubbacaritāpadānaṃ udānavasena pakāsento padumuttarabuddhassātiādimāha. Taṃ vuttatthameva. Ājānīyamadāsahanti ājānīyaṃ uttamajātisindhavaṃ ahaṃ adāsiṃ pūjesinti attho.

33. Then, reflecting, 'By what reason indeed have I attained this state of peace?' and directly knowing his past deed with knowledge, filled with joy, and proclaiming his Apadāna of past conduct by way of an inspired utterance, he began with 'Padumuttarabuddhassa,' and so forth. That has the meaning already stated. 'Ājānīyamadāsahaṃ' means: 'I gave a thoroughbred, a Sindhu of excellent breed; I made an offering.'

35. Sapattabhāroti sassa attano pattāni aṭṭha parikkhārāni bhārāni yassa so sapattabhāro, aṭṭhaparikkhārayuttoti attho.

35. 'Sapattabhāro' is explained as: he for whom his own obtained eight requisites are his load. The meaning is 'endowed with the eight requisites'.

36. Khamanīyamadāsahanti [M 2.0082] khamanīyayoggaṃ cīvarādikappiyaparikkhāranti attho.

36. 'Khamanīyamadāsahaṃ' means: I gave permissible requisites, such as robes, which are suitable for endurance.

40. Carimoti pariyosāno koṭippatto bhavoti attho. Sesaṃ suviññeyyamevāti.

40. 'Carimo' means the final existence, reaching the limit; such is the meaning. The rest is easily understood.

Opavayhattheraapadānavaṇṇanā samattā.

The commentary on the Apadāna of Opavayha Thera is complete.

6. Saparivārāsanattheraapadānavaṇṇanā

6. Commentary on the Apadāna of Saparivārāsana Thera

Padumuttarabuddhassātiādikaṃ āyasmato saparivārāsanattherassa apadānaṃ. Sopi purimabuddhesu katādhikāro tattha [P 0.0381] tattha bhavesu vivaṭṭūpanissayāni puññāni upacinanto padumuttarassa bhagavato kāle vibhavasampanne kulagehe nibbatto vuddhippatto saddhājāto sāsane pasanno dānaphalaṃ saddahanto nānaggarasabhojanena bhagavato piṇḍapātaṃ adāsi, datvā ca pana bhojanasālāyaṃ bhojanatthāya nisinnāsanaṃ jātisumanamallikādīhi alaṅkari. Bhagavā ca bhattānumodanamakāsi. So tena puññakammena devamanussesu saṃsaranto anekavidhaṃ sampattiṃ anubhavitvā imasmiṃ buddhuppāde vibhavasampanne kulagehe nibbatto vuddhimanvāya saddho pasanno pabbajitvā na cirasseva arahā ahosi.

The Apadāna of the Venerable Saparivārāsana Thera, beginning with 'Padumuttarabuddhassa,' and so forth. He too, having made aspirations under previous Buddhas, accumulating merits in various existences that are a basis for liberation, in the time of the Blessed One Padumuttara, was born into a prosperous family. Having reached maturity, he developed faith, became devoted to the Dispensation, and, believing in the fruit of giving, offered almsfood of various excellent flavours to the Blessed One. Having given, he then decorated the seat prepared for the meal in the dining hall with jāti flowers, jasmine, and so forth. The Blessed One then gave the anumodanā after the meal. Through that meritorious deed, wandering among devas and humans and experiencing various kinds of prosperity, in this Buddha-era, he was born into a prosperous family. Having reached maturity, he became faithful and devoted, went forth, and soon became an arahant.

43. So evaṃ pattasantipado “kena nu kho puññena idaṃ santipadaṃ anuppatta”nti ñāṇena upadhārento pubbakammaṃ disvā somanassajāto pubbacaritāpadānaṃ pakāsento padumuttarabuddhassātiādimāha. Taṃ vuttatthameva. Piṇḍapātaṃ adāsahanti tattha tattha laddhānaṃ piṇḍānaṃ kabaḷaṃ kabaḷaṃ katvā pātabbato khāditabbato āhāro piṇḍapāto, taṃ piṇḍapātaṃ bhagavato adāsiṃ, bhagavantaṃ bhojesinti attho.

43. He, having thus attained the state of peace, reflecting with knowledge, 'By what merit indeed have I attained this state of peace?', and seeing his past deed, became filled with joy. Proclaiming his Apadāna of past conduct, he began with 'Padumuttarabuddhassa,' and so forth. That has the meaning already stated. As for 'Piṇḍapātaṃ adāsaṃ ahaṃ' (I gave almsfood): there, the food obtained from various places, made into morsels, is called 'piṇḍapāta' because it is to be drunk or eaten. I gave that almsfood to the Blessed One; the meaning is, 'I fed the Blessed One.'

44. Akittayi [V 2.0076] piṇḍapātanti mayā dinnapiṇḍapātassa guṇaṃ ānisaṃsaṃ pakāsesīti attho.

44. As for 'Akittayi piṇḍapātaṃ,' the meaning is: He declared the qualities and benefits of the almsfood given by me.

48. Saṃvuto pātimokkhasminti pātimokkhasaṃvarasīlena saṃvuto pihito paṭicchannoti attho. Indriyesu ca pañcasūti cakkhundriyādīsu pañcasu [M 2.0083] indriyesu rūpādīhi gopito indriyasaṃvarasīlañca gopitoti attho. Sesaṃ suviññeyyamevāti.

48. As for 'Saṃvuto pātimokkhasmiṃ' (Restrained in the Pātimokkha), the meaning is: restrained, covered, and concealed by the morality of the Pātimokkha restraint. As for 'Indriyesu ca pañcasū' (And in the five faculties), the meaning is: guarded in the five faculties, beginning with the eye-faculty, from forms and so forth, and guarded by the morality of sense-faculty restraint. The rest is easily understood.

Saparivārāsanattheraapadānavaṇṇanā samattā.

The commentary on the Apadāna of the Elder Saparivārāsana is complete.

7. Pañcadīpakattheraapadānavaṇṇanā

7. The Commentary on the Apadāna of the Elder Pañcadīpaka

Padumuttarabuddhassātiādikaṃ āyasmato pañcadīpakattherassa apadānaṃ. Ayampi purimabuddhesu katādhikāro uppannuppannabhavesu vivaṭṭūpanissayāni puññāni upacinanto padumuttarassa bhagavato kāle kulagehe nibbatto vuddhimanvāya gharāvāse vasanto bhagavato dhammaṃ sutvā sammādiṭṭhiyaṃ patiṭṭhito saddho pasanno mahājanehi bodhipūjaṃ kayiramānaṃ disvā sayampi bodhiṃ parivāretvā dīpaṃ jāletvā pūjesi. So tena puññakammena devamanussesu saṃsaranto cakkavattisampattiādayo anubhavitvā sabbattheva uppannabhave jalamāno jotisampannavimānādīsu vasitvā imasmiṃ buddhuppāde ekasmiṃ vibhavasampanne kulagehe nibbatto vuddhippatto saddhājāto pabbajitvā nacirasseva arahā ahosi, dīpapūjānissandena dīpakattheroti pākaṭo.

The Apadāna of the venerable Pañcadīpaka begins with 'Padumuttarabuddhassa.' He too, having made his aspiration in the presence of previous Buddhas and accumulating merits that support liberation in successive existences, was born into a family home during the time of the Blessed One Padumuttara. Having reached maturity and while living the household life, he heard the Dhamma of the Blessed One and became established in right view. Faithful and devoted, seeing the great populace making offerings to the Bodhi tree, he himself also encircled the Bodhi tree, lit lamps, and made an offering. Through that meritorious deed, while wandering among devas and humans, he experienced the fortunes of a wheel-turning monarch and the like. In every place he was born, he was radiant, dwelling in luminous mansions. In this Buddha-dispensation, he was born into a prosperous family. Having reached maturity, faith arose in him, and he went forth. Not long after, he became an Arahant. As a result of his lamp offering, he became known as the Elder Pañcadīpaka.

50. So [P 0.0382] ekadivasaṃ attano pubbakammaṃ saritvā somanassajāto pubbacaritāpadānaṃ pakāsento padumuttarabuddhassātiādimāha. Taṃ vuttatthameva. Ujudiṭṭhi ahosahanti vaṅkaṃ micchādiṭṭhiṃ chaḍḍetvā uju avaṅkaṃ nibbānābhimukhaṃ pāpuṇanasammādiṭṭhi ahosinti attho.

50. One day, recalling his past deed, he became filled with joy and, proclaiming his Apadāna of past conduct, began with 'Padumuttarabuddhassa,' and so forth. That has the meaning already stated. As for 'Ujudiṭṭhi ahosahaṃ' (I was of straight view), the meaning is: having abandoned crooked wrong view, I became of straight, uncrooked right view that leads to Nibbāna.

51. Padīpadānaṃ pādāsinti ettha pakārena dibbati jotatīti padīpo, tassa dānaṃ padīpadānaṃ, taṃ adāsiṃ padīpapūjaṃ akāsinti attho. Sesaṃ sabbattha uttānatthamevāti.

51. As for 'Padīpadānaṃ adāsiṃ' (I gave an offering of lamps), here 'padīpa' (lamp) is so called because it shines (dibbati) or illuminates (jotati) in a special way (pakārena). The giving of that is 'padīpadāna' (lamp-offering). The meaning is: I gave that; I performed a lamp-offering. The rest has a clear meaning everywhere.

Pañcadīpakattheraapadānavaṇṇanā samattā.

The commentary on the Apadāna of the Elder Pañcadīpaka is complete.

8. Dhajadāyakattheraapadānavaṇṇanā

8. The Commentary on the Apadāna of the Elder Dhajadāyaka

Padumuttarabuddhassātiādikaṃ [M 2.0084][V 2.0077] āyasmato dhajadāyakattherassa apadānaṃ. Ayampi purimabuddhesu katādhikāro tattha tattha bhave vivaṭṭūpanissayāni puññāni upacinanto padumuttarassa bhagavato kāle ekasmiṃ kulagehe nibbatto vuddhimanvāya satthari pasīditvā sundarehi anekehi vatthehi dhajaṃ kārāpetvā dhajapūjaṃ akāsi. So tena puññakammena uppannuppannabhave uccakule nibbatto pūjaniyo ahosi. Aparabhāge imasmiṃ buddhuppāde ekasmiṃ kulagehe nibbatto vuddhimanvāya puttadārehi vaḍḍhitvā mahābhogo yasavā saddhājāto satthari pasanno gharāvāsaṃ pahāya pabbajitvā nacirasseva arahā ahosi.

The Apadāna of the venerable Dhajadāyaka begins with 'Padumuttarabuddhassa.' He too, having made his aspiration in the presence of previous Buddhas and accumulating merits that support liberation in his various existences, was born into a family home during the time of the Blessed One Padumuttara. Having reached maturity, he gained faith in the Teacher, had a banner made with many beautiful cloths, and performed a banner-offering. By that meritorious deed, in successive existences he was born into high families and became worthy of reverence. Later, in this Buddha-dispensation, he was born into a family home. Having reached maturity and prospered with sons and wife, he became one of great wealth and renown. Faith arose in him, and with devotion to the Teacher, he abandoned the household life, went forth, and not long after became an Arahant.

57. So pattaarahattaphalo pubbakammaṃ saritvā somanassajāto attano pubbacaritāpadānaṃ pakāsento padumuttarabuddhassātiādimāha. Tassattho pubbe vuttoyeva. Haṭṭho haṭṭhena cittenāti somanassasahagatacittayuttattā haṭṭho paripuṇṇarūpakāyo saddhāsampayuttacittatāya haṭṭhena cittena santuṭṭhena cittenāti attho. Dhajamāropayiṃ ahanti dhunāti kampati calatīti dhajaṃ, taṃ dhajaṃ āropayiṃ veḷagge laggetvā pūjesinti attho.

57. He, having attained the fruit of Arahantship and recollecting his past deed, became filled with joy and, proclaiming his Apadāna of past conduct, began with 'Padumuttarabuddhassa,' and so forth. Its meaning is as explained before. As for 'Haṭṭho haṭṭhena cittena' (Joyful, with a joyful mind), the meaning is: he was joyful because his mind was conjoined with gladness, his physical form was filled with joy, and because his mind was conjoined with faith, it was a joyful and contented mind. As for 'Dhajaṃ āropayiṃ ahaṃ' (I raised a banner), 'dhaja' (banner) is so called because it flutters (dhunāti), trembles (kampati), and moves (calati). The meaning is: I raised that banner, attached it to the tip of a bamboo pole, and made an offering.

58-9. Patitapattāni gaṇhitvāti patitāni bodhipattāni gahetvā ahaṃ bahi chaḍḍesinti attho. Antosuddhaṃ bahisuddhanti anto cittasantānanāmakāyato ca bahi cakkhusotādirūpakāyato ca suddhiṃ adhi visesena muttaṃ kilesato vimuttaṃ anāsavaṃ sambuddhaṃ viya sammukhā uttamaṃ bodhiṃ avandiṃ paṇāmamakāsinti attho. Sesaṃ sabbattha uttānatthamevāti.

As for 'Patitapattāni gaṇhitvā' (Having taken the fallen leaves), the meaning is: having taken the fallen Bodhi leaves, I discarded them outside. As for 'Antosuddhaṃ bahisuddhaṃ' (Pure within and without): I venerated the supreme enlightenment as if in the presence of the Sambuddha, who is pure both internally, in the mental continuum called the 'name-body,' and externally, in the physical body of the eye, ear, and so on; who is especially liberated, freed from defilements, and taintless. The rest has a clear meaning everywhere.

Dhajadāyakattheraapadānavaṇṇanā samattā.

The commentary on the Apadāna of the Elder Dhajadāyaka is complete.

9. Padumattheraapadānavaṇṇanā

9. The Commentary on the Apadāna of the Elder Paduma

Catusaccaṃ pakāsentotiādikaṃ āyasmato padumattherassa apadānaṃ. Ayampi purimabuddhesu katakusalasambhāro padumuttaramuninā [P 0.0383] dhammapajjote jotamāne ekasmiṃ kulagehe nibbatto gharāvāsaṃ saṇṭhapetvā [M 2.0085] bhogasampannoti pākaṭo. So satthari pasīditvā mahājanena saddhiṃ dhammaṃ suṇanto dhajena saha padumakalāpaṃ gahetvā aṭṭhāsi, sadhajaṃ taṃ padumakalāpaṃ ākāsamukkhipiṃ, taṃ [V 2.0078] acchariyaṃ disvā ativiya somanassajāto ahosi. So yāvajīvaṃ kusalaṃ katvā jīvitapariyosāne sagge nibbatto dhajamiva chakāmāvacare pākaṭo pūjito ca dibbasampattimanubhavitvā manussesu ca cakkavattisampattimanubhavitvā imasmiṃ buddhuppāde vibhavasampanne saddhāsampanne ekasmiṃ kulagehe nibbatto vuddhimanvāya saddhājāto pañcavassikova pabbajitvā nacirasseva arahā hutvā katapuññanāmena padumattheroti pākaṭo.

The Apadāna of the venerable Padumatthera begins with 'Catusaccaṃ pakāsento.' This one also, having accumulated a store of wholesome deeds under previous Buddhas, when the sage Padumuttara was illuminating with the lamp of the Dhamma, was born into a certain family. Having established a household life, he became known as 'one endowed with wealth.' He, having gained faith in the Teacher, while listening to the Dhamma together with a great crowd of people, stood holding a lotus cluster together with a banner. He threw that lotus cluster with its banner into the sky, and seeing that marvel, he became exceedingly joyful. He, having performed wholesome deeds for as long as he lived, at the end of his life was reborn in heaven. Like a banner, he was renowned and honored in the six sensual heavens. Having experienced divine fortune and having experienced the fortune of a wheel-turning monarch among humans, in this Buddha-era, he was born into a certain family that was endowed with wealth and faith. Following his growth, faith arose, and having gone forth at the age of five, not long after he became an Arahant. By the name of the merit he had made, he became renowned as the Elder Paduma.

67. Attano pubbakammaṃ saritvā somanassajāto pubbacaritāpadānaṃ pakāsento catusaccaṃ pakāsentotiādimāha. Tattha saccanti tathaṃ avitathaṃ aviparītaṃ saccaṃ, dukkhasamudayanirodhamaggavasena cattāri saccāni samāhaṭānīti catusaccaṃ, taṃ catusaccaṃ pakāsento loke pākaṭaṃ karontoti attho. Varadhammappavattakoti uttamadhammappavattako pakāsakoti attho. Amataṃ vuṭṭhinti amatamahānibbānavuṭṭhidhāraṃ pavassanto paggharanto sadevakaṃ lokaṃ temento sabbakilesapariḷāhaṃ nibbāpento dhammavassaṃ vassatīti attho.

67. Remembering his own past deeds, having become joyful, and proclaiming the Apadāna of his past conduct, he spoke beginning with 'Catusaccaṃ pakāsento.' Therein, 'saccaṃ' (truth) means that which is real, not false, not contrary. The four truths—by way of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path—are gathered together, thus it is 'catusaccaṃ' (the Four Truths). The meaning is that by proclaiming these Four Truths, he made them manifest in the world. 'Varadhammappavattako' (the one who sets in motion the excellent Dhamma) means the one who sets in motion, the proclaimer of, the highest Dhamma. 'Amataṃ vuṭṭhiṃ' (the rain of the deathless) means that showering the stream of rain of the deathless, great Nibbāna, pouring it forth, moistening the world with its gods, extinguishing the entire fever of defilements, he rains the rain of Dhamma.

68. Sadhajaṃ padumaṃ gayhāti dhajena saha ekato katvā padumaṃ padumakalāpaṃ gahetvāti attho. Aḍḍhakose ṭhito ahanti ubho ukkhipitvā ṭhito ahanti attho. Sesaṃ sabbattha uttānatthamevāti.

68. Regarding 'Sadhajaṃ padumaṃ gayha' (taking the lotus with its banner), the meaning is: 'having taken a lotus, a cluster of lotuses, together as one with the banner.' Regarding 'Aḍḍhakose ṭhito ahaṃ' (I stood half a kosa away), the meaning is: 'I stood having lifted both (the banner and the lotus cluster).' The rest is clear in meaning everywhere.

Padumattheraapadānavaṇṇanā samattā.

The commentary on the Apadāna of the Elder Paduma is complete.

10. Asanabodhiyattheraapadānavaṇṇanā

10. Commentary on the Apadāna of the Elder Asanabodhiya

Jātiyā sattavassohantiādikaṃ āyasmato asanabodhiyattherassa apadānaṃ. Ayampi purimabuddhesu katādhikāro tattha tattha bhave vivaṭṭūpanissayāni puññāni upacinanto tissassa bhagavato kāle aññatarasmiṃ kulagehe nibbatto vuddhippatto sukhappatto sāsane pasanno [M 2.0086] asanabodhito phalaṃ gahetvā tato vuṭṭhitabodhitaruṇe gahetvā bodhiṃ ropesi, yathā na vinassati tathā udakāsiñcanādikammena rakkhitvā pūjesi. So tena puññena devamanussesu sampattiyo anubhavitvā imasmiṃ buddhuppāde kulagehe nibbatto paripakkasambhārattā [P 0.0384] sattavassikova samāno pabbajitvā khuraggeyeva arahattaṃ pāpuṇi, purākatapuññanāmena asanabodhiyattheroti pākaṭo.

The Apadāna of the venerable Asanabodhiyatthera begins with 'Jātiyā sattavassohaṃ' (At seven years of age). He too, having made his aspiration under previous Buddhas, accumulating merits that are a supporting condition for emancipation in various existences, was reborn in a certain family during the time of the Blessed One Tissa. Having reached maturity and attained happiness, he gained faith in the Dispensation. He took a fruit from the Asana Bodhi tree, and from that took the young Bodhi saplings that had arisen, and planted a Bodhi tree. He protected and honored it by means of watering and other services so that it would not perish. Through that merit, he experienced prosperity among gods and humans. During this Buddha-era, he was reborn in a family and, due to the maturity of his accumulated merit, at the age of just seven years, he went forth and attained Arahantship right at the razor's edge. He became known as the Elder Asanabodhiya by the name of his past merit.

78. So [V 2.0079] pubbasambhāramanussaritvā somanassajāto pubbacaritāpadānaṃ pakāsento jātiyā sattavassohantiādimāha. Tattha jātiyāti mātugabbhato nikkhantakālato paṭṭhāyāti attho. Sattavasso paripuṇṇasarado ahaṃ lokanāyakaṃ tissaṃ bhagavantaṃ addasanti sambandho. Pasannacitto sumanoti pakārena pasannaanāluḷitaavikampitacitto, sumano sundaramano somanassasahagatacittoti attho.

78. Remembering his past accumulations, having become joyful, he proclaimed the Apadāna of his past conduct, speaking the verses beginning with 'Jātiyā sattavassohaṃ' (At seven years of age). Therein, 'jātiyā' (by birth) means from the time of exiting his mother's womb—this is the meaning. The connection is: 'I, being seven years old, of full years, saw the Leader of the World, the Blessed One Tissa.' 'Pasannacitto sumano' (with a serene mind, joyful) means his mind was pleased, unagitated, and unwavering; 'sumano' means having a beautiful mind, a mind accompanied by joy—this is the meaning.

79. Tissassāhaṃ bhagavatoti tikkhattuṃ jātoti tisso, so mātugabbhato, manussajātito, pañcakkhandhato ca mutto hutvā jāto nibbatto buddho jātoti attho. Tassa tissassa bhagavato tādino, lokajeṭṭhassa asanabodhiṃ uttamaṃ ropayinti sambandho.

79. Regarding 'Tissassāhaṃ bhagavato' (of the Blessed One Tissa, I...), 'Tissa' is so-called because he was born three times. The meaning is: he was born from his mother's womb, from the human birth, and born freed from the five aggregates—having become a Buddha, he was born. The connection is: 'I planted the supreme Asana Bodhi tree of that Blessed One Tissa, the Imperturbable, the Foremost in the World.'

80. Asano nāmadheyyenāti nāmapaññattiyā nāmasaññāya asano nāma asanarukkho bodhi ahosīti attho. Dharaṇīruhapādapoti vallirukkhapabbatagaṅgāsāgarādayo dhāretīti dharaṇī, kā sā? Pathavī, tassaṃ ruhati patiṭṭhahatīti dharaṇīruho, pādena pivatīti pādapo, pādasaṅkhātena mūlena siñcitodakaṃ pivati āporasaṃ sinehaṃ dhāretīti attho. Dharaṇīruho ca so pādapo cāti dharaṇīruhapādapo, taṃ uttamaṃ asanaṃ bodhiṃ pañca vassāni paricariṃ posesinti attho.

80. Regarding 'Asano nāmadheyyena' (by the name Asana), the meaning is that by name-concept, by name-perception, the tree named Asana became the Bodhi tree. Regarding 'Dharaṇīruhapādapo' (earth-growing tree): because it supports vines, trees, mountains, rivers, oceans, and so forth, it is called 'dharaṇī' (earth). What is that? The earth. Because it grows and is established on it, it is 'dharaṇīruha' (earth-grown). Because it drinks with its foot, it is 'pādapo' (foot-drinker); the meaning is that with its root, designated as a 'foot', it drinks the sprinkled water and holds the water-essence, the moisture. And since it is an earth-grown plant and a foot-drinker, it is a 'dharaṇīruhapādapo'. The meaning is: 'I tended and nurtured that supreme Asana Bodhi tree for five years.'

81. Pupphitaṃ pādapaṃ disvāti taṃ mayā positaṃ asanabodhirukkhaṃ pupphitaṃ accharayoggabhūtapupphattā abbhutaṃ lomahaṃsakaraṇaṃ disvā sakaṃ [M 2.0087] kammaṃ attano kammaṃ pakittento pakārena kathayanto buddhaseṭṭhassa santikaṃ agamāsinti attho. Sesaṃ sabbattha uttānatthamevāti.

81. Regarding 'Pupphitaṃ pādapaṃ disvā' (Seeing the flowering tree), the meaning is that, having seen that Asana Bodhi tree nurtured by me flowering—it being marvelous and hair-raising due to its flowering being fit for a marvel—while proclaiming his own deed, his own action, speaking of it in detail, he went to the presence of the Supreme Buddha. The rest is clear in meaning everywhere.

Asanabodhiyattheraapadānavaṇṇanā samattā.

The commentary on the Apadāna of the Elder Asanabodhiya is complete.

Chaṭṭhavaggavaṇṇanā samattā.

The commentary on the sixth chapter is complete.

7. Sakacintaniyavaggo

7. The Sakacintaniya Chapter

1. Sakacintaniyattheraapadānavaṇṇanā

1. Commentary on the Apadāna of the Elder Sakacintaniya

Pavanaṃ [V 2.0080] kānanaṃ disvātiādikaṃ āyasmato sakacintaniyattherassa apadānaṃ. Ayampi purimabuddhesu katādhikāro tattha tattha bhave vivaṭṭūpanissayāni puññāni upacinanto vipassissa bhagavato kāle ekasmiṃ kulagehe nibbatto vuddhimanvāya tassa bhagavato āyupariyosāne uppanno [P 0.0385] dharamānaṃ bhagavantaṃ apāpuṇitvā parinibbutakāle isipabbajjaṃ pabbajitvā himavante vasanto vivekaṃ ramaṇīyaṃ ekaṃ vanaṃ patvā tatthevekāya kandarāya pulinacetiyaṃ katvā bhagavati saññaṃ katvā sadhātukasaññañca katvā vanapupphehi pūjetvā namassamāno paricari. So tena puññakammena devamanussesu saṃsaranto dvīsu aggaṃ aggasampattiṃ aggañca cakkavattisampattiṃ anubhavitvā imasmiṃ buddhuppāde ekasmiṃ kulagehe nibbatto vibhavasampanno saddhāsampanno satthari pasīditvā pabbajitvā arahā chaḷabhiñño ahosi.

‘Having seen the forest, the thicket,’ and so forth, is the Apadāna of the Venerable Sakacintaniya. He too, having made a meritorious aspiration in the presence of former Buddhas and accumulating merits that support turning away from the cycle of rebirths in various existences, was reborn in a certain family during the time of the Blessed One Vipassī. Having reached maturity, born towards the end of that Blessed One's lifespan, he did not meet the living Blessed One. At the time of the Parinibbāna, he went forth as an ascetic. Dwelling in the Himalayas, he reached a secluded, delightful forest, and there, in a certain grotto, he made a sand cetiya. Establishing the perception of the Blessed One and the perception that it contained relics, he worshipped and attended to it, paying homage with forest flowers. Through that meritorious deed, while transmigrating among gods and humans, he experienced the highest prosperity, supreme in two spheres, and the highest sovereignty of a wheel-turning monarch. During this Buddha-era, he was reborn in a family endowed with wealth and faith. Having gained confidence in the Teacher, he went forth and became an Arahant possessed of the six higher knowledges.

1. So attano pubbakammaṃ saritvā somanassajāto pubbacaritāpadānaṃ pakāsento pavanaṃ kānanaṃ disvātiādimāha. Tattha pavananti pakārena vanaṃ patthaṭaṃ vitthiṇṇaṃ gahanabhūtanti pavanaṃ. Kānanaṃ avakucchitaṃ ānanaṃ avahanaṃ satataṃ sīhabyagghayakkharakkhasamaddahatthiassasupaṇṇauragehi vihaṅgagaṇasaddakukkuṭakokilehi vā bahalanti kānanaṃ, taṃ kānanasaṅkhātaṃ pavanaṃ manussasaddavirahitattā appasaddaṃ nissaddanti attho. Anāvilanti na āvilaṃ upaddavarahitanti attho. Isīnaṃ anuciṇṇanti buddhapaccekabuddhaarahantakhīṇāsavasaṅkhātānaṃ isīnaṃ anuciṇṇaṃ nisevitanti attho. Āhutīnaṃ [M 2.0088] paṭiggahanti āhunaṃ vuccati pūjāsakkāraṃ paṭiggahaṃ gehasadisanti attho.

1. Remembering his own past deed, he became joyful and, revealing the Apadāna of his past conduct, spoke the verses beginning with, ‘Having seen the forest, the thicket.’ Therein, `pavana` means a forest that is diverse, spread out, wide, and dense. `Kānana` is so called because it is thick with lions, tigers, yakkhas, rakkhasas, elephants in rut, horses, supaṇṇas, and serpents, or with the sounds of flocks of birds, roosters, and cuckoos. That `pavana`, also known as a `kānana`, is quiet and still due to the absence of human sounds; this is the meaning. `Anāvila` means not turbid, free from disturbance; this is the meaning. `Frequented by sages` means frequented and resorted to by sages, namely Buddhas, Paccekabuddhas, and Arahants whose taints are destroyed; this is the meaning. `A receptacle for offerings` means that worship and honor are called `āhuna`, and a `paṭiggaha` is a receptacle, like a house; this is the meaning.

2. Thūpaṃ katvāna veḷunāti veḷupesikāhi cetiyaṃ katvāti attho. Nānāpupphaṃ samokirinti campakādīhi anekehi pupphehi samokiriṃ pūjesinti attho. Sammukhā viya sambuddhanti [V 2.0081] sajīvamānassa sambuddhassa sammukhā iva nimmitaṃ uppāditaṃ cetiyaṃ ahaṃ abhi visesena vandiṃ paṇāmamakāsinti attho. Sesaṃ suviññeyyamevāti.

2. ‘Having made a stupa with bamboo’ means having made a shrine with bamboo strips; this is the meaning. ‘Scattering various flowers’ means ‘I scattered, I honored with many flowers such as campaka, and so forth’; this is the meaning. ‘As if face to face with the Sambuddha’ means ‘I especially venerated, I paid homage to the shrine created, produced, as if in the presence of the living Sambuddha’; this is the meaning. The rest is easily comprehensible.

Sakacintaniyattheraapadānavaṇṇanā samattā.

The commentary on the Apadāna of the Elder Sakacintaniya is complete.

2. Avopupphiyattheraapadānavaṇṇanā

2. The Commentary on the Apadāna of Avopupphiyatthera

Vihārā abhinikkhammātiādikaṃ āyasmato avopupphiyattherassa apadānaṃ. Ayampi purimabuddhesu katādhikāro tattha tattha bhave vivaṭṭūpanissayāni puññāni upacinanto sikhissa bhagavato kāle kulagehe nibbatto viññutaṃ patto saddhāsampanno dhammaṃ sutvā somanassappatto nānāpupphāni ubhohi hatthehi gahetvā buddhassa upari abbhukkiri. So tena puññena devamanussesu saṃsaranto [P 0.0386] saggasampattiñca cakkavattisampattiñca anubhavitvā sabbattha pūjito imasmiṃ buddhuppāde ekasmiṃ kulagehe nibbato vuddhippatto sāsane pasīditvā pabbajitvā nacirasseva arahā ahosi. Ā samantato kāsati dippatīti ākāso, tasmiṃ ākāse pupphānaṃ avakiritattā avopupphiyattheroti pākaṭo.

‘Having left the monastery,’ and so forth, is the Apadāna of the Venerable Avopupphiya. He too, having made a meritorious aspiration in the presence of former Buddhas and accumulating merits that support turning away from the cycle of rebirths in various existences, was reborn in a family home during the time of the Blessed One Sikhī. Having reached maturity and being endowed with faith, upon hearing the Dhamma he was filled with joy. Taking various flowers in both hands, he scattered them over the Buddha. Through that meritorious deed, while transmigrating among gods and humans, he experienced heavenly prosperity and the sovereignty of a wheel-turning monarch, and was honored everywhere. During this Buddha-era, he was reborn in a family home, reached maturity, gained confidence in the Teaching, went forth, and in no long time became an Arahant. The sky is called `ākāsa` because it shines (`kāsati`, `dippati`) all around (`ā samantato`). Because flowers were scattered down (`avakiritattā`) in that sky (`ākāse`), he became known as the Elder Avopupphiya.

7. Evaṃ pattasantipado attano pubbakammaṃ saritvā somanassajāto pubbacaritāpadānaṃ pakāsento vihārā abhinikkhammātiādimāha. Tattha vihārāti visesena harati catūhi iriyāpathehi apatantaṃ attabhāvaṃ āharati pavatteti etthāti vihāro, tasmā vihārā abhi visesena nikkhamma nikkhamitvā. Abbhuṭṭhāsi ca caṅkameti caṅkamanatthāya saṭṭhiratane caṅkame abhivisesena uṭṭhāsi, abhiruhīti attho. Catusaccaṃ [M 2.0089] pakāsentoti tasmiṃ caṅkame caṅkamanto dukkhasamudayanirodhamaggasaccasaṅkhātaṃ catusaccaṃ pakāsento pākaṭaṃ karonto amataṃ padaṃ nibbānaṃ desento vibhajanto uttānīkaronto tasmiṃ caṅkameti sambandho.

7. Thus, having attained the state of peace, he recalled his past deeds and, filled with joy, proclaimed the Apadāna of his past conduct, speaking the verses beginning, ‘Having left the monastery.’ Therein, `vihāra` (monastery) is so called because it is a place where one especially supports (`visesena harati`) one's individual existence, carrying it on (`āharati pavatteti`) through the four postures without letting it fail. Therefore, `from the monastery` means having especially departed from it. `He arose upon the walking path` means that for the purpose of walking, he especially arose upon, that is, he ascended, the sixty-cubit walking path. `Expounding the Four Truths` means that while walking on that path, he was expounding, making manifest, teaching, analyzing, and clarifying the Four Truths—namely, the truths of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path—and the deathless state, Nibbāna. This is the connection to the words `on that walking path`.

8. Sikhissa giramaññāya, buddhaseṭṭhassa tādinoti seṭṭhassa tādiguṇasamaṅgissa sikhissa buddhassa giraṃ saddaṃ ghosaṃ aññāya jānitvā. Nānāpupphaṃ gahetvānāti nāgapunnāgādianekāni pupphāni gahetvā āharitvā. Ākāsamhi samokirinti caṅkamantassa bhagavato muddhani ākāse okiriṃ pūjesiṃ.

8. ‘Having understood the speech of Sikhī, the supreme Buddha, the Such-like One’ means having known the speech, the sound, the voice of the Buddha Sikhī, the supreme one, who was possessed of the quality of being ‘such’. ‘Having taken various flowers’ means having taken and brought many flowers, such as nāga and punnāga blossoms. ‘I scattered them in the sky’ means: I scattered them, I worshipped, in the sky above the head of the Blessed One as he was walking on the path.

9. Tena kammena dvipadindāti dvipadānaṃ devabrahmamanussānaṃ inda padhānabhūta. Narāsabha narānaṃ [V 2.0082] āsabhabhūta. Pattomhi acalaṃ ṭhānanti tumhākaṃ santike pabbajitvā acalaṃ ṭhānaṃ nibbānaṃ patto amhi bhavāmi. Hitvā jayaparājayanti dibbamanussasampattisaṅkhātaṃ jayañca caturāpāyadukkhasaṅkhātaṃ parājayañca hitvā chaḍḍetvā nibbānaṃ pattosmīti attho. Sesaṃ suviññeyyamevāti.

9. ‘By that deed, lord of bipeds’ means lord and chief among bipeds, that is, among gods, Brahmās, and humans. ‘Bull among men’ means foremost among men. ‘I have attained the unshakable state’ means: having gone forth in your presence, I have attained the unshakable state, Nibbāna. ‘Abandoning victory and defeat’ means: having abandoned and left behind victory, which is designated as divine and human prosperity, and defeat, which is designated as the suffering of the four woeful states, I have attained Nibbāna; this is the meaning. The rest is easily understood.

Avopupphiyattheraapadānavaṇṇanā samatto.

The Commentary on the Apadāna of Avopupphiyatthera is complete.

3. Paccāgamaniyattheraapadānavaṇṇanā

3. The Commentary on the Apadāna of Paccāgamaniya Thera.

Sindhuyā nadiyā tīretiādikaṃ āyasmato paccāgamaniyattherassa apadānaṃ. Ayampi purimabuddhesu katādhikāro tattha tattha bhave vivaṭṭūpanissayāni puññāni upacinanto vipassissa bhagavato kāle sindhuyā gaṅgāya samīpe cakkavākayoniyaṃ nibbatto pubbasambhārayuttattā pāṇino akhādanto sevālameva bhakkhayanto carati. Tasmiṃ samaye vipassibhagavā sattānuggahaṃ karonto tattha agamāsi. Tasmiṃ khaṇe so cakkavāko vijjotamānaṃ [P 0.0387] bhagavantaṃ disvā pasannamānaso tuṇḍena sālarukkhato sālapupphaṃ chinditvā āgamma pūjesi. So teneva cittappasādena tato cuto devaloke uppanno aparāparaṃ chakāmāvacarasampattiṃ anubhavitvā tato cuto manussaloke uppajjitvā cakkavattisampattiādayo anubhavitvā imasmiṃ buddhuppāde ekasmiṃ kulagehe [M 2.0090] nibbatto viññutaṃ patto pubbacaritavasena satthari pasanno pabbajitvā nacirasseva arahā ahosi, cakkavāko hutvā bhagavantaṃ disvā katthaci gantvā pupphamāharitvā pūjitattā pubbapuññanāmena paccāgamaniyattheroti pākaṭo.

The Apadāna of the Venerable Paccāgamaniya Thera, beginning with 'On the bank of the Sindhu River.' He too, having made a foundation of merit under past Buddhas and accumulating in various existences merits that are a strong supporting condition for release from the round of rebirths, was reborn during the time of the Blessed One Vipassī as a ruddy goose near the river Sindhu. Due to his past accumulations, not eating living beings, he went about feeding only on algae. At that time, the Blessed One Vipassī, showing favour to beings, went there. At that moment, the ruddy goose, seeing the radiant Blessed One, with a mind of faith, plucked a sāla flower from a sāla tree with his beak, came, and offered it in worship. Through that very serenity of mind, after passing away from that existence, he was reborn in the celestial world. There, he repeatedly enjoyed the splendour of the six sense-sphere heavens. After passing away from there, he was reborn in the human world, where he experienced the splendour of a universal monarch and so forth. In this Buddha-era, he was born into a certain family, attained discernment, and, by the power of his past conduct, developed faith in the Teacher. He went forth and soon became an Arahant. Because, having been a ruddy goose, he saw the Blessed One, went somewhere, brought back a flower, and worshipped, he became known as Paccāgamaniya Thera by the name of his past merit.

13. Attano pubbakammaṃ saritvā somanassajāto pubbacaritāpadānaṃ pakāsento sindhuyā nadiyā tīretiādimāha. Sīti saddaṃ kurumānā dhunāti kampatīti sindhu, nadati saddaṃ karonto gacchatīti nadi. Cakkavāko ahaṃ tadāti cakkaṃ sīghaṃ gacchantaṃ iva udake vā thale vā ākāse vā sīghaṃ vāti gacchatīti cakkavāko. Tadā vipassiṃ bhagavantaṃ dassanakāle ahaṃ cakkavāko ahosinti attho. Suddhasevālabhakkhohanti aññagocaraamissattā suddhasevālameva khādanto ahaṃ vasāmi. Pāpesu ca susaññatoti pubbavāsanāvasena pāpakaraṇe suṭṭhu saññato tīhi dvārehi saññato susikkhito.

13. Recalling his past deeds, filled with joy, and revealing the Apadāna of his past conduct, he spoke the verse beginning 'On the bank of the Sindhu River.' The word 'Sindhu' means 'that which, making the sound “sī,” shakes and trembles.' The word 'nadi' means 'that which goes while making a sound.' Regarding 'I was a ruddy goose then': a cakkavāka is so called because it travels swiftly like a swiftly moving wheel, whether in water, on land, or in the sky. The meaning is: at the time of seeing the Blessed One Vipassī, I was a ruddy goose. 'Feeding on pure algae' means that, not mixing with other feeding grounds, I lived eating only pure algae. 'And well-restrained in evils' means that by the power of past habituations, I was well-restrained in committing evil, restrained by the three doors, and well-trained.

14. Addasaṃ [V 2.0083] virajaṃ buddhanti rāgadosamohavirahitattā virajaṃ nikkilesaṃ buddhaṃ addasaṃ addakkhiṃ. Gacchantaṃ anilañjaseti anilañjase ākāsapathe gacchantaṃ buddhaṃ. Tuṇḍena mayhaṃ mukhatuṇḍena tālaṃ sālapupphaṃ paggayha paggahetvā vipassissābhiropayiṃ vipassissa bhagavato pūjesinti attho. Sesaṃ suviññeyyamevāti.

14. 'I saw the stainless Buddha' means that because he is free from lust and hatred, he is stainless, free from defilements—I saw the Buddha, I beheld him. 'Walking on the wind’s path' means the Buddha walking on the sky-path. 'With my beak... I offered to Vipassī' means: with my mouth-beak, having taken up a sāla flower, I worshipped the Blessed One Vipassī. The rest is easily understood.

Paccāgamaniyattheraapadānavaṇṇanā samattā.

The Commentary on the Apadāna of Paccāgamaniya Thera is complete.

4. Parappasādakattheraapadānavaṇṇanā

4. The Explanation of the Apadāna of the Elder Parappasādaka.

Usabhaṃ pavaraṃ vīrantiādikaṃ āyasmato parappasādakattherassa apadānaṃ. Ayampi purimabuddhesu katādhikāro tattha tattha bhave vivaṭṭūpanissayāni puññāni upacinanto siddhatthassa bhagavato kāle brāhmaṇakule nibbatto tiṇṇaṃ vedānaṃ pāragū itihāsapañcamānaṃ padako veyyākaraṇo sanighaṇḍukeṭubhānaṃ sākkharappabhedānaṃ lokāyatamahāpurisalakkhaṇesu anavayo nāmena selabrāhmaṇoti pākaṭo siddhatthaṃ bhagavantaṃ disvā dvattiṃsamahāpurisalakkhaṇehi asītianubyañjanehi cāti sayaṃ sobhamānaṃ disvā pasannamānaso anekehi kāraṇehi [M 2.0091] anekāhi [P 0.0388] upamāhi thomanaṃ pakāsesi. So tena puññakammena devaloke sakkamārādayo cha kāmāvacarasampattiyo anubhavitvā manussesu cakkavattisampattiṃ anubhavitvā imasmiṃ buddhuppāde vibhavasampanne ekasmiṃ kulagehe nibbatto viññutaṃ patto satthari pasīdisvā pabbajito nacirasseva catupaṭisambhidāchaḷabhiññappatto mahākhīṇāsavo ahosi, buddhassa thutiyā sattānaṃ sabbesaṃ cittappasādakaraṇato parappasādakattheroti pākaṭo.

The Apadāna of the Venerable Elder Parappasādaka, beginning with 'The Bull, the Excellent, the Hero,' and so on. He too, having made meritorious deeds in the presence of previous Buddhas, accumulating wholesome deeds here and there as a supporting condition for release from the round of rebirths, was reborn in the time of the Blessed One Siddhattha in a brahmin family. He was a master of the three Vedas, with the Itihāsa as the fifth; an expert in metrics and grammar, skilled in the Nighaṇḍu and Keṭubha with their etymological distinctions, and unerring in the Lokāyata and the marks of a great man. Known by the name Sela the brahmin, he saw the Blessed One Siddhattha, who was self-radiant with the thirty-two marks of a great man and the eighty minor characteristics. With a mind of faith, he expressed praise with many reasons and numerous similes. By that meritorious deed, he enjoyed the six sense-sphere splendours in the celestial realms, including those of Sakka and Māra. Then, among humans, he experienced the splendour of a wheel-turning monarch. In this Buddha-era, he was reborn in a wealthy family, attained discernment, gained faith in the Teacher, and went forth. Not long after, he achieved the four analytical knowledges and the six higher knowledges, becoming a great Arahant whose cankers were destroyed. Because he caused the minds of all beings to become serene by praising the Buddha, he became known as the Elder Parappasādaka.

20. Ekadivasaṃ attano pubbakammaṃ saritvā somanassajāto pubbacaritāpadānaṃ pakāsento usabhaṃ pavaraṃ vīrantiādimāha. Tattha usabhanti vasabho nisabho visabho āsabhoti cattāro jeṭṭhapuṅgavā. Tattha gavasatajeṭṭhako vasabho, gavasahassajeṭṭhako nisabho, gavasatasahassajeṭṭhako visabho, gavakoṭisatasahassajeṭṭhako āsabhoti ca yassa kassaci thutiṃ karontā brāhmaṇapaṇḍitā bahussutā attano attano paññāvasena thutiṃ karonti, buddhānaṃ pana sabbākārena thutiṃ kātuṃ samattho ekopi natthi. Appameyyo hi buddho. Vuttañhetaṃ –

20. One day, recalling his past deeds and filled with joy, revealing the Apadāna of his past conduct, he proclaimed, 'The Bull, the Excellent, the Hero,' and so on. Therein, 'usabha' refers to four foremost bulls: vasabha, nisabha, visabha, and āsabha. Among these, vasabha is the chief of a hundred cows, nisabha is the chief of a thousand cows, visabha is the chief of a hundred thousand cows, and āsabha is the chief of a hundred thousand koṭis of cows. When praising someone, learned brahmins of great hearing praise according to their own wisdom, but there is not even one who is capable of praising the Buddhas in every aspect. For the Buddha is immeasurable. And this was said:

“Buddhopi [V 2.0084] buddhassa bhaṇeyya vaṇṇaṃ, kappampi ce aññamabhāsamāno;

Khīyetha kappo ciradīghamantare, vaṇṇo na khīyetha tathāgatassā”ti. (dī. ni. aṭṭha. 1.304; 3.141; ma. ni. aṭṭha. 2.425; udā. aṭṭha. 53) –

“Even a Buddha praising another Buddha, speaking for a whole aeon without ceasing, that aeon, long and lasting, might come to an end, but the praise of the Tathāgata would never be exhausted.”

Ādikaṃ. Ayampi brāhmaṇo mukhārūḷhavasena ekapasīdanavasena “āsabha”nti vattabbe “usabha”ntiādimāha. Varitabbo patthetabboti varo. Anekesu kappasatasahassesu katavīriyattā vīro.
