At that time, seeing the Blessed One Phussa who had arrived in that region, and seeing the six-colored Buddha-rays emanating from his body, darting here and there like rays radiating from a torch, he became confident. Raising his joined hands, he paid homage and gladdened his mind. With that same joy and happiness, he passed away and was reborn in Tusita and other realms. There, having experienced the six kinds of sensual-sphere prosperity, during this Buddha-dispensation he was born into a family. Having reached maturity, due to the influence of past habituations, he went forth and not long after became an Arahant.

35. So aparabhāge pubbakammaṃ saritvā somanassajāto pubbacaritāpadānaṃ pakāsento pabbate himavantamhītiādimāha. Taṃ sabbaṃ uttānatthamevāti.

35. In a later period, recalling his past deed, with joy arisen, he declared the Apadāna of his former conduct, beginning with 'On the Himavanta mountain.' All of this has a clear meaning.

Dutiyaraṃsisaññakattheraapadānavaṇṇanā samattā.

The commentary on the Apadāna of the Thera Dutiyaraṃsisaññaka is concluded.

7. Phaladāyakattheraapadānavaṇṇanā

7. Commentary on the Apadāna of the Thera Phaladāyaka.

Pabbate himavantamhītiādikaṃ āyasmato phaladāyakattherassa apadānaṃ. Ayampi purimabuddhesu katakusalasambhāro tattha tattha bhave vivaṭṭūpanissayāni puññāni upacinanto phussassa bhagavato kāle ekasmiṃ kulagehe nibbatto sukhappatto taṃ sabbaṃ pahāya tāpasapabbajjaṃ pabbajitvā kharājinacammadhārī hutvā viharati. Tasmiñca samaye phussaṃ bhagavantaṃ tattha sampattaṃ disvā pasannamānaso madhurāni phalāni gahetvā bhojesi. So teneva kusalena devalokādīsu puññasampattiyo anubhavitvā imasmiṃ buddhuppāde ekasmiṃ kulagehe nibbatto vuddhimanvāya satthari pasīditvā pabbajitvā nacirasseva arahā ahosi.

The Apadāna of the Venerable Phaladāyaka Thera, beginning with 'On the Himavanta mountain.' He too, having accumulated a store of wholesome deeds under previous Buddhas, accumulating merits that are a supporting condition for liberation in various existences, was born into a family during the time of the Blessed One Phussa. Having attained happiness, he abandoned all that and went forth into the ascetic life, becoming a wearer of a rough hide garment. At that time, seeing the Blessed One Phussa who had arrived there, with a confident mind he took sweet fruits and served them. Through that wholesome deed, he experienced the prosperities of merit in the divine world and other realms. During this Buddha-dispensation, he was born into a family. Having reached maturity and gained confidence in the Teacher, he went forth and not long after became an Arahant.

39. So aparabhāge attano pubbakammaṃ anussaritvā pubbacaritāpadānaṃ pakāsento pabbate himavantamhītiādimāha. Taṃ sabbaṃ heṭṭhā vuttanayattā uttānatthamevāti.

39. In a later period, recollecting his own past deed and declaring the Apadāna of his former conduct, he spoke, beginning with 'On the Himavanta mountain.' All of this has a clear meaning due to the method stated previously.

Phaladāyakattheraapadānavaṇṇanā samattā.

The commentary on the Apadāna of the Thera Phaladāyaka is concluded.

8. Saddasaññakattheraapadānavaṇṇanā

8. Commentary on the Apadāna of the Thera Saddasaññaka.

Pabbate himavantamhītiādikaṃ āyasmato saddasaññakattherassa apadānaṃ. Ayampi purimabuddhesu katādhikāro tattha [P 0.0405] tattha bhave vivaṭṭūpanissayāni puññāni upacinanto phussassa bhagavato kāle ekasmiṃ kulagehe [M 2.0112] nibbatto vuddhippatto saddhājāto tāpasapabbajjaṃ pabbajitvā himavantamhi araññāvāse vasanto attano anukampāya upagatassa bhagavato dhammaṃ sutvā dhammesu [V 2.0104] cittaṃ pasādetvā yāvatāyukaṃ ṭhatvā aparabhāge kālaṃ katvā tusitādīsu chasu kāmāvacarasampattiyo ca manussesu manussasampattiyo ca anubhavitvā imasmiṃ buddhuppāde ekasmiṃ kulagehe nibbatto vuddhimanvāya saddhājāto pabbajitvā vipassanaṃ vaḍḍhetvā arahattaṃ pāpuṇi.

The Apadāna of the Venerable Saddasaññaka Thera, beginning with 'On the Himavanta mountain.' He too, having made his resolve under former Buddhas, accumulating merits that are a supporting condition for liberation in various existences, was born into a family during the time of the Blessed One Phussa. Having reached maturity, with faith arisen, he went forth into the ascetic life. Dwelling in a forest abode in the Himavanta, he listened to the Dhamma of the Blessed One who had approached out of compassion for him. Having gained confidence in the teachings, he remained thus for his entire lifespan. In a later period, having passed away, he experienced the six kinds of sensual-sphere prosperity in Tusita and other realms, and human prosperity among humans. During this Buddha-dispensation, he was born into a family. Having reached maturity, with faith arisen, he went forth, developed insight, and attained Arahantship.

43. So aparabhāge attano pubbakammaṃ saritvā somanassajāto pubbacaritāpadānaṃ pakāsento pabbate himavantamhītiādimāha. Taṃ sabbaṃ uttānatthamevāti.

43. In a later period, recalling his own past deed, with joy arisen, he declared the Apadāna of his former conduct, beginning with 'On the Himavanta mountain.' All of this has a clear meaning.

Saddasaññakattheraapadānavaṇṇanā samattā.

The commentary on the Apadāna of the Thera Saddasaññaka is concluded.

9. Bodhisiñcakattheraapadānavaṇṇanā

9. Commentary on the Apadāna of the Thera Bodhisiñcaka.

Vipassissa bhagavatotiādikaṃ āyasmato bodhisiñcakattherassa apadānaṃ. Ayampi purimabuddhesu katādhikāro anekāsu jātīsu vivaṭṭūpanissayāni puññāni upacinanto vipassissa bhagavato kāle kulagehe nibbatto sāsane pabbajitvā vattapaṭipattiyā sāsanaṃ sobhayanto mahājane bodhipūjaṃ kurumāne disvā anekāni pupphāni sugandhodakāni ca gāhāpetvā pūjesi. So tena puññena devaloke nibbatto cha kāmāvacarasampattiyo anubhavitvā imasmiṃ buddhuppāde kulagehe nibbatto vuddhimanvāya saddhājāto pabbajitvā nacirasseva arahā ahosi.

The Apadāna of the Venerable Bodhisiñcaka Thera, beginning with 'Of the Blessed One Vipassī.' He too, having made his resolve under former Buddhas, accumulating merits that are a supporting condition for liberation in many births, was born into a family during the time of the Blessed One Vipassī. Having gone forth into the dispensation, he adorned the teaching through the practice of his duties. Seeing the great populace making offerings to the Bodhi tree, he had many flowers and fragrant waters brought and made an offering. By that merit, he was reborn in the divine world. Having experienced the six kinds of sensual-sphere prosperity, during this Buddha-dispensation he was born into a family. Having reached maturity, with faith arisen, he went forth and not long after became an Arahant.

46. So arahā hutvā jhānaphalasukhena vītināmetvā pubbakammaṃ saritvā somanassajāto pubbacaritāpadānaṃ pakāsento vipassissa bhagavatotiādimāha. Tattha visesaṃ paramatthaṃ nibbānaṃ passatīti vipassī, visesena bhabbābhabbajane passatīti vā vipassī, vipassanto catusaccaṃ passanadakkhanasīloti vā vipassī, tassa vipassissa bhagavato mahābodhimaho [M 2.0113] ahūti sambandho. Tatrāpi mahābodhīti bodhi vuccati catūsu maggesu ñāṇaṃ, tamettha nisinno bhagavā paṭivijjhatīti kaṇikārapādaparukkhopi bodhicceva vuccati, mahito ca so devabrahmanarāsurehi bodhi ceti mahābodhi, mahato buddhassa bhagavato bodhīti vā mahābodhi, tassa maho pūjā ahosīti attho. Sesaṃ sabbattha uttānatthamevāti.

46. Having become an Arahant and having passed the time with the bliss of jhāna and its fruition, he recalled his past deed. With joy arisen, he declared the Apadāna of his former conduct, beginning with 'Of the Blessed One Vipassī.' Therein, 'Vipassī' is so-called because he sees the special, ultimate reality, Nibbāna; or, 'Vipassī' is so-called because he sees with distinction beings who are capable and incapable of being taught; or, 'Vipassī' is so-called because, while seeing with insight, he has the nature of seeing and knowing the four truths. The connection is to be understood as: 'There was a great festival for the Mahābodhi of that Blessed One Vipassī.' Therein, as to 'Mahābodhi': 'bodhi' is said to be the knowledge in the four paths. Because the Blessed One, seated there, penetrated it, even the kaṇikāra tree is called 'bodhi.' And because it was honored by devas, brahmās, and asuras, and it is 'bodhi,' it is called 'Mahābodhi.' Or, it is 'Mahābodhi' because it is the 'bodhi' of the great, Blessed Buddha. The meaning is: 'There was a great festival, an offering, for it.' The remainder has a clear meaning everywhere.

Bodhisiñcakattheraapadānavaṇṇanā samattā.

The commentary on the Apadāna of the Thera Bodhisiñcaka is concluded.

10. Padumapupphiyattheraapadānavaṇṇanā

10. Commentary on the Apadāna of the Thera Padumapupphiya.

Pokkharavanaṃ [P 0.0406][V 2.0105] paviṭṭhotiādikaṃ āyasmato padumapupphiyattherassa apadānaṃ. Ayampi purimabuddhesu katādhikāro tattha tattha bhave vivaṭṭūpanissayāni puññāni upacinanto phussassa bhagavato kāle ekasmiṃ kulagehe nibbatto vuddhimanvāya padumasampannaṃ ekaṃ pokkharaṇiṃ pavisitvā bhisamuḷāle khādanto pokkharaṇiyā avidūre gacchamānaṃ phussaṃ bhagavantaṃ disvā pasannamānaso tato padumāni ocinitvā ākāse ukkhipitvā bhagavantaṃ pūjesi, tāni pupphāni ākāse vitānaṃ hutvā aṭṭhaṃsu. So bhiyyosomattāya pasannamānaso pabbajitvā vattapaṭipattisāro samaṇadhammaṃ pūretvā tato cuto tusitabhavanamalaṃ kurumāno viya tattha uppajjitvā kamena cha kāmāvacarasampattiyo ca manussasampattiyo ca anubhavitvā imasmiṃ buddhuppāde kulagehe nibbatto vuddhippatto saddhājāto pabbajitvā nacirasseva arahā ahosi.

Beginning with 'Entering the lotus grove,' and so on—this is the Apadāna of the Venerable Padumapupphiya Thera. He too, having made his resolve under former Buddhas and accumulating merits in various existences as a support for liberation, was born in a certain family in the time of the Blessed One Phussa. Having come of age, he entered a pond rich with lotuses and, while eating lotus roots and stalks, saw the Blessed One Phussa passing by not far from the pond. With a mind of faith, he plucked lotuses from there, tossed them into the sky, and honored the Blessed One. Those flowers remained in the sky, forming a canopy. He, with even greater joy and a mind of faith, went forth and, taking the practice of duties as his essence, fulfilled the ascetic's way of life. Passing away from there, as if adorning the Tusita realm, he was reborn there. In due course, having experienced the six kinds of sensual-sphere perfections and human perfections, he was born in a family in this Buddha's dispensation. Having reached maturity, with faith arisen, he went forth and before long became an arahant.

51. So aparabhāge attano pubbakammaṃ saritvā somanassajāto pubbacaritāpadānaṃ pakāsento pokkharavanaṃ paviṭṭhotiādimāha. Tattha pakārena naḷadaṇḍapattādīhi kharantīti pokkharā, pokkharānaṃ samuṭṭhitaṭṭhena samūhanti pokkharavanaṃ, padumagacchasaṇḍehi maṇḍitaṃ majjhaṃ paviṭṭho ahanti attho. Sesaṃ sabbattha uttānamevāti.

51. Later, recollecting his past deeds and with joy arisen, he declared his former conduct in the Apadāna, beginning with 'Entering the lotus grove.' Therein, the etymology is: 'because they flow (kharanti) with various parts (pakārena) such as reeds, stalks, and leaves, they are called lotuses (pokkharā)'; 'a grove of lotuses (pokkharavanaṃ) is a collection (samūha) of them, on account of their arising together (samuṭṭhitaṭṭhena)'. The meaning is: 'I entered the middle, which was adorned with thickets of lotus plants.' The rest is clear in meaning everywhere.

Padumapupphiyattheraapadānavaṇṇanā samattā.

The commentary on the Apadāna of the Venerable Padumapupphiya Thera is concluded.

Navamavaggavaṇṇanā samattā.

The commentary on the Ninth Chapter is concluded.

10. Sudhāvaggo

10. The Plaster Chapter

1. Sudhāpiṇḍiyattheraapadānavaṇṇanā

1. The Commentary on the Apadāna of the Elder Sudhāpiṇḍiya

Pūjārahe [M 2.0114][V 2.0106] pūjayatotiādikaṃ āyasmato sudhāpiṇḍiyattherassa apadānaṃ. Ayampi purimabuddhesu katādhikāro tattha tattha bhave vivaṭṭūpanissayāni puññāni upacinanto siddhatthassa bhagavato kāle bhagavati dharamāne puññaṃ kātumasakkonto parinibbute bhagavati tassa dhātuṃ nidahitvā cetiye karīyamāne sudhāpiṇḍamadāsi. So tena puññena catunnavutikappato paṭṭhāya etthantare caturāpāyamadisvā devamanussasampattiyo anubhavitvā imasmiṃ buddhuppāde ekasmiṃ kulagehe nibbatto viññutaṃ patvā satthari pasīditvā pabbajito nacirasseva arahā ahosi.

Beginning with 'Honoring those worthy of honor,' and so on—this is the Apadāna of the Venerable Sudhāpiṇḍiya Thera. He too, having made his resolve under former Buddhas and accumulating merits in various existences as a support for liberation, was unable to perform a meritorious deed in the time of the Blessed One Siddhattha while the Blessed One was still living. After the Blessed One had attained final Nibbāna, when a cetiya was being built enshrining his relics, he gave a lump of plaster. Through that merit, for the ninety-four eons since then, he did not see the four woeful states in the interim, and having experienced celestial and human attainments, he was born in a certain family in this Buddha's dispensation. Having reached maturity, he gained faith in the Teacher, went forth, and before long became an arahant.

1-2. So aparabhāge attano pubbakammaṃ saritvā somanassajāto attano pubbacaritāpadānaṃ pakāsento pūjārahetiādimāha. Tattha pūjārahā nāma buddhapaccekabuddhaariyasāvakācariyupajjhāyamātāpitugaruādayo, tesu pūjārahesu mālādipadumavatthābharaṇacatupaccayādīhi [P 0.0407] pūjayato pūjayantassa puggalassa puññakoṭṭhāsaṃ sahassasatasahassādivasena saṅkhyaṃ kātuṃ kenaci mahānubhāvenāpi na sakkāti attho. Na kevalameva dharamāne buddhādayo pūjayato, parinibbutassāpi bhagavato cetiyapaṭimābodhiādīsupi eseva nayo.

1-2. Later, recollecting his past deeds and with joy arisen, he declared his former conduct in the Apadāna, beginning with 'Those worthy of honor.' Therein, 'those worthy of honor' refers to Buddhas, Paccekabuddhas, noble disciples, teachers, preceptors, mothers, fathers, revered persons, and so on. The meaning is that for a person who honors these worthy recipients with garlands, lamps, lotuses, robes, ornaments, the four requisites, and so on, the portion of merit cannot be calculated by anyone, even one of great power, in terms of thousands or hundreds of thousands. This principle applies not only to one who honors the Buddhas and others while they are living, but also to offerings made at cetiyas, images, Bodhi trees, and the like of the Blessed One even after he has attained final Nibbāna.

3. Taṃ dīpetuṃ catunnamapi dīpānantiādimāha. Tattha catunnamapi dīpānanti jambudīpaaparagoyānauttarakurupubbavidehasaṅkhātānaṃ catunnaṃ dīpānaṃ tadanugatānaṃ dvisahassaparittadīpānañca ekato katvā sakalacakkavāḷagabbhe issaraṃ cakkavattirajjaṃ kareyyāti attho. Ekissā pūjanāyetanti dhātugabbhe cetiye katāya ekissā pūjāya etaṃ sakalajambudīpe sattaratanādikaṃ sakalaṃ dhanaṃ. Kalaṃ nāgghati soḷasinti cetiye katapūjāya soḷasakkhattuṃ vibhattassa soḷasamakoṭṭhāsassa na agghatīti attho.

3. To illustrate this, he said, 'Even of all four continents,' and so on. Therein, 'all four continents' refers to the four continents designated as Jambudīpa, Aparagoyāna, Uttarakuru, and Pubbavideha, along with their accompanying two thousand lesser islands. The meaning is that even if one were to exercise the sovereign rule of a universal monarch over the entire world-system. Regarding 'by a single offering': all this wealth in the entire Jambudīpa, including the seven treasures and so on, is not worth a single offering made at a cetiya with a relic chamber. Regarding 'is not worth a sixteenth part': the meaning is that it is not worth the sixteenth part of an offering made at a cetiya, that part being one of sixteen divisions.

4. Siddhatthassa…pe… [M 2.0115] phalitantareti narānaṃ aggassa seṭṭhassa siddhatthassa bhagavato cetiye [V 2.0107] dhātugabbhamhi sudhākamme karīyamāne paricchedānaṃ ubhinnamantare vemajjhe, atha vā pupphadānaṭṭhānānaṃ antare phalantiyā mayā sudhāpiṇḍo dinno makkhitoti sambandho. Sesaṃ sabbattha uttānamevāti.

4. Regarding 'Of Siddhattha... in the crack': while the plaster work was being done on the relic chamber of the cetiya of the Blessed One Siddhattha, the foremost and best of men, the connection is to be understood thus: 'a lump of plaster was given and smeared by me in the middle, in the space between two sections, or in a crack between the places for flower offerings.' The rest is clear in meaning everywhere.

Sudhāpiṇḍiyattheraapadānavaṇṇanā samattā.

The commentary on the Apadāna of the Elder Sudhāpiṇḍiya is concluded.

2. Sucintikattheraapadānavaṇṇanā

2. The Commentary on the Apadāna of the Elder Sucintita

Tissassa lokanāthassātiādikaṃ āyasmato sucintikattherassa apadānaṃ. Ayampi purimabuddhesu katādhikāro anekāsu jātīsu nibbānādhigamāya puññaṃ upacinitvā tissassa bhagavato kāle ekasmiṃ kulagehe nibbatto vuddhimanvāya satthari pasīditvā satthu nisīdanatthāya parisuddhaṃ siliṭṭhaṃ kaṭṭhamayamanagghapīṭhamadāsi. So tena puññakammena sugatisukhamanubhavitvā tattha tattha saṃsaranto imasmiṃ buddhuppāde ekasmiṃ kulagehe nibbatto vuddhimanvāya satthari pasīditvā pabbajito nacirasseva arahā ahosi.

Beginning with 'Of Tissa, the Protector of the World,' and so on—this is the Apadāna of the Venerable Sucintita Thera. He too, having made his resolve under former Buddhas and having accumulated merit in many lifetimes for the attainment of Nibbāna, was born in a certain family in the time of the Blessed One Tissa. Having come of age, he gained faith in the Teacher and gave a pure, smooth, priceless wooden stool for the Teacher's seating. Through that meritorious deed, he experienced the happiness of good destinations, wandering through various existences. In this Buddha's dispensation, he was born in a certain family, and having come of age, he gained faith in the Teacher, went forth, and before long became an arahant.

8. So pattaarahattaphalo pubbakammaṃ saritvā somanassajāto pubbacaritāpadānaṃ pakāsento tissassa lokanāthassātiādimāha. Taṃ sabbaṃ uttānatthamevāti.

8. He, having attained the fruit of arahantship, recollected his past deeds, and with joy arisen, declared the Apadāna of his former conduct, beginning with, 'Of Tissa, the Protector of the World.' All of that has a clear meaning.

Sucintikattheraapadānavaṇṇanā samattā.

The commentary on the Apadāna of the Elder Sucintita is concluded.

3. Aḍḍhaceḷakattheraapadānavaṇṇanā

3. The Commentary on the Apadāna of the Elder Aḍḍhaceḷaka

Tissassāhaṃ [P 0.0408] bhagavatotiādikaṃ āyasmato aḍḍhaceḷakattherassa apadānaṃ. Ayampi thero purimabuddhesu katādhikāro tattha tattha bhave vivaṭṭūpanissayāni puññāni upacinanto tissassa bhagavato kāle ekenākusalena kammena duggatakulagehe nibbatto vuddhimanvāya saddhammadesanaṃ ñatvā pasannamānaso cīvaratthāya aḍḍhabhāgaṃ ekaṃ dussamadāsi. So [M 2.0116] teneva pītisomanassena kālaṃ katvā sagge nibbatto cha kāmāvacarasampattimanubhavitvā tato cuto manussesu manussasampattīnaṃ aggabhūtaṃ cakkavattisampattiṃ anubhavitvā imasmiṃ buddhuppāde ekasmiṃ addhakule [V 2.0108] nibbatto vuddhippatto satthu dhammadesanaṃ sutvā pasannamānaso pabbajitvā nacirasseva arahā ahosi.

The words beginning with 'Of Tissa, the Blessed One...' are the Apadāna of the Venerable Elder Aḍḍhaceḷaka. This elder, too, having made an aspiration in the presence of former Buddhas and accumulating, in various existences, merits that serve as a basis for liberation, was born in a poor family home during the time of the Blessed One Tissa due to a single unwholesome deed. Having come of age and heard the teaching of the true Dhamma, with a gladdened mind, he gave a single piece of cloth, half its value, for the purpose of a robe. Through that very joy and gladness, he passed away and was reborn in heaven. Having experienced the sixfold sensual-sphere attainments, he passed away from there and, among humans, experienced the fortune of a wheel-turning monarch, which is the foremost of human attainments. In this Buddha-dispensation, he was born into a poor family, and having come of age, he heard the Teacher’s Dhamma teaching. With a gladdened mind, he went forth and, before long, became an arahant.

14. So aparabhāge attano pubbakammaṃ saritvā somanassajāto pubbacaritāpadānaṃ pakāsento tissassāhaṃ bhagavatotiādimāha. Taṃ sabbaṃ uttānatthamevāti.

14. In a later time, recollecting his own past deeds and becoming filled with joy, he proclaimed the apadāna of his former conduct, speaking the verses beginning, 'Of Tissa, the Blessed One...'. All of that has a plain meaning.

Aḍḍhaceḷakattheraapadānavaṇṇanā samattā.

The Commentary on the Apadāna of the Elder Aḍḍhaceḷaka is concluded.

4. Sūcidāyakattheraapadānavaṇṇanā

4. Commentary on the Apadāna of the Elder Sūcidāyaka

Kammārohaṃ pure āsintiādikaṃ āyasmato sūcidāyakattherassa apadānaṃ. Ayampi purimabuddhesu katādhikāro antarantarā kusalabījāni pūrento vipassissa bhagavato kāle antarantarā katena ekena kammacchiddena kammārakule nibbatto vuddhimanvāya sakasippesu nipphattiṃ patto satthu dhammadesanaṃ sutvā pasannamānaso cīvarasibbanatthāya sūcidānamadāsi, tena puññena dibbasampattiṃ anubhavitvā aparabhāge manussesu uppanno cakkavattādayo sampattiyo ca anubhavanto uppannuppannabhave tikkhapañño vajīrañāṇo ahosi. So kamena imasmiṃ buddhuppāde nibbatto vuddhippatto mahaddhano saddhājāto tikkhapañño ahosi. So ekadivasaṃ satthu dhammadesanaṃ sutvā dhammānusārena ñāṇaṃ pesetvā nisinnāsaneyeva arahā ahosi.

Beginning with 'Once I was a blacksmith,' this is the Apadāna of the Venerable Elder Sūcidāyaka. He too, having made an aspiration under former Buddhas, from time to time fulfilling the seeds of skillfulness, during the time of the Blessed One Vipassī, due to a single intervening karmic flaw, was born in a blacksmith's family. Having come of age, he attained proficiency in all crafts. Hearing the Teacher's Dhamma discourse, his mind became gladdened, and he gave a needle for the purpose of sewing robes. Through that merit, he experienced divine prosperity. In a later time, being born among humans and experiencing various prosperities, including that of a wheel-turning monarch, in each succeeding existence, he possessed sharp wisdom and diamond-like knowledge. In due course, in this Buddha-dispensation, he was born, grew up, and became very wealthy and sharp-witted. One day, hearing the Teacher's Dhamma discourse, he directed his knowledge in accordance with the Dhamma, and right there on his seat, he became an arahant.

19. So arahā samāno attano pubbakammaṃ saritvā somanassajāto pubbacaritāpadānaṃ pakāsento kammārohaṃ pure āsintiādimāha. Tattha kammāroti ayokammalohakammādinā kammena jīvati ruhati vuddhiṃ virūḷhiṃ āpajjatīti kammāro, pubbe puññakaraṇakāle kammāro āsiṃ ahosinti attho. Sesaṃ sabbattha uttānamevāti.

19. Having become an arahant, recollecting his past deeds, filled with joy, he declared his former conduct in the Apadāna, beginning with 'Once I was a blacksmith.' Here, 'blacksmith' means one who lives by the work of iron, metal, etc., or lives, grows, and thrives by such work. The meaning is, 'In the past, during the time of doing meritorious deeds, I was a blacksmith.' The rest is clear throughout.

Sūcidāyakattheraapadānavaṇṇanā samattā.

The Commentary on the Apadāna of the Elder Sūcidāyaka is concluded.

5. Gandhamāliyattheraapadānavaṇṇanā

5. Commentary on the Apadāna of the Elder Gandhamāliya

Siddhatthassa [M 2.0117][P 0.0409] bhagavatotiādikaṃ āyasmato gandhamāliyattherassa apadāna. Ayampi purimabuddhesu [V 2.0109] katādhikāro siddhatthassa bhagavato kāle kulagehe nibbatto mahaddhano mahābhogo ahosi. So satthari pasīditvā candanāgarukappūrakassaturādīni anekāni sugandhāni vaḍḍhetvā satthu gandhathūpaṃ kāresi. Tassupari sumanapupphehi chādesi, buddhañca aṭṭhaṅganamakkāraṃ akāsi. So tena puññakammena devamanussesu sampattiyo anubhavitvā imasmiṃ buddhuppāde vibhavasampanne ekasmiṃ kulagehe nibbatto vuddhimanvāya satthari pasīditvā pabbajito nacirasseva arahā ahosi.

The words beginning with 'Of the Blessed One Siddhattha...' are the Apadāna of the Venerable Elder Gandhamāliya. He too, having made an aspiration under former Buddhas, was born into a household during the time of the Blessed One Siddhattha and became very wealthy and affluent. Having gained faith in the Teacher, he prepared in abundance many fragrant substances such as sandalwood, aloeswood, camphor, and musk, and had a fragrant thūpa made for the Teacher. He covered it over with sumana flowers and paid homage to the Buddha with the eight-limbed prostration. Through that meritorious deed, he experienced prosperity among gods and humans. In this Buddha-dispensation, he was born into a prosperous household endowed with wealth. Having come of age and gained faith in the Teacher, he went forth and, before long, became an arahant.

24. So aparabhāge attano pubbakammaṃ saritvā somanassajāto pubbacaritāpadānaṃ pakāsento siddhatthassa bhagavatotiādimāha. Taṃ sabbaṃ uttānatthamevāti.

24. In a later time, recollecting his own past deeds and becoming filled with joy, he proclaimed the apadāna of his former conduct, speaking the verses beginning, 'Of the Blessed One Siddhattha...'. All of that has a plain meaning.

Gandhamāliyattheraapadānavaṇṇanā samattā.

The Commentary on the Apadāna of the Elder Gandhamāliya is concluded.

6. Tipupphiyattheraapadānavaṇṇanā

6. Commentary on the Apadāna of the Elder Tipupphiya

Migaluddo pure āsintiādikaṃ āyasmato tipupphiyattherassa apadānaṃ. Ayampi purimabuddhesu katādhikāro antarā kenaci akusalacchiddena vipassissa bhagavato kāle nesādakule nibbatto migaluddo hutvā araññe viharati. Tadā vipassissa bhagavato pāṭalibodhiṃ sampuṇṇapattapallavaṃ haritavaṇṇaṃ nīlobhāsaṃ manoramaṃ disvā tīhi pupphehi pūjetvā purāṇapattaṃ chaḍḍetvā bhagavato sammukhā viya pāṭalimahābodhiṃ vandi. So tena puññena tato cuto devaloke uppanno tattha dibbasampattiṃ aparāparaṃ anubhavitvā tato cuto manussesu jāto tattha cakkavattisampattiādayo anubhavitvā imasmiṃ buddhuppāde ekasmiṃ kulagehe nibbatto vuddhimanvāya satthu dhammadesanaṃ sutvā paṭiladdhasomanassahadayo gehaṃ pahāya pabbajitvā nacirasseva arahā ahosi.

Beginning with 'Migaluddo pure āsiṃ,' this is the Apadāna of the Venerable Elder Tipupphiya. He, too, having established his aspiration under former Buddhas, due to some unwholesome karmic impediment, during the time of the Blessed One Vipassī, was born into a hunter's family and lived in the forest. Seeing the Pāṭali Bodhi tree of the Blessed One Vipassī—complete with leaves and foliage, green in color, with a blue radiance, and delightful—he offered three flowers, discarded the old leaves, and paid homage to the Pāṭali Great Bodhi tree as if in the presence of the Blessed One. Through that merit, after passing away, he was reborn in the heavenly realm, where he repeatedly experienced divine prosperity. Then, passing away from there, he was born among humans, experiencing the prosperity of a wheel-turning monarch and other blessings. In this Buddha’s dispensation, he was born into a family. Growing up, upon hearing the Teacher’s Dhamma discourse, his heart regained joy. He left home, went forth, and before long became an arahant.

31. So [M 2.0118] evaṃ siddhippatto attano pubbakammaṃ saritvā somanassajāto pubbacaritāpadānaṃ pakāsento migaluddo pure āsintiādimāha. Tattha maraṇāya gacchati pāpuṇātīti migo, atha vā magayamāno ihati pavattatīti migo, migānaṃ māraṇe luddo lobhī gedhoti migaluddo, pure mayhaṃ puññakaraṇasamaye kānanasaṅkhāte mahāaraññe migaluddo āsinti sambandho. Pāṭaliṃ haritaṃ disvāti tattha pakārena talena rattavaṇṇena bhavatīti pāṭali[V 2.0110], pupphānaṃ [P 0.0410] rattavaṇṇatāya pāṭalīti vohāro, pattānaṃ haritatāya haritaṃ nīlavaṇṇaṃ pāṭalibodhiṃ disvāti attho. Sesaṃ sabbattha uttānatthamevāti.

31. Having thus reached attainment, he recalled his past deeds and, filled with joy, revealed his former conduct by declaring his Apadāna, beginning, 'In the past, I was a deer hunter...'. Herein, migo (deer) is so called because 'it goes to death' (maraṇāya gacchati), or alternatively, because 'it moves about while being sought' (magayamāno ihati). A migaluddo (deer hunter) is one who is cruel, greedy, and covetous in the killing of deer. The connection is: 'In the past, during my time of making merit, I was a deer hunter in the great forest known as Kānana.' Regarding 'having seen the green Pāṭali': Pāṭali is so called because it is red in color by nature, or because of the red color of its flowers. 'Green' (harita) refers to the greenness of its leaves; thus, the meaning is 'having seen the green-leafed, blue-hued Pāṭali Bodhi tree'. The rest has a plain meaning everywhere.

Tipupphiyattheraapadānavaṇṇanā samattā.

The Commentary on the Apadāna of the Elder Tipupphiya is concluded.

7. Madhupiṇḍikattheraapadānavaṇṇanā

7. The Commentary on the Apadāna of the Elder Madhupiṇḍika.

Vivane kānane disvātiādikaṃ āyasmato madhupiṇḍikattherassa apadānaṃ. Ayampi purimabuddhesu katādhikāro tattha tattha bhave vivaṭṭūpanissayāni puññāni upacinanto siddhatthassa bhagavato kāle nesādayoniyaṃ nibbatto mahāaraññe paṭivasati. Tadā vivekābhiratiyā sampattaṃ siddhatthaṃ bhagavantaṃ disvā samādhito vuṭṭhitassa tassa sumadhuraṃ madhumadāsi. Tattha ca pasannamānaso vanditvā pakkāmi. So teneva puññena sampattiṃ anubhavanto devamanussesu saṃsaritvā imasmiṃ buddhuppāde kulagehe nibbatto vuddhippatto satthari pasīditvā pabbajito nacirasseva arahā ahosi.

The Apadāna of the Venerable Elder Madhupiṇḍika begins with the words, “Having seen in the wilderness, in the forest…” He too, having made his aspiration under previous Buddhas, accumulated merits in various existences that were a basis for liberation. During the time of the Blessed One Siddhattha, he was reborn into a hunter’s lineage and lived in a great forest. At that time, he saw the Blessed One Siddhattha, who delighted in seclusion, arrive. To the Blessed One, who had arisen from concentration, he offered very sweet honey. With a pleased mind, he paid homage and departed. By that very merit, experiencing prosperity, he wandered among devas and humans, and at the time of this Buddha’s arising, was reborn in a good family. Having come of age, he gained faith in the Teacher, went forth, and before long became an arahant.

37. So aparabhāge attano pubbakammaṃ saritvā somanassajāto pubbacaritāpadānaṃ pakāsento vivane kānane disvātiādimāha. Tattha vivaneti visesena vanaṃ patthaṭaṃ vivanaṃ, hatthiassarathasaddehi bherisaddehi ca vatthukāmakilesakāmehi ca vigataṃ byāpagatanti attho, kānanasaṅkhāte mahāaraññe vivaneti sambandho. Osadhiṃva virocantanti bhavavaḍḍhakijanānaṃ icchiticchitaṃ nipphādetīti osadhaṃ. Ojānibbattikāraṇaṃ paṭicca yāya tārakāya uggatāya uddharanti gaṇhantīti sā osadhi. Osadhitārakā [M 2.0119] iva virocantīti vattabbe gāthābandhasukhatthaṃ “osadhiṃva virocanta”nti ca vuttaṃ. Sesaṃ sabbattha uttānamevāti.

37. Later, recalling his past deeds and becoming filled with joy, he revealed his former conduct, beginning with the words, “Having seen in the wilderness, in the forest…” Herein, vivana means a forest that is particularly expansive; the meaning is that it is free from the sounds of elephants, horses, chariots, and drums, and devoid of sensual desires for objects and sensual desires as defilements. The connection is to be made thus: in the vivana, that is, in the great wilderness known as kānana. Regarding “shining like a medicinal herb” (osadhiṃva virocanti): it is called osadha because it fulfills the various wishes of people who increase existence. It is called osadhi because, dependent on the cause for the production of vitality, it is gathered when that star has risen. Although it should be said, “shining like the medicinal-herb star,” for the sake of metrical ease it is said, “shining like a medicinal herb.” The rest is clear everywhere.

Madhupiṇḍikattheraapadānavaṇṇanā samattā.

The Commentary on the Apadāna of the Elder Madhupiṇḍika is concluded.

8. Senāsanadāyakattheraapadānavaṇṇanā

8. The Commentary on the Apadāna of the Elder Senāsanadāyaka.

Siddhatthassa bhagavatotiādikaṃ āyasmato senāsanadāyakattherassa apadānaṃ. Ayampi purimabuddhesu katādhikāro tattha tattha bhave vivaṭṭūpanissayāni puññāni upacinanto siddhatthassa bhagavato [V 2.0111] kāle kulagehe nibbatto vuddhippatto satthari pasīditvā attano vasanaṭṭhānaṃ vanantaraṃ sampattassa bhagavato paṇāmaṃ katvā paṇṇasantharaṃ santharitvā adāsi. Bhagavato nisinnaṭṭhānassa samantato bhittiparicchedaṃ katvā pupphapūjamakāsi. So tena puññena [P 0.0411] devamanussesu saṃsaranto ubhayasampattiyo anubhavitvā imasmiṃ buddhuppāde kulagehe nibbatto vuddhippatto satthari pasīditvā pabbajito nacirasseva arahā ahosi.

The Apadāna of the Venerable Elder Senāsanadāyaka begins with the words, “Of the Blessed One Siddhattha…” He too, having made his aspiration under previous Buddhas, accumulated merits in various existences that were a basis for liberation. During the time of the Blessed One Siddhattha, he was reborn in a good family. Having come of age, he gained faith in the Teacher. When the Blessed One arrived in the forest near his dwelling place, he paid homage, and having spread out a layer of leaves, gave it as an offering. He made a wall-enclosure all around the Blessed One’s seating place and made an offering of flowers. By that merit, wandering among devas and humans and experiencing both kinds of success, at the time of this Buddha’s arising, he was reborn in a good family. Having come of age, he gained faith in the Teacher, went forth, and before long became an arahant.

45. So aparabhāge attano pubbakammaṃ saritvā somanassajāto attano pubbacaritāpadānaṃ dassento siddhatthassa bhagavatotiādimāha. Taṃ sabbaṃ heṭṭhā vuttanayattā uttānatthamevāti.

45. Later, recalling his past deeds and becoming filled with joy, he revealed his former conduct, beginning with the words, “Of the Blessed One Siddhattha…” All of that has a clear meaning, following the method stated previously.

Senāsanadāyakattheraapadānavaṇṇanā samattā.

The Commentary on the Apadāna of the Elder Senāsanadāyaka is concluded.

9. Veyyāvaccakarattheraapadānavaṇṇanā

9. The Commentary on the Apadāna of the Elder Veyyāvaccakara.

Vipassissa bhagavatotiādikaṃ āyasmato veyyāvaccakarattherassa apadānaṃ. Tassa uppattiādayo heṭṭhā vuttaniyāmeneva daṭṭhabbā.

The Apadāna of the Venerable Elder Veyyāvaccakara begins with the words, “Of the Blessed One Vipassī…” His birth and other details should be understood according to the principle stated previously.

Veyyāvaccakarattheraapadānavaṇṇanā samattā.

The Commentary on the Apadāna of the Elder Veyyāvaccakara is concluded.

10. Buddhupaṭṭhākattheraapadānavaṇṇanā

10. The Commentary on the Apadāna of the Elder Buddhupaṭṭhāka.

Vipassissa [M 2.0120] bhagavatotiādikaṃ āyasmato buddhupaṭṭhākattherassa apadānaṃ. Ayampi purimabuddhesu katādhikāro tattha tattha bhave vivaṭṭūpanissayāni puññāni upacinanto vipassissa bhagavato kāle saṅkhadhamakakule nibbatto vuddhimanvāya attano sippe saṅkhadhamane cheko ahosi, niccakālaṃ bhagavato saṅkhaṃ dhametvā saṅkhasaddeneva pūjesi. So tena puññena devamanussesu saṃsaranto sabbattha pākaṭo mahāghoso mahānādī madhurassaro ahosi, imasmiṃ buddhuppāde ekasmiṃ pākaṭakule nibbatto vuddhippatto madhurassaroti pākaṭo, satthari pasīditvā pabbajito nacirasseva arahā ahosi, aparabhāge madhurassarattheroti pākaṭo.

The Apadāna of the Venerable Elder Buddhupaṭṭhāka begins with the words, “Of the Blessed One Vipassī…” He too, having made his aspiration under previous Buddhas, accumulated merits in various existences that were a basis for liberation. During the time of the Blessed One Vipassī, he was reborn in a family of conch-blowers. Having come of age, he became skilled in his craft of conch-blowing, and constantly blew the conch for the Blessed One, thus venerating him with the sound of the conch alone. By that merit, wandering among devas and humans, he was everywhere renowned as one with a great voice, a mighty sound, and a sweet tone. At the time of this Buddha’s arising, he was reborn in a well-known family. Having come of age, he became known as “Sweet-Voiced.” Having gained faith in the Teacher, he went forth, and before long became an arahant. Later, he was known as the Elder Madhurassara (Sweet-Voiced).

51. So [V 2.0112] ekadivasaṃ attano pubbakammaṃ saritvā somanassajāto pubbacaritāpadānaṃ pakāsento vipassissa bhagavatotiādimāha. Taṃ heṭṭhā vuttameva. Ahosiṃ saṅkhadhamakoti saṃ suṭṭhu khananto gacchatīti saṅkho, samuddajalapariyante caramāno gacchati vicaratīti attho. Taṃ saṅkhaṃ dhamati ghosaṃ karotīti saṅkhadhamako, sohaṃ saṅkhadhamakova ahosinti attho. Sesaṃ sabbattha uttānamevāti.

51. One day, recalling his past deeds and becoming filled with joy, he revealed his former conduct, beginning with the words, “Of the Blessed One Vipassī…” That has been stated previously. Regarding “I was a conch-blower” (Ahosiṃ saṅkhadhamako): a saṅkha is so-called because it goes along digging well (saṃ suṭṭhu khananto gacchati); the meaning is that it travels and wanders at the edge of the ocean. One who blows (dhamati) that conch (saṅkha), making a sound (ghosaṃ), is a conch-blower (saṅkhadhamako). Thus, the meaning is: “I was indeed a conch-blower.” The rest is clear everywhere.

Buddhupaṭṭhākattheraapadānavaṇṇanā samattā.

The Commentary on the Apadāna of the Elder Buddhupaṭṭhāka is concluded.

Dasamavaggavaṇṇanā samattā.

The Commentary on the Tenth Chapter is concluded.

11. Bhikkhadāyivaggo

11. The Chapter of the Givers of Alms-food

1. Bhikkhādāyakattheraapadānavaṇṇanā

1. The Commentary on the Apadāna of the Elder Bhikkhādāyaka

Suvaṇṇavaṇṇaṃ [P 0.0412][V 2.0113] sambuddhantiādikaṃ āyasmato bhikkhādāyakattherassa apadānaṃ. Ayampi purimajinavaresu katādhikāro tattha tattha bhave vivaṭṭūpanissayāni puññāni upacinanto siddhatthassa bhagavato kāle ekasmiṃ kulagehe nibbatto vuddhimanvāya vibhavasampanno saddhājāto vihārato nikkhamitvā piṇḍāya caramānaṃ siddhatthaṃ bhagavantaṃ disvā pasannamānaso āhāramadāsi. Bhagavā taṃ paṭiggahetvā anumodanaṃ vatvā [M 2.0121] pakkāmi. So teneva kusalena yāvatāyukaṃ ṭhatvā āyupariyosāne devaloke nibbatto tattha cha kāmāvacarasampattiyo anubhavitvā manussesu ca manussasampattimanubhavitvā imasmiṃ buddhuppāde kulagehe nibbatto vuddhimanvāya saddhājāto pabbajitvā nacirasseva arahā ahosi.

"Golden-hued, the Fully Enlightened One," and so forth—this is the Apadāna of the Venerable Elder Bhikkhādāyaka. He too, having performed meritorious deeds under previous Conquerors and accumulating wholesome actions conducive to liberation in various existences, was born in a certain family in the time of the Blessed One Siddhattha. Having come of age and become wealthy, with faith arisen, he saw the Blessed One Siddhattha wandering for alms after coming forth from the monastery. With a confident mind, he gave food. The Blessed One, accepting it, gave a blessing and departed. Through that very wholesome deed, having lived for the extent of his lifespan, at the end of his life, he was reborn in the deva world. There, he experienced the prosperities of the six sense-sphere heavens. And among humans, he experienced human prosperity. In this Buddha's dispensation, he was reborn in a family, came of age, developed faith, went forth, and not long after, became an arahant.

1. So aparabhāge attano pubbakammaṃ anussaritvā somanassajāto pubbacaritāpadānaṃ pakāsento suvaṇṇavaṇṇaṃ sambuddhantiādimāha. Taṃ sabbaṃ heṭṭhā vuttanayameva. Pavarā abhinikkhantanti pakārena varitabbaṃ patthetabbanti pavaraṃ, rammabhūtato vivekabhūtato sakavihārato abhi visesena nikkhantanti attho. Vānā nibbānamāgatanti vānaṃ vuccati taṇhā, tato nikkhantattā nibbānaṃ, vānanāmaṃ taṇhaṃ padhānaṃ katvā sabbakilese pahāya nibbānaṃ pattanti attho.

1. Later, recalling his past deeds and filled with joy, he revealed his former virtuous conduct, declaring, “Golden-hued, the Fully Enlightened One,” and so forth. All of this is in accordance with the method stated earlier. “The excellent one had gone forth”—‘pavara’ means that which should be chosen and wished for; the meaning is: “Having gone forth with special distinction from his own dwelling, which was delightful and secluded.” “Having come to Nibbāna from Vāna”—‘vāna’ is called craving. Nibbāna is so called because of having gone forth from that. The meaning is: having striven against the craving called vāna, and having abandoned all defilements, he attained Nibbāna.

2. Kaṭacchubhikkhaṃ datvānāti karatalena gahetabbā dabbi kaṭacchu, bhikkhīyati āyācīyatīti bhikkhā, abhi visesena khāditabbā bhakkhitabbāti vā bhikkhā, kaṭacchunā gahetabbā bhikkhā kaṭacchubhikkhā, dabbiyā bhattaṃ datvāti attho. Sesaṃ sabbattha uttānatthamevāti.

2. "Having given alms with a ladle"—'Kaṭacchu' means a ladle to be held in the palm of the hand. 'Bhikkhā' means what is begged or requested, or what should be especially eaten or consumed. 'Kaṭacchubhikkhā' means alms taken with a ladle; the meaning is: "Having given food with a ladle." The rest is clear in meaning throughout.

Bhikkhādāyakattheraapadānavaṇṇanā samattā.

The Commentary on the Apadāna of the Elder Bhikkhādāyaka is concluded.

2. Ñāṇasaññikattheraapadānavaṇṇanā

2. The Commentary on the Apadāna of the Elder Ñāṇasaññika

Suvaṇṇavaṇṇaṃ [V 2.0114] sambuddhantiādikaṃ āyasmato ñāṇasaññikattherassa apadānaṃ. Kā uppatti? Ayampi purimabuddhesu katādhikāro tattha tattha bhave vivaṭṭūpanissayāni puññāni upacinanto siddhatthassa bhagavato kāle kulagehe nibbatto vuddhimanvāya saddhājāto saddhammassavane sādaro sālayo bhagavato dhammadesanānusārena ñāṇaṃ pesetvā ghosapamāṇattā bhagavato ñāṇe pasanno pañcaṅgaaṭṭhaṅganamakkāravasena paṇāmaṃ katvā pakkāmi. So tato cuto devalokesu uppanno tattha cha kāmāvacare dibbasampattimanubhavanto tato cavitvā manussaloke jāto tatthaggabhūtā cakkavattisampadādayo [P 0.0413] anubhavitvā imasmiṃ [M 2.0122] buddhuppāde vibhavasampanne ekasmiṃ kulagehe nibbatto vuddhimanvāya satthari pasīditvā pabbajito nacirasseva arahā ahosi.

The Apadāna of the Venerable Ñāṇasaññika Thera, beginning with "Golden-hued, the Fully Enlightened One..." What is his origin? This one too, having performed meritorious deeds in the presence of previous Buddhas, accumulated virtues here and there as a foundation for liberation in various existences. In the time of the Blessed One Siddhattha, he was born into a respectable family. Growing up, he developed faith and, being eager and devoted to listening to the true Dhamma, according to the Blessed One’s teaching, he directed his wisdom. Being pleased with the Buddha's knowledge because of its renowned extent, he paid homage with prostrations of five and eight points of contact before departing. Passing away from there, he was reborn in the heavenly realms, where he experienced divine pleasures in the six sense-sphere heavens. Then, passing away from there, he was born in the human world, experiencing pre-eminent fortunes such as the wealth of a wheel-turning monarch. In the dispensation of this Buddha, he was born into a prosperous family. Growing up, he gained confidence in the Teacher, went forth, and before long became an arahant.

7. So aparabhāge attano pubbakammaṃ saritvā somanassajāto pubbacaritāpadānaṃ pakāsento suvaṇṇavaṇṇaṃ sambuddhantiādimāha. Taṃ vuttatthameva. Nisabhājāniyaṃ yathāti gavasatasahassajeṭṭho nisabho, nisabho ca so ājāniyo seṭṭho uttamo ceti nisabhājāniyo. Yathā nisabhājāniyo, tatheva bhagavāti attho. Lokavisayasaññātaṃ paññattivasena evaṃ vuttaṃ. Anupameyyo hi bhagavā. Sesaṃ sabbattha uttānatthamevāti.

7. Then, in later times, recalling his own past deeds and filled with joy, he revealed the story of his former virtuous conduct, saying, "Golden-hued, the Fully Enlightened One," and so on. That meaning is as stated. "Like the noble thoroughbred bull" — a nisabha bull is the foremost among a hundred thousand cows, and that nisabha bull is a thoroughbred, the best and supreme; just as a nisabha thoroughbred, so too is the Blessed One. This is the meaning. This is said by way of conventional designation, being known in the realm of the world. Indeed, the Blessed One is incomparable. The rest is clear in meaning throughout.

Ñāṇasaññikattheraapadānavaṇṇanā samattā.

The Commentary on the Apadāna of the Elder Ñāṇasaññika is concluded.

3. Uppalahatthiyattheraapadānavaṇṇanā

3. The Commentary on the Apadāna of the Elder Uppalahatthaka

Tivarāyaṃ nivāsīhantiādikaṃ āyasmato uppalahatthakattherassa apadānaṃ. Ayampi purimajinavaresu katakusalo tattha tattha bhave vivaṭṭūpanissayāni puññāni upacinanto siddhatthassa bhagavato kāle mālākārakule nibbatto vuddhimanvāya mālākārakammena anekāni pupphāni vikkiṇanto jīvati. Athekadivasaṃ pupphāni gahetvā caranto bhagavantaṃ ratanagghikamiva caramānaṃ disvā rattuppalakalāpena pūjesi. So tato cuto teneva puññena sugatīsu puññamanubhavitvā imasmiṃ buddhuppāde kulagehe nibbatto vuddhimanvāya saddhājāto pabbajitvā nacirasseva arahā ahosi.

This is the Apadāna of the Venerable Uppalahatthaka Thera, beginning with "Dwelling in Tivarā..." He too, having performed wholesome deeds under previous foremost Conquerors, accumulating merits as the foundation for liberation in various existences, during the time of the Blessed One Siddhattha, was reborn in a family of garland-makers. Having come of age, he made a living by selling many flowers through the garland-making profession. Then one day, while carrying flowers, he saw the Blessed One walking like a priceless gem and offered him a cluster of red lotuses. After passing away from that life, he enjoyed the fruits of that merit in fortunate realms. In this Buddha's dispensation, he was reborn in a family, came of age, developed faith, went forth, and not long after, became an arahant.

13. So [V 2.0115] aparabhāge attano pubbakammaṃ saritvā somanassajāto pubbacaritāpadānaṃ pakāsento tivarāyaṃ nivāsīhantiādimāha. Tattha tivarāti tīhi vārehi kāritaṃ sañcaritaṃ paṭicchannaṃ nagaraṃ, tassaṃ tivarāyaṃ nivāsī, vasanasīlo nivāsanaṭṭhānagehe vā vasanto ahanti attho. Ahosiṃ māliko tadāti tadā nibbānatthāya puññasambhārakaraṇasamaye māliko mālākārova pupphāni kayavikkayaṃ katvā jīvanto ahosinti attho.

13. Then, in later times, recollecting his past deeds and filled with joy, he revealed the story of his former virtuous conduct, saying, "Dwelling in Tivarā..." Herein, 'Tivarā' means a city constructed with three circuits, traversed, and concealed. The meaning is: "I was a dweller in that Tivarā," that is, he was accustomed to living there, or living in a dwelling place. "I was a florist at that time" means that at that time, during the period of accumulating merit for the sake of Nibbāna, he lived as a florist, making and selling flowers.

14. Pupphahatthamadāsahanti [M 2.0123] siddhatthaṃ bhagavantaṃ disvā uppalakalāpaṃ adāsiṃ pūjesinti attho. Sesaṃ sabbattha uttānatthamevāti.

14. "I offered a handful of flowers"—meaning, seeing the Blessed One Siddhattha, he offered a cluster of lotuses as worship. The rest is clear in meaning throughout.

Uppalahatthakattheraapadānavaṇṇanā samattā.

The Commentary on the Apadāna of the Elder Uppalahatthaka is concluded.

4. Padapūjakattheraapadānavaṇṇanā

4. Commentary on the Apadāna of the Elder Padapūjaka

Siddhatthassa [P 0.0414] bhagavatotiādikaṃ āyasmato padapūjakattherassa apadānaṃ. Ayampi purimabuddhesu katādhikāro siddhatthassa bhagavato kāle kulagehe nibbatto vuddhimanvāya satthari pasanno sumanapupphena pādamūle pūjesi. So tena puññena devamanussesu saṃsaranto sakkasampattiṃ anubhavitvā imasmiṃ buddhuppāde ekasmiṃ kulagehe nibbatto vuddhimanvāya satthari pasīditvā pabbajito vipassanaṃ vaḍḍhetvā arahattaphale patiṭṭhāsi.

The Apadāna of the Venerable Elder Padapūjaka begins with 'Siddhatthassa bhagavato.' This one, too, having made his aspiration under former Buddhas, was reborn in a family in the time of the Blessed One Siddhattha. Having grown up, he became pleased with the Teacher and worshipped at his feet with sumana flowers. By that merit, wandering on among devas and humans, he experienced the prosperity of Sakka. In this Buddha-dispensation, he was reborn in a family; having grown up and gained faith in the Teacher, he went forth, developed insight, and became established in the fruit of arahantship.

19. So aparabhāge attano pubbakammaṃ saritvā somanassajāto pubbacaritāpadānaṃ pakāsento siddhatthassa bhagavatotiādimāha. Jātipupphamadāsahanti jātisumanapupphaṃ adāsiṃ ahanti vattabbe gāthābandhasukhatthaṃ sumanasaddassa lopaṃ katvā vuttaṃ. Tattha jātiyā nibbatto vikasamānoyeva sumanaṃ janānaṃ somanassaṃ karotīti sumanaṃ, pupphanaṭṭhena vikasanaṭṭhena pupphaṃ, sumanañca taṃ pupphañcāti sumanapupphaṃ, tāni sumanapupphāni siddhatthassa bhagavato ahaṃ pūjesinti attho. Sesaṃ sabbattha uttānamevāti.

19. Later, recollecting his past deeds and filled with joy, he declared his former conduct, beginning with 'Siddhatthassa bhagavato.' The phrase 'Jātipupphamadāsahaṃ' (I offered a jāti flower) is stated by omitting the word 'sumana' for the sake of metrical ease, though it should be 'jātisumanapupphaṃ adāsiṃ ahaṃ' (I offered a jāti-sumana flower). Herein, 'jāti' refers to its species. It is called 'sumana' because as it blossoms it brings joy to the minds of people. 'Puppha' means 'flower' in the sense of blooming or blossoming; and 'sumanapuppha' is a 'sumana' and also a 'flower.' The meaning is: 'I worshipped the Blessed One Siddhattha with those sumana flowers.' The rest is clear throughout.

Padapūjakattheraapadānavaṇṇanā samattā.

The commentary on the Apadāna of the Elder Padapūjaka is concluded.

5. Muṭṭhipupphiyattheraapadānavaṇṇanā

5. Commentary on the Apadāna of the Elder Muṭṭhipupphiya

Sudassano [V 2.0116] nāma nāmenātiādikaṃ āyasmato muṭṭhipupphiyattherassa apadānaṃ. Ayampi purimabuddhesu katādhikāro tattha tattha bhave vivaṭṭūpanissayāni puññāni upacinanto padumuttarassa bhagavato kāle mālākārakule nibbatto vuddhimanvāya sakasippe nipphattiṃ patto ekadivasaṃ [M 2.0124] bhagavantaṃ disvā pasannamānaso jātisumanapupphāni ubhohi hatthehi bhagavato pādamūle okiritvā pūjesi. So tena kusalasambhārena devamanussesu saṃsaranto ubho sampattiyo anubhavitvā imasmiṃ buddhuppāde kulagehe nibbatto vuddhippatto pubbavāsanāvasena satthari pasīditvā pabbajito nacirasseva arahā ahosi.

The Apadāna of the Venerable Elder Muṭṭhipupphiya begins with 'Sudassano nāma nāmenāti.' This one too, having made his aspiration under former Buddhas, accumulating merits that are the basis for turning away from existence in various lives, was reborn in a garland-maker's family in the time of the Blessed One Padumuttara. Having grown up and attained proficiency in his own craft, one day, having seen the Blessed One, with a serene mind, he scattered jāti-sumana flowers with both hands at the feet of the Blessed One and worshipped him. By that accumulation of wholesome deeds, wandering on among devas and humans, experiencing both kinds of prosperity, in this Buddha-dispensation, he was reborn in a family; having attained maturity, due to the power of former inclinations, having gained faith in the Teacher, he went forth and soon became an Arahant.

14-25. So aparabhāge attano pubbakammaṃ anussaritvā somanassajāto pubbacaritāpadānaṃ pakāsento sudassano nāma nāmenātiādimāha. Tattha sudassanoti ārohapariṇāharūpasaṇṭhānayobbaññasobhanena sundaro dassanoti sudassano, nāmena sudassano nāma mālākāro hutvā jātisumanapupphehi padumuttaraṃ bhagavantaṃ pūjesinti attho. Sesaṃ sabbattha uttānamevāti.

14-25. Later, recollecting his former deeds, filled with joy, he declared his former conduct, beginning with 'Sudassano nāma nāmenāti.' Here, 'Sudassano' means 'beautiful to see' because of the beauty of his stature, proportions, bodily form, and youthfulness. The meaning is: 'Being a garland-maker named Sudassano, I worshipped the Blessed One Padumuttara with jāti-sumana flowers.' The rest is clear throughout.

Muṭṭhipupphiyattheraapadānavaṇṇanā samattā.

The commentary on the Apadāna of the Elder Muṭṭhipupphiya is concluded.

6. Udakapūjakattheraapadānavaṇṇanā

6. Commentary on the Apadāna of the Elder Udakapūjaka

Suvaṇṇavaṇṇaṃ [P 0.0415] sambuddhantiādikaṃ āyasmato udakapūjakattherassa apadānaṃ. Ayampi purimajinavaresu pūritakusalasañcayo tattha tattha bhave vivaṭṭūpanissayāni puññāni paripūriyamāno pudumuttarassa bhagavato kāle ekasmiṃ kulagehe nibbatto vuddhimanvāya kusalākusalaṃ jānanto padumuttarassa bhagavato ākāse gacchato nikkhantachabbaṇṇabuddharaṃsīsu pasanno ubhohi hatthehi udakaṃ gahetvā pūjesi. Tena pūjitaṃ udakaṃ rajatabubbulaṃ viya ākāse aṭṭhāsi. So abhippasanno teneva somanassena tusitādīsu nibbatto dibbasampattiyo anubhavitvā aparabhāge manussasampattiyo ca anubhavitvā imasmiṃ buddhuppāde kulagehe nibbatto viññutaṃ patto satthari pasīditvā pabbajito nacirasseva arahā ahosi.

The Apadāna of the Venerable Elder Udakapūjaka begins with 'Suvaṇṇavaṇṇaṃ sambuddhaṃ.' This one too, having fulfilled the accumulation of wholesome deeds in the presence of previous Conquerors, completing merits that are the basis for turning away from existence in various lives, was reborn in a certain family in the time of the Blessed One Padumuttara. Having grown up and knowing what is wholesome and unwholesome, having seen the Blessed One Padumuttara going through the sky, being pleased by the six-colored Buddha-rays emanating forth, he took water in both hands and worshipped with it. The water offered by him remained in the sky like silver bubbles. Greatly pleased, reborn by that same joy in Tusita and other realms, he experienced divine prosperity; and later, having experienced human prosperity as well, in this Buddha-dispensation, he was reborn in a family; having attained understanding, having gained faith in the Teacher, he went forth and soon became an Arahant.

29. So [V 2.0117] aparabhāge attano pubbakammaṃ saritvā somanassajāto pubbacaritāpadānaṃ pakāsento suvaṇṇavaṇṇaṃ sambuddhantiādimāha. Taṃ heṭṭhā vuttameva. Ghatāsanaṃva jalitanti ghataṃ vuccati sappi, ghatassa āsanaṃ ādhāranti ghatāsanaṃ, aggi, atha vā taṃ asati bhuñjatīti ghatāsanaṃ[M 2.0125], aggiyeva. Yathā ghate āsitte aggimhi aggisikhā atīva jalati, evaṃ aggikkhandhaṃ iva jalamānaṃ bhagavantanti attho. Ādittaṃva hutāsananti hutaṃ vuccati pūjāsakkāre, hutassa pūjāsakkārassa āsananti hutāsanaṃ, jalamānaṃ sūriyaṃ iva dvattiṃsamahāpurisalakkhaṇehi byāmappabhāmaṇḍalehi vijjotamānaṃ suvaṇṇavaṇṇaṃ sambuddhaṃ anilañjase ākāse gacchantaṃ addasanti sambandho. Sesaṃ sabbattha uttānamevāti.

29. Later, recollecting his past deeds, filled with joy, he declared his former conduct, beginning with 'Suvaṇṇavaṇṇaṃ sambuddhaṃ.' That has been stated previously. Regarding 'Ghatāsanaṃva jalitaṃ' (blazing like a fire): 'Ghata' means ghee; 'āsana' means 'seat' or 'basis' of ghee, hence 'ghatāsana' is fire. Alternatively, it is called 'ghatāsana' because it consumes what is put into it, meaning fire. The meaning is: 'Just as a flame blazes intensely when ghee is poured into the fire, so the Blessed One was blazing like a mass of fire.' Regarding 'Ādittaṃva hutāsanaṃ' (blazing like a sacrificial fire): 'Huta' means offerings and honors; 'hutāsana' means the seat of offerings and honors. The connection is: 'I saw the golden-colored Perfectly Enlightened One, shining with the thirty-two marks of a great man and a halo of a fathom's length, like the blazing sun, going through the sky.' The rest is clear throughout.

Udakapūjakattheraapadānavaṇṇanā samattā.

The commentary on the Apadāna of the Elder Udakapūjaka is concluded.

7. Naḷamāliyattheraapadānavaṇṇanā

7. The Commentary on the Apadāna of the Elder Naḷamāliya

Padumuttarabuddhassātiādikaṃ āyasmato naḷamāliyattherassa apadānaṃ. Esopi purimajinavaresu katādhikāro anekāsu jātīsu vivaṭṭūpanissayāni kusalakammāni upacinanto padumuttarassa bhagavato kāle kulagehe nibbatto vuddhimanvāya gharāvāsaṃ saṇṭhapetvā kāme ādīnavaṃ disvā gehaṃ pahāya tāpasapabbajjaṃ pabbajitvā himavante vasanto tatthāgataṃ bhagavantaṃ disvā pasanno vanditvā tiṇasantharaṃ santharitvā tattha nisinnassa bhagavato naḷamālehi bījaniṃ katvā bījetvā adāsi. Paṭiggahesi bhagavā tassānukampāya, anumodanañca akāsi. So tena puññena devamanussesu saṃsaranto uppannuppannabhave pariḷāhasantāpavivajjito kāyacittacetasikasukhappatto anekasukhamanubhavitvā [P 0.0416] imasmiṃ buddhuppāde ekasmiṃ kulagehe nibbatto vuddhimanvāya pubbavāsanābalena satthari pasanno pabbajitvā nacirasseva arahā ahosi.

The Apadāna of the Elder Naḷamāliya begins with [the words] 'Of the Buddha Padumuttara...' This elder, too, having performed meritorious deeds in the presence of previous supreme Buddhas, accumulated wholesome kamma conducive to liberation over many births. In the time of the Blessed One Padumuttara, he was born into a respectable family and, having grown up, established a household life. Seeing the danger in sensual pleasures, he abandoned the household life and went forth into the ascetic life. Dwelling in the Himalayas, he saw the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, who had arrived there, felt faith, paid homage, and spread a grass mat. Then, making a fan from reeds, he fanned the Blessed One seated there and offered it. The Blessed One accepted it out of compassion for him and expressed his appreciation. Through that merit, he wandered on among devas and humans, free from burning and torment in every existence he was reborn in, experiencing bodily, mental, and volitional happiness. Having experienced much happiness, he was reborn in this Buddha-dispensation into a respectable family. Having grown up, by the power of his past wholesome tendencies, he developed faith in the Teacher, went forth, and not long after became an arahant.

36. So aparabhāge attano pubbakammaṃ saritvā somanassajāto pubbacaritāpadānaṃ pakāsento padumuttarabuddhassātiādimāha. Taṃ heṭṭhā vuttameva.

36. Later, recollecting his past kamma and becoming joyful, he revealed the apadāna of his past conduct, speaking beginning with [the words] 'Of the Buddha Padumuttara...' That has been stated below.

37. Naḷamālaṃ gahetvānāti naḷati asāro nissāro hutvā veḷuvaṃsatopi tanuko sallahuko jātoti naḷo, naḷassa mālā [M 2.0126] pupphaṃ naḷamālaṃ, tena naḷamālena bījaniṃ kāresinti sambandho[V 2.0118]. Bījissati janissati vāto anenāti bījanī, taṃ bījaniṃ buddhassa upanāmesiṃ, paṭiggahesinti attho. Sesaṃ sabbattha uttānamevāti.

37. Regarding 'Naḷamālaṃ gahetvāna' (Having taken a reed-garland): `naḷa` is so called because it grows to be hollow, pithless, thinner, and lighter even than bamboo. A `naḷamāla` is a garland or flower of reeds. The connection is that a fan was made with that reed-garland. `Bījanī` is that by which wind is fanned or generated. The meaning is: 'I presented that fan to the Buddha, and he accepted it.' The rest is clear everywhere.

Naḷamāliyattheraapadānavaṇṇanā samattā.

The Commentary on the Apadāna of the Elder Naḷamāliya is concluded.

Sattamabhāṇavāravaṇṇanā samattā.

The Commentary on the Seventh Recitation Section is concluded.

8. Āsanupaṭṭhāhakattheraapadānavaṇṇanā

8. The Commentary on the Apadāna of the Elder Āsanupaṭṭhāhaka

Kānanaṃ vanamoggayhātiādikaṃ āyasmato āsanupaṭṭhāhakattherassa apadānaṃ. Ayampi purimabuddhesu katādhikāro tattha tattha bhave vivaṭṭūpanissayāni puññāni upacinanto atthadassissa bhagavato kāle kulagehe nibbatto gharāvāsaṃ vasanto tattha dosaṃ disvā gharāvāsaṃ pahāya tāpasapabbajjaṃ pabbajitvā himavante vasanto tattha sampattaṃ bhagavantaṃ disvā pasanno sīhāsanaṃ adāsi, tattha nisinnaṃ bhagavantaṃ mālākalāpaṃ gahetvā pūjetvā taṃ padakkhiṇaṃ katvā pakkāmi. So tena puññena devamanussesu saṃsaranto nibbattanibbattabhave uccakuliko vibhavasampanno ahosi. So kālantarena imasmiṃ buddhuppāde kulagehe nibbatto vuddhimanvāya satthari pasīditvā pabbajito nacirasseva arahā ahosi.

The Apadāna of the Elder Āsanupaṭṭhāhaka begins with [the words] 'Having entered the forest, the wilderness...' This one, too, having performed meritorious deeds in the presence of previous Buddhas, accumulated wholesome deeds conducive to liberation in various existences. In the time of the Blessed One Atthadassī, he was born into a respectable family. While living the household life, seeing the danger there, he abandoned the household life and went forth into the ascetic life. Dwelling in the Himalayas, he saw the Blessed One who had arrived there. Filled with faith, he offered a lion-throne. Having taken a garland, he honored the Blessed One seated upon it. Having circumambulated him, he departed. Through that merit, he wandered on among devas and humans, being of high birth and endowed with wealth in every existence he was reborn in. In time, in this Buddha-dispensation, he was born into a respectable family. Having grown up, having faith in the Teacher, he went forth and not long after became an arahant.

47. So arahā samāno attano pubbakammaṃ saritvā somanassajāto pubbacaritāpadānaṃ pakāsento kānanaṃ vanamoggayhātiādimāha. Taṃ sabbaṃ heṭṭhā vuttatthamevāti.

47. Being an Arahant, he recollected his past kamma and, becoming joyful, revealed the apadāna of his past conduct, speaking beginning with [the words] 'Having entered the forest, the wilderness...' All of that has the same meaning as stated below.

Āsanupaṭṭhāhakattheraapadānavaṇṇanā samattā.

The Commentary on the Apadāna of the Elder Āsanupaṭṭhāhaka is concluded.

9. Biḷālidāyakattheraapadānavaṇṇanā

9. The Commentary on the Apadāna of the Elder Biḷālidāyaka

Himavantassāvidūretiādikaṃ āyasmato biḷālidāyakattherassa apadānaṃ. Ayampi purimajinavaresu katādhikāro tattha tattha bhave vivaṭṭūpanissayāni puññāni upacinanto padumuttarassa bhagavato kāle kulagehe [M 2.0127] nibbatto viññutaṃ patto gharāvāsaṃ vasanto tatthādīnavaṃ [P 0.0417] disvā gharāvāsaṃ pahāya tāpasapabbajjaṃ pabbajitvā himavante vasanto atīva appicchasantuṭṭho āluvādīhi yāpento vasati. Tadā padumuttaro bhagavā tassa anukampāya taṃ himavantaṃ agamāsi[V 2.0119]. Taṃ disvā pasanno vanditvā biḷāliyo gahetvā patte okiri. Taṃ tathāgato tassānukampāya somanassuppādayanto paribhuñji. So tena kammena tato cuto devamanussesu ubhayasampattiyo anubhavitvā imasmiṃ buddhuppāde kulagehe nibbattitvā vuddhimanvāya satthari pasanno sāsane pabbajitvā nacirasseva arahā ahosi.

The Apadāna of the Elder Biḷālidāyaka begins with [the words] 'Not far from the Himalayas...' This one, too, having performed meritorious deeds in the presence of previous supreme Buddhas, accumulated wholesome deeds conducive to liberation in various existences. In the time of the Blessed One Padumuttara, he was born into a respectable family, and having attained understanding, while living the household life, seeing the danger there, he abandoned the household life and went forth into the ascetic life. Dwelling in the Himalayas, he lived being very content with little, sustaining himself on aluva roots and so forth. Then the Blessed One Padumuttara, out of compassion for him, went to that Himalayas. Seeing him, he felt faith, paid homage, and taking biḷāli fruits, he poured them into his bowl. The Tathāgata, out of compassion for him, partook of them, generating joy in him. By that kamma, having passed away from there, he experienced both kinds of prosperity among devas and humans. In this Buddha-dispensation, having been reborn into a respectable family, having grown up, having faith in the Teacher, he went forth in the Dispensation and not long after became an arahant.

53. So aparabhāge attano kusalakammaṃ saritvā somanassajāto pubbacaritāpadānaṃ pakāsento himavantassāvidūretiādimāha. Taṃ sabbaṃ heṭṭhā vuttanayattā uttānatthameva. Āluvakarambhādayo tesaṃ tesaṃ kandajātīnaṃ nāmānevāti.

53. Later, recollecting his own wholesome kamma, he became joyful and, revealing the apadāna of his past conduct, spoke beginning with [the words] 'Not far from the Himalayas...' All of that has a clear meaning, being stated below in the same manner. 'Āluvakarambha' and so forth are simply the names of various kinds of tubers.

Biḷālidāyakattheraapadānavaṇṇanā samattā.

The Commentary on the Apadāna of the Elder Biḷālidāyaka is concluded.

10. Reṇupūjakattheraapadānavaṇṇanā

10. The Commentary on the Apadāna of the Elder Reṇupūjaka

Suvaṇṇavaṇṇaṃ sambuddhantiādikaṃ āyasmato reṇupūjakattherassa apadānaṃ. Ayampi purimajinavaresu katādhikāro tattha tattha bhave vivaṭṭūpanissayāni puññāni upacinanto vipassissa bhagavato kāle kulagehe nibbatto vuddhimanvāya satthari pasanno viññutaṃ patto aggikkhandhaṃ viya vijjotamānaṃ bhagavantaṃ disvā pasannamānaso nāgapupphakesaraṃ gahetvā pūjesi. Atha bhagavā anumodanamakāsi.

The Apadāna of the Venerable Elder Reṇupūjaka begins with [the words] 'Suvaṇṇavaṇṇaṃ sambuddhaṃ.' This one too, having performed deeds of merit in the presence of previous supreme Conquerors, accumulating merits in various existences as a supporting condition for emancipation, was reborn in a family during the time of the Blessed One Vipassī. Having grown up, he developed faith in the Teacher and attained understanding. Seeing the Blessed One shining like a mass of fire, with a serene mind he took nāga flower filaments and offered them in worship. Then the Blessed One expressed his appreciation.

62-3. So tena puññena tato cuto devamanussesu saṃsaranto ubhayasampattiyo anubhavitvā uppannuppannabhave sabbattha pūjito imasmiṃ buddhuppāde kulagehe nibbatto viññutaṃ patto pubbavāsanābalena satthari pasanno sāsane pabbajito nacirasseva arahā hutvā dibbacakkhunā attano pubbakammaṃ disvā somanassajāto pubbacaritāpadānaṃ pakāsento suvaṇṇavaṇṇaṃ sambuddhantiādimāha. Taṃ heṭṭhā vuttatthameva. Sataraṃsiṃva bhāṇumanti satamattā satappamāṇā raṃsi pabhā yassa sūriyassa [M 2.0128] so sataraṃsi, gāthābandhasukhatthaṃ sataraṃsīti vuttaṃ, anekasatassa anekasatasahassaraṃsīti attho. Bhāṇu vuccati pabhā, bhāṇu pabhā yassa so bhāṇumā, bhāṇumasaṅkhātaṃ sūriyaṃ iva vipassiṃ bhagavantaṃ disvā sakesaraṃ nāgapupphaṃ gahetvā abhiropayiṃ pūjesinti attho. Sesaṃ uttānamevāti.

62-3. Through that merit, after passing away from there, he wandered among devas and humans, experiencing both kinds of prosperity, and in every existence wherein he arose, he was honored. In this Buddha-dispensation, he was reborn in a family, attained understanding, and through the power of his past habituations, developed faith in the Teacher. He went forth into the Dispensation and soon became an Arahant. With the divine eye, he saw his past deeds and, filled with joy, he declared his former life story in the Apadāna, beginning with 'Suvaṇṇavaṇṇaṃ sambuddhaṃ.' Its meaning is as stated below. 'Like the sun with a hundred rays' (Sataraṃsiṃva bhāṇumaṃ): The sun which has a hundred rays or has a hundred as its measure of rays is called 'hundred-rayed' (sataraṃsi). For the sake of metrical ease, it is said 'sataraṃsi,' meaning it has many hundreds and thousands of rays. 'Bhāṇu' is said to mean radiance; 'Bhāṇumā' is one who has radiance. The meaning is: 'Seeing the Blessed One Vipassī, who was like the sun called 'Bhāṇumā,' I took a nāga flower with its filaments and offered it up in worship.' The rest is self-evident.

Reṇupūjakattheraapadānavaṇṇanā samattā.

The Commentary on the Apadāna of the Elder Reṇupūjaka is concluded.

Ekādasamavaggavaṇṇanā samattā.

The Commentary on the Eleventh Chapter is concluded.

12. Mahāparivāravaggo

12. The Chapter on the Great Retinue

1. Mahāparivārakattheraapadānavaṇṇanā

1. The Commentary on the Apadāna of the Elder Mahāparivāraka

Vipassī [P 0.0418][V 2.0120] nāma bhagavātiādikaṃ āyasmato mahāparivārakattherassa apadānaṃ. Ayampi purimajinavaresu katādhikāro tattha tattha bhave vivaṭṭūpanissayāni puññāni upacinanto vipassissa bhagavato uppannasamaye yakkhayoniyaṃ nibbatto anekayakkhasatasahassaparivāro ekasmiṃ khuddakadīpe dibbasukhamanubhavanto viharati. Tasmiñca dīpe cetiyābhisobhito vihāro atthi, tattha bhagavā agamāsi. Atha so yakkhasenādhipati taṃ bhagavantaṃ tattha gatabhāvaṃ disvā dibbavatthāni gahetvā gantvā bhagavantaṃ vanditvā dibbavatthehi pūjesi, saparivāro saraṇamagamāsi. So tena puññakammena tato cuto devaloke nibbattitvā tattha cha kāmāvacarasukhamanubhavitvā tato cuto manussesu aggacakkavattiādisukhamanubhavitvā aparabhāge imasmiṃ buddhuppāde kulagehe nibbatto viññutaṃ patto satthari pasīditvā pabbajito nacirasseva arahā ahosi.

The Apadāna of the Venerable Elder Mahāparivāraka begins with 'Vipassī by name, the Blessed One.' He also, having performed meritorious deeds in the presence of previous Conquerors and having accumulated merits in various existences that serve as a supporting condition for liberation, was reborn in a yaksha existence at the time of the Blessed One Vipassī's arising. Surrounded by many hundreds of thousands of yakshas, he dwelt on a small island, experiencing divine happiness. On that island there was a monastery adorned with a cetiya, and the Blessed One went there. Then that commander of the yaksha army, seeing that the Blessed One had arrived, took divine garments, went to the Blessed One, paid homage, and honored him with the divine garments. Together with his retinue, he went for refuge. Through that meritorious kamma, after passing away from there, he was reborn in the deva world, where he experienced the happiness of the six sensual spheres. After passing away from there, he was reborn among humans, experiencing the happiness of a paramount wheel-turning monarch and so on. In a later period, during this Buddha-dispensation, he was born into a family home, attained understanding, and having gained faith in the Teacher, he went forth and not long after became an Arahant.

1-2. So aparabhāge attano pubbakammaṃ saritvā somanassajāto pubbacaritāpadānaṃ pakāsento vipassī nāma bhagavātiādimāha. Tattha visesaṃ paramatthaṃ nibbānaṃ passatīti vipassī, vividhe satipaṭṭhānādayo sattatiṃsabodhipakkhiyadhamme passatīti vā vipassī, vividhe [M 2.0129] anekappakāre bodhaneyyasatte visuṃ visuṃ passatīti vā vipassī, so vipassī bhagavā dīpacetiyaṃ dīpe pūjanīyaṭṭhānaṃ vihāramagamāsīti attho. Sesaṃ sabbattha uttānamevāti.

1-2. In a later period, recollecting his own past kamma, he became joyful and, declaring his former life story, spoke the Apadāna, beginning with 'Vipassī by name, the Blessed One.' Therein, 'Vipassī' is one who sees distinctly the ultimate reality, Nibbāna. Or, 'Vipassī' is one who sees in various ways the thirty-seven factors of awakening, such as the foundations of mindfulness. Or, 'Vipassī' is one who sees separately and distinctly beings capable of being awakened in many different ways. The meaning is that the Blessed One Vipassī went to the monastery, the Dīpa Cetiya, a place worthy of veneration on the island. The rest is self-evident everywhere.

Mahāparivārakattheraapadānavaṇṇanā samattā.

The Commentary on the Apadāna of the Elder Mahāparivāraka is concluded.

2. Sumaṅgalattheraapadānavaṇṇanā

2. The Commentary on the Apadāna of the Elder Sumaṅgala

Atthadassī jinavarotiādikaṃ āyasmato sumaṅgalattherassa apadānaṃ. Ayampi purimabuddhesu katādhikāro [V 2.0121] tattha tattha bhave vivaṭṭūpanissayāni puññāni upacinanto atthadassissa bhagavato kāle ekasmiṃ taḷākasamīpe rukkhadevatā hutvā nibbatti. Tasmiṃ samaye bhagavā vihārato nikkhamitvā nahāyitukāmo tassa taḷākassa tīraṃ gantvā tattha nhatvā ekacīvaro jalamāno brahmā viya sūriyo viya suvaṇṇabimbaṃ viya aṭṭhāsi. Atha so devaputto somanassajāto pañjaliko thomanamakāsi, attano dibbagītatūriyehi [P 0.0419] upahārañca akāsi. So tena puññakammena devamanussesu sampattiyo anubhavitvā aparabhāge imasmiṃ buddhuppāde kulagehe nibbatto viññutaṃ patto satthari pasīditvā pabbajitvā nacirasseva arahā ahosi.

The Apadāna of the Venerable Elder Sumaṅgala begins with 'Atthadassī, the Chief Conqueror.' He also, having performed meritorious deeds in the presence of previous Buddhas and having accumulated merits in various existences that serve as a supporting condition for liberation, was reborn as a tree deity near a pond at the time of the Blessed One Atthadassī. At that time, the Blessed One, having left the monastery and wishing to bathe, went to the shore of that pond. After bathing there, he stood with a single robe, glowing like Brahmā, like the sun, like a golden image. Then that son of the devas, becoming joyful, with hands joined in reverence, offered praise and made an offering with divine song and musical instruments. Through that meritorious kamma, he experienced prosperity among devas and humans. In a later period, during this Buddha-dispensation, he was born into a family home, attained understanding, and having gained faith in the Teacher, he went forth and not long after became an Arahant.

11. So pacchā pubbakammaṃ saritvā somanassajāto pubbacaritāpadānaṃ pakāsento atthadassī jinavarotiādimāha. Tattha paramatthaṃ nibbānaṃ dakkhati passatīti atthadassī, atha vā sabbasattānaṃ caturāriyasaccasaṅkhātaṃ atthapayojanaṃ dassanasīloti atthadassī, kilese ajini jināti jinissatīti jino. Varitabbo patthetabbo sabbasattehīti varo, atthadassī jino ca so varo cāti atthadassī jinavaro. Lokajeṭṭhoti lujjati palujjatīti loko, lokīyati passīyati buddhādīhi pārappattoti vā loko, loko ca loko ca loko cāti loko. Ekasesasamāsavasena “lokā”ti vattabbe “loko”ti vutto. Lokassa jeṭṭho lokajeṭṭho, so lokajeṭṭho narāsabhoti attho. Sesaṃ sabbattha uttānamevāti.

11. Afterwards, recollecting his past kamma and becoming joyful, he declared his former life story, speaking the Apadāna, beginning with 'Atthadassī, the Chief Conqueror.' Therein, 'Atthadassī' is one who sees or will see the ultimate reality, Nibbāna. Alternatively, 'Atthadassī' is one whose nature it is to show the goal and purpose for all beings, designated as the Four Noble Truths. 'Jina' is one who has conquered, conquers, or will conquer the defilements. 'Vara' is one who is to be chosen or aspired to by all beings. Thus, 'Atthadassī Jinavara' is 'Atthadassī' who is a 'Jina' and is 'Vara.' 'Lokajeṭṭha' (Foremost of the World): 'Loka' is so-called because it crumbles and disintegrates; or it is that which is seen and perceived by Buddhas and others who have reached the further shore. The world, and the world, and the world, is 'the worlds' (loko). By way of an ekaśeṣa compound, 'loko' is said when 'lokā' should be stated. The foremost of the world is 'Lokajeṭṭha.' The meaning is 'the Foremost of the World, the Bull Among Men.' The rest is self-evident everywhere.

Sumaṅgalattheraapadānavaṇṇanā samattā.

The Commentary on the Apadāna of the Elder Sumaṅgala is concluded.

3. Saraṇagamaniyattheraapadānavaṇṇanā

3. The Commentary on the Apadāna of the Elder Saraṇagamaniya

Ubhinnaṃ [M 2.0130] devarājūnantyādikaṃ āyasmato saraṇagamaniyattherassa apadānaṃ. Ayampi purimabuddhesu katādhikāro uppannuppannabhave vivaṭṭūpanissayāni puññāni upacinanto padumuttare bhagavati uppanne ayaṃ himavante devarājā hutvā nibbatti, tasmiṃ aparena yakkhadevaraññā saddhiṃ saṅgāmatthāya upaṭṭhite dve anekayakkhasahassaparivārā phalakāvudhādihatthā saṅgāmatthāya samupabyūḷhā ahesuṃ. Tadā padumuttaro bhagavā tesu sattesu kāruññaṃ uppādetvā ākāsena tattha gantvā saparivārānaṃ dvinnaṃ devarājūnaṃ dhammaṃ desesi. Tadā te sabbe phalakāvudhāni chaḍḍetvā bhagavantaṃ gāravabahumānena vanditvā saraṇamagamaṃsu. Tesaṃ ayaṃ paṭhamaṃ saraṇamagamāsi. So tena puññena [V 2.0122] devamanussesu saṃsaranto ubhayasampattiyo anubhavitvā imasmiṃ buddhuppāde kulagehe nibbatto vuddhimanvāya satthari pasanno pabbajitvā nacirasseva arahā ahosi.

The Apadāna of the Venerable Saraṇagamaniya, beginning with 'the two deva kings,' is as follows: He too, having performed meritorious deeds under previous Buddhas, accumulated merits in successive existences that served as a basis for liberation. When the Blessed One Padumuttara arose, he was reborn as a deva king in the Himalayas. At that time, when he and another yaksha deva king, each accompanied by many thousands of yaksha followers armed with shields and other weapons, were arrayed for battle, the Blessed One Padumuttara, generating compassion for those beings, went there through the air and taught the Dhamma to the two deva kings and their retinues. Then all of them discarded their shields and weapons, paid homage to the Blessed One with reverence and respect, and went for refuge. Among them, he was the first to go for refuge. By the merit of that deed, he wandered through the realms of devas and humans, experiencing both kinds of prosperity. In this Buddha’s dispensation, he was reborn into a good family, grew up, developed faith in the Teacher, went forth, and soon became an arahant.

20. So aparabhāge pubbakusalaṃ saritvā somanassajāto pubbacaritāpadānaṃ pakāsento ubhinnaṃ devarājūnantiādimāha. Tattha sucilomakharalomaāḷavakakumbhīrakuverādayo viya nāmagottena apākaṭā dve yakkharājāno aññāpadesena dassento “ubhinnaṃ devarājūna”ntiādimāha. Saṅgāmo samupaṭṭhitoti [P 0.0420] saṃ suṭṭhu gāmo kalahatthāya upagamananti saṅgāmo, so saṅgāmo saṃ suṭṭhu upaṭṭhito, ekaṭṭhāne upagantvā ṭhitoti attho. Ahosi samupabyūḷhoti saṃ suṭṭhu upasamīpe rāsibhūtoti attho.

20. Later, recollecting his past wholesome deeds, he became joyful and, revealing the Apadāna of his former conduct, he spoke beginning with 'the two deva kings.' Herein, indicating two yakkha kings who, like Suciloma, Kharaloma, Āḷavaka, Kumbhīra, and Kuvera, were not well-known by name and clan, he alluded to them with the words 'the two deva kings.' The phrase 'a battle was imminent' (saṅgāmo samupaṭṭhito) means that saṅgāma, a thorough coming together for the purpose of conflict, had arisen; that battle was well prepared, meaning they had come together and stood in one place. The phrase 'ahosi samupabyūḷho' means they had thoroughly assembled in close proximity, forming a mass.

21. Saṃvejesi mahājananti tesaṃ rāsibhūtānaṃ yakkhānaṃ ākāse nisinno bhagavā catusaccadhammadesanāya saṃ suṭṭhu vejesi, ādīnavadassanena gaṇhāpesi viññāpesi bodhesīti attho. Sesaṃ sabbattha uttānamevāti.

21. The phrase 'he stirred the multitude' (saṃvejesi mahājanaṃ) means the Blessed One, seated in the sky, thoroughly stirred the massed yakkhas with the teaching of the Four Noble Truths, meaning he made them grasp, understand, and awaken through the perception of danger. The rest is clear throughout.

Saraṇagamaniyattheraapadānavaṇṇanā samattā.

The commentary on the Apadāna of the Elder Saraṇagamaniya is concluded.

4. Ekāsaniyattheraapadānavaṇṇanā

4. Commentary on the Apadāna of the Elder Ekāsaniya

Varuṇo [M 2.0131] nāma nāmenātiādikaṃ āyasmato ekāsaniyattherassa apadānaṃ. Ayampi purimabuddhesu katādhikāro tattha tattha bhave vivaṭṭūpanissayāni puññāni upacinanto atthadassissa bhagavato kāle varuṇo nāma devarājā hutvā nibbatti. So bhagavantaṃ disvā pasannamānaso gandhamālādīhi gītavāditehi ca upaṭṭhayamāno saparivāro pūjesi. Tato aparabhāge bhagavati parinibbute tassa mahābodhirukkhaṃ buddhadassanaṃ viya sabbatūriyatāḷāvacarehi saparivāro upahāramakāsi. So tena puññena tato kālaṅkatvā nimmānaratidevaloke uppajji. Evaṃ devasampattimanubhavitvā manussesu ca manussabhūto cakkavattisampattiṃ anubhavitvā imasmiṃ buddhuppāde kulagehe nibbatto viññutaṃ patvā satthu sāsane pabbajitvā nacirasseva arahā ahosi.

The Apadāna of the Venerable Ekāsaniya, beginning with 'Varuṇa by name,' is as follows: He too, having performed meritorious deeds under previous Buddhas, accumulated merits in various existences that served as a basis for liberation. During the time of the Blessed One Atthadassī, he was reborn as a deva king named Varuṇa. Seeing the Blessed One, with his mind filled with faith, he honored him with perfumes, garlands, and music, along with his retinue, and venerated him. Later, after the Blessed One’s parinibbāna, he made offerings to his great Bodhi tree with all kinds of musical instruments and his retinue, as if seeing the Buddha himself. By that merit, after passing away from there, he was reborn in the Nimmānarati deva-world. Having experienced such divine prosperity, and the fortune of a universal monarch when born among humans, he was reborn in a good family during this Buddha’s dispensation.
