He had a companion named Candana. Both of them heard the Dhamma from the Teacher and, with confident minds, went forth. They guarded their virtue their entire lives and, being of perfectly pure virtue, they passed away and were reborn in a deva world, where they experienced divine bliss for one Buddha-interval. Of these two, this one was reborn in the Sākiyan clan during the present Buddha-dispensation; the other, Candana, became a devaputta and was reborn in the Tāvatiṃsa realm. Then, when the Blessed One—at the request of Kāḷudāyī, who inspired confidence in the Sākiyan clan—gave a discourse on the Vessantara Jātaka (Jā 2.22.1655ff.) to crush the pride of the Sākiyan kings, this one saw the psychic miracle of the lotus-rain. With a confident mind, he went forth. After hearing the discourse on the Bhaddekaratta Sutta as taught in the Majjhima Nikāya (MN 131), he went to dwell in the forest. Recollecting the instructions in the Bhaddekaratta Sutta (MN 131ff.), he directed his knowledge accordingly, brought the meditation subject to mind, and attained arahantship.

225. Arahattaṃ [M 2.0268] patvā attano pubbakammaṃ saritvā sañjātasomanasso pubbacaritāpadānaṃ pakāsento imamhi bhaddake kappetiādimāha. Tattha kappo tāva catubbidho – sārakappo, varakappo, maṇḍakappo, bhaddakappoti. Tesu yasmiṃ kappe eko buddho uppajjati, ayaṃ sārakappo nāma. Yasmiṃ dve vā tayo vā buddhā uppajjanti, ayaṃ varakappo nāma. Yasmiṃ cattāro buddhā uppajjanti, ayaṃ maṇḍakappo nāma. Yasmiṃ pañca buddhā uppajjanti, ayaṃ bhaddakappo nāma. Aññattha pana –

225. Having attained arahantship, he recollected his past kamma and, filled with joy, proclaimed the apadāna of his former conduct, beginning with the words: “In this fortunate eon….” Herein, an eon is fourfold: an essence-eon (sārakappa), an excellent-eon (varakappa), a quintessential-eon (maṇḍakappa), and a fortunate-eon (bhaddakappa). Among these, an eon in which one Buddha arises is called an essence-eon. An eon in which two or three Buddhas arise is called an excellent-eon. An eon in which four Buddhas arise is called a quintessential-eon. An eon in which five Buddhas arise is called a fortunate-eon. But elsewhere—

“Sārakappo [P 0.0542] maṇḍakappo, sāramaṇḍakappo tathā;

Varakappo bhaddakappo, kappā pañcavidhā siyuṃ.

“The essence-eon, the dregs-eon, and the essence-and-dregs-eon; the excellent-eon, the fortunate-eon—eons are of five kinds.

“Eko dve tayo cattāro, pañca buddhā yathākkamaṃ;

Etesu pañcakappesu, uppajjanti vināyakā”ti. –

“One, two, three, four, five Buddhas in due order; in these five eons, the Leaders arise.”

Evaṃ [V 2.0264] pañca kappā vuttā. Tesu ayaṃ kappo “kakusandho koṇāgamano kassapo gotamo metteyyo”ti pañcabuddhapaṭimaṇḍitattā bhaddakappo nāma jāto.

Thus, five eons have been mentioned. Among them, this eon has come to be called the Fortunate Eon because it is adorned with five Buddhas: Kakusandha, Koṇāgamana, Kassapa, Gotama, and Metteyya.

Tasmā imasmiṃ bhaddakappamhi kassapo nāyako uppajjīti sambandho. Sesaṃ uttānatthamevāti.

Therefore, the connection is: ‘In this Fortunate Eon the leader Kassapa arose.’ The rest has an obvious meaning.

Lomasakaṅgiyattheraapadānavaṇṇanā samattā.

The Commentary on the Apadāna of the Elder Lomasakaṅgiya is concluded.

9. Vanavacchattheraapadānavaṇṇanā

9. The Commentary on the Apadāna of the Elder Vanavaccha

Navamāpadāne imamhi bhaddake kappetiādikaṃ āyasmato vanavacchattherassa apadānaṃ. Ayampi purimabuddhesu katādhikāro tattha tattha bhave vivaṭṭūpanissayāni puññāni upacinanto kassapassa bhagavato kāle kulagehe nibbatto viññutaṃ patvā satthu dhammadesanaṃ sutvā saddhājāto pabbajitvā parisuddhaṃ brahmacariyaṃ caritvā tato cuto devaloke nibbatto, tato cuto araññāyatane bhikkhūnaṃ samīpe kapotayoniyaṃ nibbatto. Tesu mettacitto dhammaṃ sutvā tato cuto devamanussesu saṃsaranto imasmiṃ buddhuppāde kapilavatthusmiṃ brāhmaṇakule nibbatti. Tassa mātukucchigatakāleyeva mātu dohaḷo udapādi vane vasituṃ vane vijāyituṃ[M 2.0269]. Tato icchānurūpavasena vane vasantiyā gabbhavuṭṭhānaṃ ahosi. Gabbhato nikkhantañca naṃ kāsāvakhaṇḍena paṭiggahesuṃ. Tadā bodhisattassa uppannakālo, rājā taṃ kumāraṃ āharāpetvā saheva posesi. Atha bodhisatto mahābhinikkhamanaṃ nikkhamitvā pabbajitvā chabbasāni dukkarakārikaṃ katvā buddhe jāte so mahākassapassa santikaṃ gantvā tassovāde pasanno tassa santikā buddhuppādabhāvaṃ sutvā satthu santikaṃ gantvā dhammaṃ sutvā pabbajitvā nacirasseva chaḷabhiñño arahā ahosi.

In the ninth Apadāna, this is the Apadāna of the Venerable Vanavaccha, beginning with 'in this fortunate eon.' He too, having made an aspiration under previous Buddhas, accumulated merits in various existences that are a basis for liberation. During the time of the Blessed One Kassapa, he was born in a good family, and having reached maturity, he heard the Teacher’s Dhamma exposition. Inspired by faith, he went forth and lived the perfectly pure holy life. After passing away from there, he was reborn in a deva world. Passing away from there, he was reborn from a pigeon’s womb near some monks in a forest hermitage. With a mind of loving-kindness towards them, he listened to the Dhamma. After passing away from there, he wandered through the realms of devas and humans until, during this Buddha-era, he was born into a brahmin family in Kapilavatthu. While he was in his mother’s womb, a pregnancy-craving arose in her to dwell in the forest and to give birth in the forest. In accordance with her wish, while she was dwelling in the forest, her delivery from the womb occurred. When he emerged from the womb, they received him with a piece of saffron-colored cloth. At that time, the Bodhisatta had been born. The king had the boy brought and raised him together with the Bodhisatta. Then, after the Bodhisatta had gone forth in the great renunciation, practiced austerities for six years, and awakened as the Buddha, this one went to Mahākassapa. Pleased with his instruction, he heard from him about the Buddha’s appearance. He then went to the Teacher, listened to the Dhamma, went forth, and before long became an arahant endowed with the six higher knowledges.

251. So arahattaṃ patvā attano pubbakammaṃ saritvā somanassajāto pubbacaritāpadānaṃ pakāsento imamhi bhaddake kappetiādimāha. Tattha brahmabandhu mahāyasoti ettha brāhmaṇānaṃ bandhu ñātakoti brāhmaṇabandhūti vattabbe gāthābandhasukhatthaṃ “brahmabandhū”ti [P 0.0543] vuttanti veditabbaṃ. Lokattayabyāpakayasattā mahāyaso. Sesaṃ sabbaṃ suviññeyyamevāti.

251. Having attained arahantship, he recollected his own past deeds and, filled with joy, he declared his past life story, beginning with: 'In this fortunate eon…' Herein, regarding 'a kinsman of brahmins, of great fame': when it should have been said 'brāhmaṇabandhu,' meaning a kinsman or relative of brahmins, it should be understood that it was said as 'brahmabandhū' for the sake of metrical ease. 'Of great fame' means his fame pervaded the three worlds. The rest is all easily understood.

Vanavacchattheraapadānavaṇṇanā samattā.

The Commentary on the Apadāna of the Elder Vanavaccha is complete.

10. Cūḷasugandhattheraapadānavaṇṇanā

10. The Commentary on the Apadāna of the Elder Cūḷasugandha

Dasamāpadāne [V 2.0265] imamhi bhaddake kappetiādikaṃ āyasmato sugandhattherassa apadānaṃ. Ayampi purimabuddhesu katādhikāro tattha tattha bhave vivaṭṭūpanissayāni puññāni upacinanto kassapasammāsambuddhakāle bārāṇasiyaṃ vibhavasampanne kule nibbatto viññutaṃ patvā satthu santike dhammaṃ sutvā sabbadā namassamāno mahādānaṃ dadamāno māsassa sattakkhattuṃ bhagavato gandhakuṭiyā catujjātigandhena vilimpesi. “Mama nibbattanibbattaṭṭhāne sarīrato sugandhagandho nibbattatū”ti patthanaṃ akāsi. Bhagavā taṃ byākāsi. So yāvatāyukaṃ ṭhatvā puññāni karonto tato cuto devaloke nibbatto kāmāvacaralokaṃ sarīragandhena sugandhaṃ kurumāno sugandhadevaputtoti pākaṭo ahosi. So devalokasampattiyo anubhavitvā tato cuto imasmiṃ buddhuppāde mahābhogakule [M 2.0270] nibbatti, tassa mātukucchigatasseva mātuyā sarīragandhena sakalagehaṃ sakalanagarañca sugandhena ekagandhaṃ ahosi, jātakkhaṇe sakalaṃ sāvatthinagaraṃ sugandhakaraṇḍako viya ahosi, tenassa sugandhoti nāmaṃ kariṃsu. So vuddhiṃ agamāsi. Tadā satthā sāvatthiyaṃ patvā jetavanamahāvihāraṃ paṭiggahesi, taṃ disvā pasannamānaso bhagavato santike pabbajitvā nacirasseva saha paṭisambhidāhi arahattaṃ pāpuṇi. Tassa uppannadivasato paṭṭhāya yāva parinibbānā etthantare nipannaṭṭhānādīsu sugandhameva vāyi. Devāpi dibbacuṇṇadibbagandhapupphāni okiranti.

In the tenth Apadāna, this is the Apadāna of the Venerable Sugandha, beginning with 'in this fortunate eon.' He too, having made an aspiration under previous Buddhas, accumulated merits in various existences that are a basis for liberation. During the time of Kassapa the Perfectly Self-Enlightened One, he was born into a wealthy family in Bārāṇasī. Having reached maturity, he listened to the Dhamma in the Teacher's presence, always paying homage and giving great gifts. Seven times a month, he anointed the Blessed One's fragrant chamber with the four kinds of scents. He made the aspiration: 'May a fragrant scent arise from my body wherever I am reborn.' The Blessed One made a prediction about this for him. He lived out his lifespan performing meritorious deeds, and after passing away, was reborn in a deva world. Making the sense-sphere world fragrant with his bodily scent, he became known as the deva-son Sugandha. After enjoying the felicities of the deva world, he passed away and was reborn during this Buddha-era into a family of great wealth. From the moment he was conceived in his mother’s womb, the whole house and the whole city became uniformly fragrant with the scent from his mother's body. At the moment of his birth, the whole city of Sāvatthī became like a perfume casket, so they named him Sugandha. He grew up. At that time, the Teacher arrived in Sāvatthī and accepted the Jetavana Mahāvihāra. Seeing him, Sugandha, with a confident mind, went forth in the Blessed One's presence and before long attained arahantship together with the analytical knowledges. From the day of his birth until his final Nibbāna, a fragrant scent wafted from the places where he lay down and so on. The devas, too, scattered divine powders, divine perfumes, and divine flowers.

272. Sopi thero arahattaṃ patvā attano pubbakammaṃ saritvā somanassajāto pubbacaritāpadānaṃ pakāsento imamhi bhaddake kappetiādimāha. Taṃ sabbaṃ heṭṭhā vuttanayattā uttānatthattā ca suviññeyyameva, kevalaṃ puññanānattaṃ nāmanānattañca viseso.

272. That elder, too, having attained arahantship, recollected his own past deeds and, filled with joy, declared his past life story, beginning with: 'In this fortunate eon…' All of this is easily understood, as the method has been explained above and the meaning is plain. The only differences are the variety of the meritorious deeds and the variety of the names.

Cūḷasugandhattheraapadānavaṇṇanā samattā.

The Commentary on the Apadāna of the Elder Cūḷasugandha is complete.

Pañcapaññāsamavaggavaṇṇanā samattā.

The commentary on the Fifty-fifth Chapter is complete.

56. Yasavaggo

56. The Chapter on Yasa

1. Yasattheraapadānavaṇṇanā

1. The Commentary on the Apadāna of Venerable Yasa.

Chappaññāsame [P 0.0544][V 2.0266] vagge paṭhamāpadāne mahāsamuddaṃ oggayhātiādikaṃ āyasmato yasattherassa apadānaṃ. Ayampi purimabuddhesu katādhikāro tattha tattha bhave vivaṭṭūpanissayāni puññāni upacinanto sumedhassa bhagavato kāle mahānubhāvo nāgarājā hutvā buddhappamukhaṃ bhikkhusaṅghaṃ attano bhavanaṃ netvā mahādānaṃ pavattesi, bhagavantaṃ mahagghena ticīvarena acchādesi, ekekañca bhikkhuṃ mahaggheneva paccekadussayugena sabbena ca samaṇaparikkhārena. So tena puññakammena devamanussesu saṃsaranto siddhatthassa bhagavato kāle seṭṭhiputto hutvā mahābodhimaṇḍalaṃ sattahi ratanehi pūjesi. Kassapassa bhagavato kāle sāsane pabbajitvā samaṇadhammaṃ akāsi. Evaṃ so sugatīsuyeva saṃsaranto amhākaṃ bhagavato kāle bārāṇasiyaṃ mahāvibhavassa seṭṭhino putto [M 2.0271] hutvā sujātāya bhagavato khīrapāyāsaṃ dinnāya seṭṭhidhītāya kucchimhi nibbatti, yaso nāma nāmena paramasukhumālo. Tassa tayo pāsādā honti – eko hemantiko, eko gimhiko, eko vassikoti. So vassike pāsāde vassike cattāro māse nippurisehi tūriyehi paricārayamāno vasati, heṭṭhāpāsādaṃ na otarati. Hemantike pāsāde cattāro māse suphusitavātapānakavāṭe tattheva paṭivasati. Gimhike pāsāde bahukavāṭavātapānajālāhi sampanne tattheva vasati. Hatthapādānaṃ sukhumālatāya bhūmiyaṃ nisajjādikiccaṃ natthi. Simbalitulādipuṇṇasabhāve attharitvā tattha upadhānāni kiccāni karoti. Evaṃ devaloke devakumāro viya pañcahi kāmaguṇehi samappitassa samaṅgībhūtassa paricārayamānassa paṭikacceva niddā okkami, parijanassāpi niddā okkami, sabbarattiyo ca telapadīpo jhāyati. Atha kho yaso kulaputto paṭikacceva pabujjhitvā addasa sakaṃ parijanaṃ supantaṃ aññissā kacche vīṇaṃ, aññissā kaṇṭhe mudiṅgaṃ, aññissā kacche āḷambaraṃ, aññaṃ vikesikaṃ, vikkheḷikaṃ, aññā vippalapantiyo hatthapattaṃ susānaṃ maññe, disvānassa ādīnavo pāturahosi, nibbidāya cittaṃ saṇṭhāsi. Atha kho yaso kulaputto udānaṃ udānesi – “upaddutaṃ vata bho, upassaṭṭhaṃ vata bho”ti.

In the first Apadāna of the fifty-sixth chapter, the Apadāna of the Venerable Yasa begins with 'Having entered the great ocean,' and so on. He too had made his aspiration under previous Buddhas, accumulating in various existences merits that are a supporting condition for liberation. During the time of the Blessed Sumedha, he became a mighty nāga king. He led the community of bhikkhus headed by the Buddha to his palace and made a great offering. He clothed the Blessed One with a magnificent triple robe and each bhikkhu with a very valuable pair of cloths, along with all other requisites for ascetics. Through that meritorious deed, he wandered among devas and humans until, during the time of the Blessed Siddhattha, he was born as the son of a wealthy merchant and honored the great Bodhi-terrace with seven kinds of jewels. During the dispensation of the Blessed Kassapa, he went forth into homelessness and practiced the ascetic life. Thus, wandering only in happy destinies, during the time of our Blessed One, he was born in Bārāṇasī as the son of a very wealthy merchant. He was conceived in the womb of Sujātā, the merchant’s daughter, who had offered milk-rice to the Blessed One. He was named Yasa and was exceedingly delicate. He had three mansions—one for winter, one for summer, and one for the rainy season. In the rainy-season mansion, he spent the four months being attended by musical instruments played by women, never descending to the lower floors. In the winter mansion, he stayed for four months in rooms with well-fitted window shutters. In the summer mansion, he resided in rooms fitted with many windows and lattices. Due to the extreme delicacy of his hands and feet, he had no need to sit or perform any tasks on the ground. Instead, soft cushions filled with silk-cotton were spread, and he performed his activities upon them. Thus, like a young deva in the heavenly realm, he was served and fully endowed with the five strands of sensual pleasures. As he was being attended to, sleep overcame him early, and his attendants also fell asleep. Throughout the night, oil lamps burned. Then, the young man Yasa awoke early and saw his attendants asleep—one with a lute in her lap, another with a drum at her throat, another with a kettle-drum in her lap, some with disheveled hair, some drooling, others muttering in their sleep. He thought it was like a charnel ground. Seeing this, a sense of danger arose in him, and his mind settled into disenchantment. Then, the young man Yasa uttered this inspired exclamation: 'Distressed indeed, afflicted indeed!'

Atha [V 2.0267] kho yaso kulaputto suvaṇṇapādukāyo ārohitvā yena nivesanadvāraṃ tenupasaṅkami, amanussā dvāraṃ vivariṃsu – “mā yasassa kulaputtassa [P 0.0545] koci antarāyamakāsi agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajjāyā”ti. Atha kho yaso kulaputto yena nagaradvāraṃ tenupasaṅkami, amanussā dvāraṃ vivariṃsu – “mā yasassa kulaputtassa koci antarāyamakāsi agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajjāyā”ti. Atha kho yaso kulaputto yena isipatanaṃ migadāyo tenupasaṅkami.

Then the young man Yasa, having put on his golden sandals, approached the door of his dwelling. Non-human beings opened the door, saying, 'Let no one cause an obstruction to the young man Yasa going forth from the household life into homelessness.' Then the young man Yasa approached the city gate. Non-human beings opened the gate, saying, 'Let no one cause an obstruction to the young man Yasa going forth from the household life into homelessness.' Then the young man Yasa approached the Deer Park at Isipatana.

Tena kho pana samayena bhagavā rattiyā paccūsasamayaṃ paccuṭṭhāya ajjhokāse caṅkamati, addasā kho bhagavā yasaṃ kulaputtaṃ dūratova āgacchantaṃ, disvāna caṅkamā orohitvā paññatte āsane nisīdi. Atha kho yaso kulaputto bhagavato avidūre udānaṃ udānesi – “upaddutaṃ vata bho, upassaṭṭhaṃ vata bho”ti. Atha kho bhagavā yasaṃ kulaputtaṃ [M 2.0272] etadavoca – “idaṃ kho, yasa, anupaddutaṃ, idaṃ anupassaṭṭhaṃ, ehi, yasa, nisīda, dhammaṃ te desessāmī”ti. Atha kho yaso kulaputto, “idaṃ kira anupaddutaṃ, idaṃ anupassaṭṭha”nti haṭṭho udaggo suvaṇṇapādukāhi orohitvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi, ekamantaṃ nisinnassa kho yasassa kulaputtassa bhagavā anupubbiṃ kathaṃ kathesi, seyyathidaṃ, dānakathaṃ sīlakathaṃ saggakathaṃ kāmānaṃ ādīnavaṃ okāraṃ saṃkilesaṃ nekkhamme ānisaṃsaṃ pakāsesi. Yadā bhagavā aññāsi yasaṃ kulaputtaṃ kallacittaṃ muducittaṃ vinīvaraṇacittaṃ udaggacittaṃ pasannacittaṃ, atha yā buddhānaṃ sāmukkaṃsikā dhammadesanā, taṃ pakāsesi dukkhaṃ samudayaṃ nirodhaṃ maggaṃ. Seyyathāpi nāma suddhaṃ vatthaṃ apagatakāḷakaṃ sammadeva rajanaṃ paṭiggaṇheyya, evameva yasassa kulaputtassa tasmiṃyeva āsane virajaṃ vītamalaṃ dhammacakkhuṃ udapādi – “yaṃ kiñci samudayadhammaṃ, sabbaṃ taṃ nirodhadhamma”nti.

At that time, the Blessed One had risen at dawn and was walking in the open air. He saw the young man Yasa coming from afar. Seeing him, the Blessed One stepped down from his walking path and sat down on a prepared seat. Then the young man Yasa uttered this exclamation not far from the Blessed One: 'Distressed indeed, afflicted indeed!' Then the Blessed One said to the young man Yasa: 'This, Yasa, is not distressed. This is not afflicted. Come, Yasa, sit down. I will teach you the Dhamma.' Then the young man Yasa, thinking, 'This is indeed not distressed, this is not afflicted,' joyful and elated, took off his golden sandals and approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. To the young man Yasa sitting to one side, the Blessed One gave a progressive talk, that is to say, a talk on generosity, on virtue, on the heavens; he revealed the danger, degradation, and defilement of sensual pleasures and the benefit of renunciation. When the Blessed One knew that the young man Yasa's mind was malleable, soft, free from hindrances, uplifted, and serene, he revealed the teaching unique to the Buddhas: suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path. Just as a clean cloth free from stains would perfectly absorb dye, so too in the young man Yasa, while sitting right there, arose the dust-free, stainless vision of the Dhamma: 'Whatever is subject to arising is all subject to cessation.'

Atha kho yasassa kulaputtassa mātā pāsādaṃ abhiruhitvā yasaṃ kulaputtaṃ apassantī yena seṭṭhi gahapati tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā seṭṭhiṃ gahapatiṃ etadavoca – “putto te gahapati yaso na dissatī”ti. Atha kho, seṭṭhi gahapati, catuddisā assadūte uyyojetvā sāmaṃyeva yena isipatanaṃ migadāyo tenupasaṅkami. Addasā kho, seṭṭhi gahapati, suvaṇṇapādukānaṃ nikkhepaṃ, disvāna taṃyeva anugamāsi. Addasā kho bhagavā seṭṭhiṃ gahapatiṃ dūratova āgacchantaṃ, disvāna bhagavato etadahosi – “yaṃnūnāhaṃ tathārūpaṃ iddhābhisaṅkhāraṃ abhisaṅkhareyyaṃ, yathā seṭṭhi gahapati idha nisinno idha nisinnaṃ yasaṃ kulaputtaṃ na passeyyā”ti. Atha kho bhagavā tathārūpaṃ iddhābhisaṅkhāraṃ abhisaṅkharesi. Atha kho seṭṭhi gahapati yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami[P 0.0546][V 2.0268]; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “api, bhante, bhagavā yasaṃ kulaputtaṃ passeyyā”ti. Tena hi gahapati nisīda, appeva nāma idha nisinno idha nisinnaṃ yasaṃ kulaputtaṃ passeyyāsīti. Atha kho seṭṭhi gahapati “idheva kirāhaṃ nisinno idha nisinnaṃ yasaṃ kulaputtaṃ passissāmī”ti haṭṭho udaggo bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi, ekamantaṃ nisinnassa kho seṭṭhissa gahapatissa bhagavā anupubbiṃ kathaṃ kathesi…pe… aparappaccayo atthu sāsane bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “abhikkantaṃ bhante, abhikkantaṃ bhante, seyyathāpi[M 2.0273], bhante, nikkujjitaṃ vā ukkujjeyya, paṭicchannaṃ vā vivareyya mūḷhassa vā maggaṃ ācikkheyya, andhakāre vā telapajjotaṃ dhāreyya ‘cakkhumanto rūpāni dakkhantī’ti, evamevaṃ bhagavatā anekapariyāyena dhammo pakāsito. Esāhaṃ, bhante, bhagavantaṃ saraṇaṃ gacchāmi dhammañca bhikkhusaṅghañca, upāsakaṃ maṃ bhagavā dhāretu ajjatagge pāṇupetaṃ saraṇaṃ gata”nti. Sova loke paṭhamaṃ upāsako ahosi tevāciko.

Then the mother of the clansman Yasa, having ascended the mansion and not seeing the clansman Yasa, approached the merchant householder. Having approached, she said to the merchant householder: 'Householder, your son Yasa is not to be seen.' Then the merchant householder dispatched messengers on horseback in the four directions and himself went to Isipatana, the deer park. The merchant householder saw the golden sandals that had been cast off, and having seen them, he followed that very path. The Blessed One saw the merchant householder coming from afar, and upon seeing him, this thought occurred to the Blessed One: 'What if I were to perform such a psychic feat that the merchant householder, sitting here, would not see the clansman Yasa sitting here?' Then the Blessed One performed such a psychic feat. Then the merchant householder approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he said to the Blessed One: 'Venerable sir, might the Blessed One have seen the clansman Yasa?' 'Well then, householder, sit down. Perhaps while sitting here, you might see the clansman Yasa sitting here.' Then the merchant householder, delighted and elated, thinking, 'Surely, while sitting here, I will see the clansman Yasa sitting here,' paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. As the merchant householder sat to one side, the Blessed One gave him a progressive talk... having become independent of others in the Teacher's teaching, he spoke thus to the Blessed One: 'Excellent, venerable sir! Excellent, venerable sir! Just as one might set upright what was overturned, reveal what was hidden, show the way to one who is lost, or hold up an oil lamp in the darkness so that those with eyes might see forms, so has the Blessed One made the Dhamma clear in many ways. I go for refuge to the Blessed One, to the Dhamma, and to the Sangha of bhikkhus. May the Blessed One remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge from this day forward for as long as life lasts.' He was the first lay follower in the world with the threefold utterance.

Atha kho yasassa kulaputtassa pituno dhamme desiyamāne yathādiṭṭhaṃ yathāviditaṃ bhūmiṃ paccavekkhantassa anupādāya āyavehi cittaṃ vimucci. Atha kho bhagavato etadahosi – “yasassa kho kulaputtassa pituno dhamme desiyamāne yathādiṭṭhaṃ yathāviditaṃ bhūmiṃ paccavekkhantassa anupādāya āsavehi cittaṃ vimuttaṃ, abhabbo kho yaso kulaputto hīnāyāvattitvā kāme paribhuñjituṃ, seyyathāpi pubbe agārikabhūto, yaṃnūnāhaṃ taṃ iddhābhisaṅkhāraṃ paṭippassambheyya”nti. Atha kho bhagavā taṃ iddhābhisaṅkhāraṃ paṭippassambhesi. Addasā kho seṭṭhi gahapati yasaṃ kulaputtaṃ nisinnaṃ, disvāna yasaṃ kulaputtaṃ etadavoca – “mātā te tāta, yasa, paridevasokasamāpannā, dehi mātuyā jīvita”nti. Atha kho yaso kulaputto bhagavantaṃ ullokesi. Atha kho bhagavā seṭṭhiṃ gahapatiṃ etadavoca – “taṃ kiṃ maññasi, gahapati, yassa sekkhena ñāṇena sekkhena dassanena dhammo diṭṭho vidito seyyathāpi tayā, tassa yathādiṭṭhaṃ yathāviditaṃ bhūmiṃ paccavekkhantassa anupādāya āsavehi cittaṃ vimuttaṃ, bhabbo nu kho so, gahapati, hīnāyāvattitvā kāme paribhuñjituṃ seyyathāpi pubbe agārikabhūto”ti? “No hetaṃ, bhante”. “Yasassa kho, gahapati, kulaputtassa sekkhena ñāṇena sekkhena dassanena dhammo diṭṭho vidito seyyathāpi tayā, tassa yathādiṭṭhaṃ yathāviditaṃ bhūmiṃ paccavekkhantassa anupādāya āsavehi cittaṃ vimuttaṃ, abhabbo kho, gahapati, yaso kulaputto hīnāyāvattitvā kāme paribhuñjituṃ seyyathāpi pubbe agārikabhūto”ti. “Lābhā, bhante, yasassa kulaputtassa, suladdhaṃ, bhante, yasassa kulaputtassa[P 0.0547], yathā yasassa kulaputtassa anupādāya āsavehi cittaṃ vimuttaṃ, adhivāsetu me, bhante bhagavā, ajjatanāya bhattaṃ yasena kulaputtena pacchāsamaṇenā”ti[V 2.0269]. “Adhivāsesi bhagavā tuṇhībhāvena”. Atha kho seṭṭhi gahapati[M 2.0274], bhagavato adhivāsanaṃ viditvā uṭṭhāyāsanā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā pakkāmi. Atha kho yaso kulaputto acirapakkante seṭṭhimhi gahapatimhi bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “labheyyāhaṃ, bhante, bhagavato santike pabbajjaṃ, labheyyaṃ upasampada”nti. “Ehi bhikkhū”ti bhagavā avoca – “svākkhāto dhammo, cara brahmacariyaṃ sammā dukkhassa antakiriyāyā”ti, sāva tassa āyasmato upasampadā ahosi.

Then, while the Dhamma was being taught to the clansman Yasa’s father, the mind of the clansman Yasa, who was reflecting on the stage of truth as he had seen and known it, was liberated from the taints through non-clinging. Then this thought occurred to the Blessed One: 'While the Dhamma was being taught to his father, the mind of the clansman Yasa, who was reflecting on the stage of truth as he had seen and known it, has been liberated from the taints through non-clinging. It is impossible for the clansman Yasa to return to the lower life and enjoy sensual pleasures as he did before when he was a householder. Let me now withdraw that psychic feat.' Then the Blessed One withdrew that psychic feat. The merchant householder saw the clansman Yasa seated there, and upon seeing him, he said to the clansman Yasa: 'My dear Yasa, your mother is overcome with grief and lamentation. Give life back to your mother!' Then the clansman Yasa looked up at the Blessed One. The Blessed One then said to the merchant householder: 'What do you think, householder? If someone has seen and known the Dhamma with the knowledge and vision of a trainee, just as you have, and if, while reflecting on the stage of truth as he has seen and known it, his mind were liberated from the taints through non-clinging—would it be possible, householder, for him to return to the lower life and enjoy sensual pleasures as he did before when he was a householder?' 'No, venerable sir.' 'So it is, householder, with the clansman Yasa. He has seen and known the Dhamma with the knowledge and vision of a trainee, just as you have, and while reflecting on the stage of truth as he has seen and known it, his mind has been liberated from the taints through non-clinging. It is impossible, householder, for the clansman Yasa to return to the lower life and enjoy sensual pleasures as he did before when he was a householder.' 'It is a gain for the clansman Yasa, venerable sir! It is a great gain for the clansman Yasa, venerable sir, that his mind has been liberated from the taints through non-clinging. Venerable sir, may the Blessed One, with the clansman Yasa as his attendant monk, consent to a meal from me today.' The Blessed One consented by his silence. Then the merchant householder, having understood the Blessed One’s consent, rose from his seat, paid homage to the Blessed One, circumambulated him keeping his right side towards him, and departed. Then, not long after the merchant householder had left, the clansman Yasa said to the Blessed One: 'Venerable sir, may I receive the going forth in the Blessed One’s presence? May I receive the higher ordination?' 'Come, bhikkhu,' the Blessed One said, 'the Dhamma is well proclaimed. Live the holy life for the complete ending of suffering.' That was the venerable one’s higher ordination.

1. Arahā pana hutvā somanassajāto attano pubbacaritāpadānaṃ pakāsento mahāsamuddaṃ oggayhātiādimāha. Tattha samuddanti aṅgulimuddāya saṃ suṭṭhu dassetabbato samuddo, atha vā saṃ suṭṭhu udiyati khobhiyati pasodhiyati ghosanaṃ karonto āluḷiyatīti samuddo, mahanto ca so samuddo cāti mahāsamuddo, taṃ mahāsamuddaṃ. Oggayhāti ajjhogāhetvā abbhantaraṃ pavisitvā tassa mahāsamuddassa anto pavisitvā, sāmyatthe cetaṃ upayogavacananti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Bhavanaṃ me sumāpitanti ettha bhavanti nibbattanti nivasanti catūhi iriyāpathehi vāsaṃ kappenti etthāti bhavanaṃ, mayhaṃ taṃ bhavanaṃ taṃ vimānaṃ taṃ pāsādaṃ pañcapākārakūṭāgārehi saṃ suṭṭhu māpitaṃ nagaraṃ, attano balena suṭṭhu nimmitanti attho. Sunimmitā pokkharaṇīti sumahantā hutvā bhūtā itā gatā pavattā khaṇitā katāti pokkharaṇī, macchakacchapapupphapulinatitthamadhurodakādīhi suṭṭhu nibbattā nimmitāti attho. Cakkavākūpakūjitāti cakkavākakukkuṭahaṃsādīhi kūjitā ghositā nāditā sā pokkharaṇīti sambandho. Ito paraṃ nadīvanadvipadacatuppadapādapapakkhīnaṃ vaṇṇañca sumedhassa bhagavato dassanañca nimantetvā sumedhassa bhagavato dānakkamañca suviññeyyameva.

1. Then, having become an Arahant and filled with joy, he revealed the account of his past conduct, speaking of the great ocean and so on. Herein, 'samudda' (ocean) is so called because it is to be clearly shown with a finger gesture, or because it rises well, is agitated, is purified, makes a sound, and is stirred up—thus it is 'samudda.' And because it is a great ocean, it is 'mahāsamudda,' the great ocean. 'Oggayha' means having plunged into, having entered within, having gone inside that great ocean; this should be understood as a usage in a relational sense. In 'Bhavanaṃ me sumāpitaṃ,' 'bhavana' is where beings come to be, are born, and dwell, where they pass their time in the four postures. My dwelling, that celestial mansion, that palace, that city with five ramparts and gabled chambers, was well-made, meaning it was excellently created by my own power. 'Sunimmitā pokkharaṇī' means a great lotus pond that has come into being, existed, gone, flowed, been dug, and made; meaning it was well-formed and fashioned with fish, turtles, flowers, sandy banks, fords, sweet water, and so on. 'Cakkavākūpakūjitā' means that lotus pond resounded with the calls of ruddy geese, cocks, swans, and other birds—this is the connection. From here onward, the description of rivers, forests, bipeds, quadrupeds, trees, and birds, as well as the sight of the Blessed Sumedha, the invitation, and the manner of giving to the Blessed Sumedha, are easily understood.

Lokāhutipaṭiggahanti ettha loke āhuti lokāhuti, kāmarūpārūpasaṅkhātassa lokassa āhutiṃ pūjāsakkāraṃ paṭiggaṇhātīti lokāhutipaṭiggahaṃ, sumedhaṃ bhagavantanti attho. Sesaṃ byākaraṇadānañca arahattappattaphalañca suviññeyyamevāti.

'Lokāhutipaṭiggahaṃ'—here, 'lokāhuti' is an offering in the world. Because he receives the offerings, honor, and reverence of the world—that is, the world consisting of the realms of desire, form, and formlessness—he is called 'lokāhutipaṭiggahaṃ,' meaning the Blessed One Sumedha. The rest—the giving of the prophecy and the fruit of attaining Arahantship—is easily understood.

Yasattheraapadānavaṇṇanā samattā.

The commentary on the Apadāna of Elder Yasa is concluded.

2. Nadīkassapattheraapadānavaṇṇanā

2. The Commentary on the Apadāna of the Elder Nadīkassapa.

Dutiyāpadāne [M 2.0275][P 0.0548][V 2.0270] padumuttarassa bhagavatotiādikaṃ āyasmato nadīkassapattherassa apadānaṃ. Ayampi purimabuddhesu katādhikāro tattha tattha bhave vivaṭṭūpanissayāni puññāni upacinanto padumuttarassa bhagavato kāle kulagehe nibbattitvā viññutaṃ patto ekadivasaṃ satthāraṃ piṇḍāya carantaṃ disvā pasannamānaso attanā ropitassa ambarukkhassa paṭhamuppannaṃ manosilāvaṇṇaṃ ekaṃ ambaphalaṃ adāsi. So tena puññakammena devamanussesu saṃsaranto imasmiṃ buddhuppāde magadharaṭṭhe brāhmaṇakule uruvelakassapassa bhātā hutvā nibbatto vayappatto nissaraṇajjhāsayatāya gharāvāsaṃ anicchanto tāpasapabbajjaṃ pabbajitvā tīhi tāpasasatehi saddhiṃ nerañjarāya nadiyā tīre assamaṃ māpetvā viharati. Nadītīre vasanato kassapagottatāya ca nadīkassapoti samaññā ahosi. Tassa bhagavā saparisassa ehibhikkhubhāvena upasampadaṃ adāsi. So bhagavato gayāsīse ādittapariyāya desanāya (mahāva. 54; saṃ. ni. 4.28) arahatte patiṭṭhāsi.

The second Apadāna is that of the Venerable Elder Nadīkassapa, beginning with the Blessed One Padumuttara. He too, having performed meritorious deeds in the presence of previous Buddhas, accumulating merits that were a supporting condition for liberation in various existences, was born in a good family during the time of the Blessed One Padumuttara. Having reached maturity, one day he saw the Teacher walking for alms and, with a joyful mind, offered the first mango fruit from a mango tree he himself had planted, which was orpiment-colored. By the merit of that deed, he wandered on among devas and humans until, in this Buddha’s dispensation, he was born in a brahmin family in the Magadha country as the brother of Uruvelakassapa. Having reached maturity and not desiring household life due to his inclination for renunciation, he went forth into the ascetic’s life. With three hundred ascetics, he had a hermitage built on the bank of the Nerañjarā River and dwelt there. Because he lived by the river and belonged to the Kassapa clan, he became known as Nadīkassapa. The Blessed One gave him ordination with the “Come, bhikkhu” formula together with his retinue. At Gayāsīsa, during the Blessed One’s discourse on the Fire Sermon (Mahāvagga 54; Saṃyutta Nikāya 4.28), he was established in arahantship.

Tatrāyaṃ anupubbikathā – satthā yasaṃ kulaputtaṃ pabbājetvā uruvelāyaṃ tayo bhātikajaṭile dametuṃ yena uruvelā tadavasari. Tena kho pana samayena uruvelāyaṃ tayo jaṭilā paṭivasanti uruvelakassapo nadīkassapo gayākassapoti, tesu uruvelakassapo jaṭilo pañcannaṃ jaṭilasatānaṃ nāyako hoti vināyako aggo pamukho pāmokkho, nadīkassapo jaṭilo tiṇṇaṃ jaṭilasatānaṃ nāyako hoti vināyako aggo pamukho pāmokkho, gayākassapo jaṭilo dvinnaṃ jaṭilasatānaṃ nāyako hoti vināyako aggo pamukho pāmokkho. Atha kho bhagavā yena uruvelakassapassa jaṭilassa assamo tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā uruvelakassapaṃ jaṭilaṃ etadavoca – “sace te, kassapa, agaru, vaseyyāma ekarattaṃ agyāgāre”ti. Na kho me, mahāsamaṇa, garu, caṇḍettha nāgarājā iddhimā āsiviso ghoraviso, so taṃ mā viheṭhesīti. Dutiyampi kho bhagavā uruvelakassapaṃ jaṭilaṃ etadavoca…pe… tatiyampi…pe… so taṃ mā viheṭhesīti. Appeva maṃ na viheṭheyya, iṅgha tvaṃ, kassapa, anujānāhi agyāgāranti[M 2.0276]. Vihara, mahāsamaṇa, yathāsukhanti. Atha kho bhagavā agyāgāraṃ pavisitvā tiṇasanthārakaṃ paññapetvā nisīdi pallaṅkaṃ ābhujitvā ujuṃ kāyaṃ paṇidhāya parimukhaṃ satiṃ upaṭṭhapetvā.

Here is the sequential account: After ordaining Yasa, the young man of good family, the Teacher set out for Uruvelā to tame the three matted-hair brothers, and arrived there. Now at that time, three matted-hair ascetics were dwelling in Uruvelā: Uruvelā Kassapa, Nadī Kassapa, and Gayā Kassapa. Of these, Uruvelā Kassapa was the leader, guide, chief, foremost, and principal of five hundred matted-hair ascetics. Nadī Kassapa was the leader, guide, chief, foremost, and principal of three hundred matted-hair ascetics. Gayā Kassapa was the leader, guide, chief, foremost, and principal of two hundred matted-hair ascetics. Then the Blessed One approached the hermitage of Uruvelā Kassapa. Having approached, he said to Uruvelā Kassapa: “Kassapa, if it is no trouble to you, I would like to spend one night in the fire-hall.” “It is no trouble to me, Great Ascetic, but there is a fierce nāga-king here, powerful, a venomous snake with deadly venom; he might harm you.” A second time, the Blessed One said to Uruvelā Kassapa…pe… a third time…pe… “He might harm you.” “Perhaps he will not harm me. Please, Kassapa, grant me the use of the fire-hall.” “Stay, Great Ascetic, as you please.” Then the Blessed One entered the fire-hall, spread out a grass mat, sat down cross-legged, set his body erect, and established mindfulness in front of him.

Addasā kho so nāgo bhagavantaṃ paviṭṭhaṃ, disvā dummano padhūpāyi. Atha kho bhagavato etadahosi [V 2.0271] – “yaṃnūnāhaṃ imassa nāgassa anupahacca chaviñca cammañca [P 0.0549] maṃsañca nhāruñca aṭṭhiñca aṭṭhimiñjañca tejasā tejaṃ pariyādiyeyya”nti. Atha kho bhagavā tathārūpaṃ iddhābhisaṅkhāraṃ abhisaṅkharitvā padhūpāyi. Atha kho so nāgo makkhaṃ asahamāno pajjali. Bhagavāpi tejodhātuṃ samāpajjitvā pajjali. Ubhinnaṃ sajotibhūtānaṃ agyāgāraṃ ādittaṃ viya hoti sampajjalitaṃ sajotibhūtaṃ. Atha kho te jaṭilā agyāgāraṃ parivāretvā evamāhaṃsu – “abhirūpo vata, bho, mahāsamaṇo nāgena viheṭhiyatī”ti. Atha kho bhagavā tassā rattiyā accayena tassa nāgassa anupahacca chaviñca cammañca maṃsañca nhāruñca aṭṭhiñca aṭṭhimiñjañca tejasā tejaṃ pariyādiyitvā patte pakkhipitvā uruvelakassapassa jaṭilassa dassesi – “ayaṃ te, kassapa, nāgo pariyādinno assa tejasā tejo”ti. Atha kho uruvelakassapassa jaṭilassa etadahosi – “mahiddhiko kho mahāsamaṇo mahānubhāvo, yatra hi nāma caṇḍassa nāgarājassa iddhimato āsivisassa ghoravisassa tejasā tejaṃ pariyādiyissati, na tveva kho arahā yathā aha”nti.

The nāga saw the Blessed One entering and, upon seeing him, became distressed and emitted smoke. Then the Blessed One thought: “Why don’t I, without harming this nāga’s skin, hide, flesh, sinews, bones, or marrow, overpower his fire with my own fire?” Then the Blessed One generated such a psychic formation and emitted smoke. Unable to endure his anger, the nāga blazed forth. The Blessed One, too, entered the fire element and blazed forth. For the two, being radiant, the fire-hall was as if ablaze, fully blazing, radiant. Then the matted-hair ascetics surrounded the fire-hall and said: “Alas, the handsome great ascetic is being tormented by the nāga!” When the night had passed, the Blessed One, having overpowered the nāga’s fire with his own fire without harming his skin, hide, flesh, sinews, bones, or marrow, placed him in his almsbowl and showed him to Uruvelā Kassapa, the matted-hair ascetic, saying: “Here, Kassapa, is your nāga, his fire overpowered by my fire.” Then Uruvelā Kassapa thought: “The great ascetic is indeed of great psychic power and great might, in that he has overpowered the fire of this fierce, powerful nāga-king, a venomous snake of deadly poison. Yet he is not an arahant as I am.”

“Nerañjarāyaṃ bhagavā, uruvelakassapaṃ jaṭilaṃ avoca;

Sace te kassapa agaru, viharemu ajjaṇho aggisālamhī”ti.

At the Nerañjarā, the Blessed One said to the matted-hair ascetic Uruvelā Kassapa:

“If it is no trouble to you, Kassapa,

Let us dwell tonight in the fire-hall.”

“Na kho me mahāsamaṇa garu, phāsukāmova taṃ nivāremi;

Caṇḍettha nāgarājā, iddhimā āsiviso ghoraviso;

So taṃ mā viheṭhesī”ti.

“It is not a burden to me, great ascetic; desiring your comfort, I restrain you.

A fierce nāga-king is here, powerful, a venomous snake of deadly poison;

May he not harm you.”

“Appeva [M 2.0277] maṃ na viheṭheyya, iṅgha tvaṃ kassapa anujānāhi agyāgāranti;

Dinnanti naṃ viditvā, abhīto pāvisi bhayamatīto.

“Perhaps he will not harm me. Please, Kassapa, grant me the fire-hall.”

Knowing it was given, fearless, he entered, having transcended fear.

“Disvā isiṃ paviṭṭhaṃ, ahināgo dummano padhūpāyi;

Sumanamanaso adhimano, manussanāgopi tattha padhūpāyi.

Seeing the sage who had entered, the serpent-king, displeased, emitted smoke;

With a joyful mind and elated heart, the human nāga also emitted smoke there.

“Makkhañca asahamāno, ahināgo pāvakova pajjali;

Tejodhātusukusalo, manussanāgopi tattha pajjali.

Unable to endure his anger, the serpent-king blazed forth like a fire;

Skilled in the fire element, the human nāga also blazed forth there.

“Ubhinnaṃ [V 2.0272] sajotibhūtānaṃ,

Agyāgāraṃ ādittaṃ hoti sampajjalitaṃ sajotibhūtaṃ;

Udicchare jaṭilā, abhirūpo vata bho mahāsamaṇo;

Nāgena viheṭhiyatīti bhaṇanti.

For the two, being radiant,

The fire-hall was ablaze, fully blazing, radiant;

The matted-hair ascetics exclaimed: “Alas, the handsome great ascetic!

He is being tormented by the nāga!” they declared.

“Atha tassā rattiyā accayena, hatā nāgassa acciyo honti;

Iddhimato pana ṭhitā, anekavaṇṇā acciyo honti.

Then, at the end of that night, the nāga’s flames were extinguished;

But for the one endowed with psychic power, multicolored flames remained.

“Nīlā atha lohitikā, mañjiṭṭhā pītakā phalikavaṇṇāyo;

Aṅgīrasassa kāye, anekavaṇṇā acciyo honti.

Blue, then red, madder, yellow, crystal-colored:

On Aṅgīrasa’s body, flames of many colors were.

“Pattamhi odahitvā, ahināgaṃ brāhmaṇassa dassesi;

Ayaṃ te kassapa nāgo, pariyādinno assa tejasā tejo”ti.

Having placed the serpent in the bowl, he showed it to the brahmin, saying:

“This, Kassapa, is your nāga, his fire overpowered by my fire.”

Atha [M 2.0278] kho uruvelakassapo jaṭilo bhagavato iminā iddhipāṭihāriyena abhippasanno bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “idheva, mahāsamaṇa, vihara, ahaṃ te dhuvabhattenā”ti.

Then Uruvelā Kassapa, the matted-hair ascetic, being deeply impressed by this miracle of the Blessed One, said to him: “Stay here, Great Ascetic, I will provide you with regular food.”

Paṭhamaṃ pāṭihāriyaṃ.

The first miracle.

Atha [P 0.0550] kho bhagavā uruvelakassapassa jaṭilassa assamassa avidūre aññatarasmiṃ vanasaṇḍe vihāsi. Atha kho cattāro mahārājāno abhikkantāya rattiyā abhikkantavaṇṇā kevalakappaṃ vanasaṇḍaṃ obhāsetvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā catuddisā aṭṭhaṃsu seyyathāpi mahantā aggikkhandhā. Atha kho uruvelakassapo jaṭilo tassā rattiyā accayena yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “kālo, mahāsamaṇa, niṭṭhitaṃ bhattaṃ, te nu kho te, mahāsamaṇa, abhikkantāya rattiyā abhikkantavaṇṇā kevalakappaṃ vanasaṇḍaṃ obhāsetvā yena tvaṃ tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā taṃ abhivādetvā catuddisā aṭṭhaṃsu seyyathāpi mahantā aggikkhandhā”ti. Ete kho, kassapa, cattāro mahārājāno yenāhaṃ tenupasaṅkamiṃsu dhammassavanāyāti. Atha kho uruvelakassapassa jaṭilassa etadahosi – “mahiddhiko kho mahāsamaṇo mahānubhāvo, yatra hi nāma cattāropi mahārājāno upasaṅkamissanti dhammassavanāya, na tveva ca kho arahā yathā aha”nti[V 2.0273]. Atha kho bhagavā uruvelakassapassa jaṭilassa bhattaṃ bhuñjitvā tasmiṃyeva vanasaṇḍe vihāsi.

Then the Blessed One dwelt in a certain grove not far from the hermitage of Uruvelā Kassapa, the matted-hair ascetic. Then, when the night was far advanced, the Four Great Kings, with surpassing radiance, illuminating the entire grove, approached the Blessed One. Having approached, they paid homage to the Blessed One and stood in the four directions, just as great masses of fire. Then, when the night had passed, Uruvelā Kassapa the matted-hair ascetic approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he said to the Blessed One: “It is time, great ascetic, the meal is ready. Who were those, great ascetic, who, when the night was far advanced, with surpassing radiance, illuminating the entire grove, approached you; having approached, they paid homage to you and stood in the four directions just as great masses of fire?” “Those, Kassapa, were the Four Great Kings who came to me to hear the Dhamma.” Then Uruvelā Kassapa the matted-hair ascetic thought: “The great ascetic is indeed of great psychic power and great might, in that even the Four Great Kings come to hear the Dhamma. Yet he is not an arahant as I am.” Then the Blessed One, having eaten the meal from Uruvelā Kassapa the matted-hair ascetic, stayed in that same grove.

Dutiyaṃ pāṭihāriyaṃ.

The second miracle.

Atha kho sakko devānamindo abhikkantāya rattiyā abhikkantavaṇṇo kevalakappaṃ vanasaṇḍaṃ obhāsetvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi seyyathāpi mahāaggikkhandho purimāhi vaṇṇanibhāhi abhikkantataro ca paṇītataro ca. Atha kho uruvelakassapo jaṭilo tassā rattiyā accayena yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “kālo, mahāsamaṇa, niṭṭhitaṃ bhattaṃ, ko nu kho so, mahāsamaṇa, abhikkantāya [M 2.0279] rattiyā abhikkantavaṇṇo kevalakappaṃ vanasaṇḍaṃ obhāsetvā yena tvaṃ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā taṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi seyyathāpi mahāaggikkhandho purimāhi vaṇṇanibhāhi abhikkantataro ca paṇītataro cā”ti. Eso kho, kassapa, sakko devānamindo yenāhaṃ tenupasaṅkami dhammassavanāyāti. Atha kho uruvelakassapassa jaṭilassa etadahosi – “mahiddhiko kho mahāsamaṇo mahānubhāvo, yatra hi nāma sakkopi devānamindo upasaṅkamissati dhammassavanāya, na tveva ca kho arahā yathā aha”nti[P 0.0551]. Atha kho bhagavā uruvelakassapassa jaṭilassa bhattaṃ bhuñjitvā tasmiṃyeva vanasaṇḍe vihāsi.

Then, when the night was far advanced, Sakka, lord of the devas, with his surpassing radiance illuminating the entire grove, approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One and stood to one side, like a great mass of fire, more brilliant and sublime than his previous radiances. Then, when the night had passed, Uruvela Kassapa the matted-hair ascetic approached the Blessed One and said: “It is time, great ascetic, the meal is ready. Who was it, great ascetic, who, when the night was far advanced, with his surpassing radiance illuminating the entire grove, approached you, paid homage to you, and stood to one side, like a great mass of fire, more brilliant and sublime than his previous radiances?” “That, Kassapa, was Sakka, lord of the devas, who approached me to hear the Dhamma.” Then this thought occurred to Uruvela Kassapa the matted-hair ascetic: “The great ascetic is truly of great psychic power and might, since even Sakka, lord of the devas, approaches him to hear the Dhamma. Yet he is not an arahant like me.” Then the Blessed One, having eaten the meal of Uruvela Kassapa the matted-hair ascetic, remained in that same grove.

Tatiyaṃ pāṭihāriyaṃ.

The third wonder.

Atha kho brahmā sahampati abhikkantāya rattiyā abhikkantavaṇṇo kevalakappaṃ vanasaṇḍaṃ obhāsetvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi seyyathāpi mahāaggikkhandho purimāhi vaṇṇanibhāhi abhikkantataro ca paṇītataro ca. Atha kho uruvelakassapo jaṭilo tassā rattiyā accayena yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “kālo, mahāsamaṇa, niṭṭhitaṃ bhattaṃ, ko nu kho so, mahāsamaṇa, abhikkantāya rattiyā abhikkantavaṇṇo kevalakappaṃ vanasaṇḍaṃ obhāsetvā yena tvaṃ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā taṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi seyyathāpi mahāaggikkhandho purimāhi vaṇṇanibhāhi abhikkantataro ca paṇītataro cā”ti. Eso kho, kassapa, brahmā sahampati yenāhaṃ tenupasaṅkami dhammassavanāyāti. Atha kho uruvelakassapassa jaṭilassa etadahosi – “mahiddhiko kho mahāsamaṇo mahānubhāvo, yatra hi nāma brahmāpi sahampati upasaṅkamissati [V 2.0274] dhammassavanāya, na tveva ca kho arahā yathā aha”nti. Atha kho bhagavā uruvelakassapassa jaṭilassa bhattaṃ bhuñjitvā tasmiṃyeva vanasaṇḍe vihāsi.

Then, when the night was far advanced, Brahmā Sahampati, with his surpassing radiance illuminating the entire grove, approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One and stood to one side, like a great mass of fire, more brilliant and sublime than his previous radiances. Then, when the night had passed, Uruvela Kassapa the matted-hair ascetic approached the Blessed One and said: “It is time, great ascetic, the meal is ready. Who was it, great ascetic, who, when the night was far advanced, with his surpassing radiance illuminating the entire grove, approached you, paid homage to you, and stood to one side, like a great mass of fire, more brilliant and sublime than his previous radiances?” “That, Kassapa, was Brahmā Sahampati, who approached me to hear the Dhamma.” Then this thought occurred to Uruvela Kassapa the matted-hair ascetic: “The great ascetic is truly of great psychic power and might, since even Brahmā Sahampati approaches him to hear the Dhamma. Yet he is not an arahant like me.” Then the Blessed One, having eaten the meal of Uruvela Kassapa the matted-hair ascetic, remained in that same grove.

Catutthaṃ pāṭihāriyaṃ.

The fourth wonder.

Tena kho pana samayena uruvelakassapassa jaṭilassa mahāyañño paccupaṭṭhito hoti, kevalakappā ca aṅgamagadhā pahūtaṃ khādanīyaṃ bhojanīyaṃ [M 2.0280] ādāya abhikkamitukāmā honti. Atha kho uruvelakassapassa jaṭilassa etadahosi – “etarahi kho me mahāyañño paccupaṭṭhito, kevalakappā ca aṅgamagadhā pahūtaṃ khādanīyaṃ bhojanīyaṃ ādāya abhikkamissanti, sace mahāsamaṇo mahājanakāye iddhipāṭihāriyaṃ karissati, mahāsamaṇassa lābhasakkāro abhivaḍḍhissati, mama lābhasakkāro parihāyissati, aho nūna mahāsamaṇo svātanāya nāgaccheyyā”ti. Atha kho bhagavā uruvelakassapassa jaṭilassa cetasā cetoparivitakkamaññāya uttarakuruṃ gantvā tato piṇḍapātaṃ āharitvā anotattadahe paribhuñjitvā tattheva divāvihāraṃ akāsi. Atha kho uruvelakassapo jaṭilo tassā rattiyā accayena yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “kālo, mahāsamaṇa, niṭṭhitaṃ bhattaṃ, kiṃ nu kho, mahāsamaṇa, hiyyo nāgamāsi, apica mayaṃ taṃ sarāma, ‘kiṃ nu kho mahāsamaṇo nāgacchatī’ti, khādanīyassa ca bhojanīyassa [P 0.0552] ca te paṭivīso ṭhapito”ti. Nanu te, kassapa, etadahosi – “etarahi kho me mahāyañño paccupaṭṭhito kevalakappā ca aṅgamagadhā pahūtaṃ khādanīyaṃ bhojanīyaṃ ādāya abhikkamissanti, sace mahāsamaṇo mahājanakāye iddhipāṭihāriyaṃ karissati, mahāsamaṇassa lābhasakkāro abhivaḍḍhissati, mama lābhasakkāro parihāyissati, aho nūna mahāsamaṇo svātanāya nāgaccheyyā”ti, so kho ahaṃ, kassapa, tava cetasā cetoparivitakkamaññāya uttarakuruṃ gantvā tato piṇḍapātaṃ āharitvā anotattadahe paribhuñjitvā tattheva divāvihāraṃ akāsinti. Atha kho uruvelakassapassa jaṭilassa etadahosi – “mahiddhiko kho mahāsamaṇo mahānubhāvo, yatra hi nāma cetasāpi cittaṃ pajānissati, na tveva ca kho arahā yathā aha”nti. Atha kho bhagavā uruvelakassapassa jaṭilassa bhattaṃ bhuñjitvā tasmiṃyeva vanasaṇḍe vihāsi.

At that time, a great sacrifice had been prepared for Uruvela Kassapa the matted-hair ascetic, and the entire populace of Aṅga and Magadha wanted to come bringing abundant hard and soft food. Then this thought occurred to Uruvela Kassapa the matted-hair ascetic: ‘Now this great sacrifice has been prepared for me, and the entire populace of Aṅga and Magadha will come bringing abundant hard and soft food. If the great ascetic performs a wonder of psychic power in this great assembly, his gain and honor will increase, while my gain and honor will diminish. If only the great ascetic would not come tomorrow!’ Then the Blessed One, having known with his own mind the thought in the mind of Uruvela Kassapa, went to Uttarakuru, brought almsfood from there, ate it by the Anotatta Lake, and spent the day there. Then, when the night had passed, Uruvela Kassapa the matted-hair ascetic approached the Blessed One and said: “It is time, great ascetic, the meal is ready. Why did you not come yesterday, great ascetic? We were thinking of you: ‘Why has the great ascetic not come?’ A portion of the hard and soft food was set aside for you.” “Kassapa, did not this thought occur to you: ‘Now this great sacrifice has been prepared for me, and the entire populace of Aṅga and Magadha will come bringing abundant hard and soft food. If the great ascetic performs a wonder of psychic power in this great assembly, his gain and honor will increase, while my gain and honor will diminish. If only the great ascetic would not come tomorrow!’? That is why, Kassapa, having known with my own mind the thought in your mind, I went to Uttarakuru, brought almsfood from there, ate it by the Anotatta Lake, and spent the day there.” Then this thought occurred to Uruvela Kassapa the matted-hair ascetic: “The great ascetic is truly of great psychic power and might, in that he knows my mind with his own. Yet he is not an arahant like me.” Then the Blessed One, having eaten the meal of Uruvela Kassapa the matted-hair ascetic, remained in that same grove.

Pañcamaṃ pāṭihāriyaṃ.

The fifth wonder.

Tena [V 2.0275] kho pana samayena bhagavato paṃsukūlaṃ uppannaṃ hoti. Atha kho bhagavato etadahosi – “kattha nu kho ahaṃ paṃsukūlaṃ dhoveyya”nti? Atha kho sakko devānamindo bhagavato cetasā cetoparivitakkamaññāya [M 2.0281] pāṇinā pokkharaṇiṃ khaṇitvā bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “idha, bhante bhagavā, paṃsukūlaṃ dhovatū”ti. Atha kho bhagavato etadahosi – “kimhi nu kho ahaṃ paṃsukūlaṃ parimaddeyya”nti? Atha kho sakko devānamindo bhagavato cetasā cetoparivitakkamaññāya mahatiṃ silaṃ upanikkhipi – “idha, bhante bhagavā, paṃsukūlaṃ parimaddatū”ti. Atha kho bhagavato etadahosi – “kimhi nu kho ahaṃ ālambitvā uttareyya”nti? Atha kho kakudhe adhivatthā devatā bhagavato cetasā cetoparivitakkamaññāya sākhaṃ onāmesi – “idha, bhante bhagavā, ālambitvā uttaratū”ti. Atha kho bhagavato etadahosi – “kimhi nu kho ahaṃ paṃsukūlaṃ vissajjeyya”nti? Atha kho sakko devānamindo bhagavato cetasā cetoparivitakkamaññāya mahatiṃ silaṃ upanikkhipi – “idha, bhante bhagavā, paṃsukūlaṃ vissajjetū”ti. Atha kho uruvelakassapo jaṭilo tassā rattiyā accayena yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “kālo, mahāsamaṇa, niṭṭhitaṃ bhattaṃ, kiṃ nu kho, mahāsamaṇa, nāyaṃ pubbe idha pokkharaṇī sāyaṃ idha pokkharaṇī, nayimā silā pubbe upanikkhittā, kenimā silā upanikkhittā, nayimassa kakudhassa pubbe sākhā onatā, sāyaṃ sākhā onatā”ti? Idha me, kassapa, paṃsukūlaṃ uppannaṃ [P 0.0553] ahosi, tassa mayhaṃ, kassapa, etadahosi – “kattha nu kho ahaṃ paṃsukūlaṃ dhoveyya”nti? Atha kho, kassapa, sakko devānamindo mama cetasā cetoparivitakkamaññāya pāṇinā pokkharaṇiṃ khaṇitvā maṃ etadavoca – “idha, bhante bhagavā, paṃsukūlaṃ dhovatū”ti. Sāyaṃ, kassapa, amanussena pāṇinā khaṇitā pokkharaṇī. Tassa mayhaṃ, kassapa, etadahosi – “kimhi nu kho ahaṃ paṃsukūlaṃ parimaddeyya”nti? Atha kho, kassapa, sakko devānamindo mama cetasā cetoparivitakkamaññāya mahatiṃ silaṃ upanikkhipi – “idha, bhante bhagavā, paṃsukūlaṃ parimaddatū”ti? Sāyaṃ, kassapa, amanussena upanikkhittā silā. Tassa mayhaṃ, kassapa, etadahosi – “kimhi nu kho ahaṃ ālambitvā uttareyya”nti? Atha kho, kassapa, kakudhe adhivatthā devatā mama cetasā cetoparivitakkamaññāya sākhaṃ onāmesi – “idha, bhante bhagavā, ālambitvā uttaratū”ti? Svāyaṃ āharahattho kakudho. Tassa mayhaṃ, kassapa, etadahosi – “kimhi nu kho ahaṃ paṃsukūlaṃ vissajjeyya”nti? Atha kho, kassapa, sakko devānamindo mama cetasā cetoparivitakkamaññāya [M 2.0282] mahatiṃ silaṃ upanikkhipi – “idha, bhante bhagavā, paṃsukūlaṃ vissajjetū”ti? Sāyaṃ, kassapa, amanussena upanikkhittā silāti. Atha kho uruvelakassapassa etadahosi – “mahiddhiko mahāsamaṇo mahānubhāvo[V 2.0276], yatra hi nāma sakkopi devānamindo veyyāvaccaṃ karissati, na tveva ca kho arahā yathā aha”nti. Atha kho bhagavā uruvelakassapassa jaṭilassa bhattaṃ bhuñjitvā tasmiṃyeva vanasaṇḍe vihāsi.

Now at that time, a rag-robe had been acquired by the Blessed One. Then the Blessed One thought: “Where can I wash this rag-robe?” Then Sakka, ruler of the devas, having known with his own mind the direction of the Blessed One’s thoughts, dug a pond with his hand and said to the Blessed One: “Here, Bhante, let the Blessed One wash the rag-robe.” Then the Blessed One thought: “On what can I scrub this rag-robe?” Then Sakka, ruler of the devas, having known with his own mind the direction of the Blessed One’s thoughts, set down a large stone slab and said: “Here, Bhante, let the Blessed One scrub the rag-robe.” Then the Blessed One thought: “Holding on to what can I get out?” Then the deity dwelling in a kakudha tree, having known with his own mind the direction of the Blessed One’s thoughts, bent down a branch and said: “Here, Bhante, holding on to this, let the Blessed One get out.” Then the Blessed One thought: “On what can I spread out this rag-robe?” Then Sakka, ruler of the devas, having known with his own mind the direction of the Blessed One’s thoughts, set down a large stone slab and said: “Here, Bhante, let the Blessed One spread out the rag-robe.” Then, when the night had passed, Uruvelā Kassapa the matted-hair ascetic went to the Blessed One and said to him: “It is time, great ascetic, the meal is ready. But, great ascetic, this pond was not here before; now it is here. These stone slabs were not placed here before; by whom have they been placed here? This branch of the kakudha tree was not bent down before; now it is bent down.” “Here, Kassapa, a rag-robe had been acquired by me. Then, Kassapa, this thought occurred to me: ‘Where can I wash this rag-robe?’ Then, Kassapa, Sakka, ruler of the devas, having known with his own mind the direction of my thoughts, dug a pond with his hand and said to me: ‘Here, Bhante, let the Blessed One wash the rag-robe.’ This pond, Kassapa, was dug by the hand of a non-human. Then, Kassapa, this thought occurred to me: ‘On what can I scrub this rag-robe?’ Then, Kassapa, Sakka, ruler of the devas, having known with his own mind the direction of my thoughts, set down a large stone slab and said: ‘Here, Bhante, let the Blessed One scrub the rag-robe.’ This stone slab, Kassapa, was set down by a non-human. Then, Kassapa, this thought occurred to me: ‘Holding on to what can I get out?’ Then, Kassapa, the deity dwelling in a kakudha tree, having known with his own mind the direction of my thoughts, bent down a branch and said: ‘Here, Bhante, holding on to this, let the Blessed One get out.’ This kakudha tree has its branch bent down. Then, Kassapa, this thought occurred to me: ‘On what can I spread out this rag-robe?’ Then, Kassapa, Sakka, ruler of the devas, having known with his own mind the direction of my thoughts, set down a large stone slab and said: ‘Here, Bhante, let the Blessed One spread out the rag-robe.’ This stone slab, Kassapa, was set down by a non-human.” Then this thought occurred to Uruvelā Kassapa: “The great ascetic is of great psychic power and great might, in that even Sakka, ruler of the devas, will attend upon him. Still, he is not an arahant as I am.” Then the Blessed One, having eaten the meal of Uruvelā Kassapa the matted-hair ascetic, dwelt in that same grove.

Atha kho uruvelakassapo jaṭilo tassā rattiyā accayena yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavato kālaṃ ārocesi – “kālo, mahāsamaṇa, niṭṭhitaṃ bhatta”nti. “Gaccha tvaṃ, kassapa, āyāmaha”nti uruvelakassapaṃ jaṭilaṃ uyyojetvā yāya jambuyā jambudīpo paññāyati, tato phalaṃ gahetvā paṭhamataraṃ āgantvā agyāgāre nisīdi. Addasā kho uruvelakassapo jaṭilo bhagavantaṃ agyāgāre nisinnaṃ, disvāna bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “katamena tvaṃ, mahāsamaṇa, maggena āgato, ahaṃ tayā paṭhamataraṃ pakkanto, so tvaṃ paṭhamataraṃ āgantvā agyāgāre nisinno”ti? “Idhāhaṃ, kassapa, taṃ uyyojetvā yāya jambuyā jambudīpo paññāyati, tato phalaṃ gahetvā paṭhamataraṃ āgantvā agyāgāre nisinno. Idaṃ kho, kassapa, jambuphalaṃ vaṇṇasampannaṃ gandhasampannaṃ rasasampannaṃ, sace ākaṅkhasi paribhuñjā”ti. “Alaṃ, mahāsamaṇa, tvaṃyeva taṃ arahasi, tvaṃyeva taṃ paribhuñjā”ti. Atha kho uruvelakassapassa jaṭilassa etadahosi – “mahiddhiko kho mahāsamaṇo mahānubhāvo, yatra hi nāma maṃ paṭhamataraṃ uyyojetvā yāya jambuyā [P 0.0554] jambudīpo paññāyati, tato phalaṃ gahetvā paṭhamataraṃ āgantvā agyāgāre nisīdissati, na tveva ca kho arahā yathā aha”nti. Atha kho bhagavā uruvelakassapassa jaṭilassa bhattaṃ bhuñjitvā tasmiṃyeva vanasaṇḍe vihāsi.

Then, when the night had passed, Uruvelā Kassapa the matted-hair ascetic went to the Blessed One and announced the time: “It is time, great ascetic, the meal is ready.” “You go, Kassapa; I will come.” Having sent off Uruvelā Kassapa the matted-hair ascetic, the Blessed One went to the rose-apple tree from which Jambudīpa gets its name, took a fruit from there, and, arriving back first, sat down in the fire-hut. Uruvelā Kassapa the matted-hair ascetic saw the Blessed One sitting in the fire-hut and said to him: “By which path did you come, great ascetic? I departed before you, but you have arrived first and are sitting in the fire-hut.” “Having sent you off, Kassapa, I went to the rose-apple tree from which Jambudīpa gets its name, took a fruit from there, and, arriving back first, sat down in the fire-hut. This rose-apple fruit, Kassapa, is endowed with color, fragrance, and taste. If you wish, eat it.” “No, great ascetic, you are the one who deserves it. You eat it.” Then this thought occurred to Uruvelā Kassapa the matted-hair ascetic: “The great ascetic is of great psychic power and great might, in that he can send me off first, go to the rose-apple tree from which Jambudīpa gets its name, take a fruit from there, and, arriving back first, sit down in the fire-hut. Still, he is not an arahant as I am.” Then the Blessed One, having eaten the meal of Uruvelā Kassapa the matted-hair ascetic, dwelt in that same grove.

Atha kho uruvelakassapo jaṭilo tassā rattiyā accayena yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavato kālaṃ ārocesi – “kālo, mahāsamaṇa, niṭṭhitaṃ bhatta”nti. “Gaccha tvaṃ, kassapa, āyāmaha”nti uruvelakassapaṃ jaṭilaṃ uyyojetvā yāya jambuyā jambudīpo paññāyati, tassā avidūre ambo…pe… tassā avidūre āmalakī…pe… [M 2.0283] tassā avidūre harītakī…pe… tāvatiṃsaṃ gantvā pāricchattakapupphaṃ gahetvā paṭhamataraṃ āgantvā agyāgāre nisīdi. Addasā kho uruvelakassapo jaṭilo bhagavantaṃ agyāgāre nisinnaṃ, disvāna bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “katamena tvaṃ, mahāsamaṇa, maggena āgato, ahaṃ tayā paṭhamataraṃ pakkanto, so tvaṃ paṭhamataraṃ āgantvā agyāgāre nisinno”ti? “Idhāhaṃ, kassapa, taṃ uyyojetvā tāvatiṃsaṃ gantvā pāricchattakapupphaṃ gahetvā paṭhamataraṃ āgantvā agyāgāre nisinno. Idaṃ kho, kassapa, pāricchattakapupphaṃ vaṇṇasampannaṃ gandhasampannaṃ, sace ākaṅkhasi gaṇhā”ti[V 2.0277]. “Alaṃ, mahāsamaṇa, tvaṃyeva taṃ arahasi, tvaṃyeva taṃ gaṇhā”ti. Atha kho uruvelakassapassa jaṭilassa etadahosi – “mahiddhiko kho mahāsamaṇo mahānubhāvo, yatra hi nāma maṃ paṭhamataraṃ uyyojetvā tāvatiṃsaṃ gantvā pāricchattakapupphaṃ gahetvā paṭhamataraṃ āgantvā agyāgāre nisīdissati, na tveva ca kho arahā yathā aha”nti.

Then, when the night had passed, Uruvelā Kassapa the matted-hair ascetic went to the Blessed One and announced the time: “It is time, great ascetic, the meal is ready.” “You go, Kassapa; I am coming.” Having sent off Uruvelā Kassapa the matted-hair ascetic, the Blessed One went to the Jambu tree from which Jambudīpa is known, then to a nearby mango tree… a nearby emblic myrobalan… a nearby yellow myrobalan… then went to the Tāvatiṃsa heaven, took a Pāricchattaka flower, and, arriving back first, sat down in the fire-hut. Uruvelā Kassapa the matted-hair ascetic saw the Blessed One sitting in the fire-hut and said to him: “By which path did you come, great ascetic? I departed before you, but you have arrived first and are sitting in the fire-hut.” “Having sent you off, Kassapa, I went to the Tāvatiṃsa heaven, took a Pāricchattaka flower, and, arriving back first, sat down in the fire-hut. This Pāricchattaka flower, Kassapa, is endowed with color and fragrance. If you wish, take it.” “Let it be, great ascetic; you are the one who deserves it. You take it.” Then this thought occurred to Uruvelā Kassapa the matted-hair ascetic: “The great ascetic is of great psychic power and great might, in that he can send me off first, go to the Tāvatiṃsa heaven, take a Pāricchattaka flower, and, arriving back first, sit down in the fire-hut. Still, he is not an arahant as I am.”

Tena kho pana samayena te jaṭilā aggiṃ paricaritukāmā na sakkonti kaṭṭhāni phāletuṃ. Atha kho tesaṃ jaṭilānaṃ etadahosi – “nissaṃsayaṃ kho mahāsamaṇassa iddhānubhāvo yathā mayaṃ na sakkoma kaṭṭhāni phāletu”nti. Atha kho bhagavā uruvelakassapaṃ [P 0.0555] jaṭilaṃ etadavoca – “phāliyantu, kassapa, kaṭṭhānī”ti. “Phāliyantu, mahāsamaṇā”ti. Sakideva pañca kaṭṭhasatāni phāliyiṃsu. Atha kho uruvelakassapassa jaṭilassa etadahosi – “mahiddhiko kho mahāsamaṇo mahānubhāvo, yatra hi nāma kaṭṭhānipi phāliyissanti, na tveva ca kho arahā yathā aha”nti.

Now at that time, those matted-hair ascetics, wishing to attend to the fire, could not split the firewood. Then this thought occurred to those matted-hair ascetics: “Without a doubt, it is because of the great ascetic’s psychic power that we cannot split the firewood.” Then the Blessed One said to Uruvelā Kassapa the matted-hair ascetic: “Let the logs be split, Kassapa.” “Let them be split, great ascetic!” And all at once the five hundred logs split apart. Then this thought occurred to Uruvelā Kassapa the matted-hair ascetic: “The great ascetic is of great psychic power and great might, in that the logs split apart. Still, he is not an arahant as I am.”

Tena kho pana samayena te jaṭilā aggiṃ paricaritukāmā na sakkonti aggiṃ ujjaletuṃ. Atha kho tesaṃ jaṭilānaṃ etadahosi – “nissaṃsayaṃ kho mahāsamaṇassa iddhānubhāvo yathā mayaṃ na sakkoma aggiṃ ujjaletu”nti. Atha kho bhagavā uruvelakassapaṃ jaṭilaṃ etadavoca – “ujjaliyantu, kassapa, aggī”ti. “Ujjaliyantu, mahāsamaṇā”ti. Sakideva pañca aggisatāni ujjaliyiṃsu. Atha kho uruvelakassapassa jaṭilassa etadahosi – “mahiddhiko kho mahāsamaṇo mahānubhāvo, yatra hi nāma aggīpi ujjaliyissanti, na tveva ca kho arahā yathā aha”nti.

At that time, those matted-hair ascetics, wishing to tend their fires, were unable to light them. Then this thought occurred to those matted-hair ascetics: “Without a doubt, it is by the great ascetic’s psychic power that we are unable to light the fires.” Then the Blessed One said to Uruvelā Kassapa the matted-hair ascetic: “Let the fires be lit, Kassapa.” “Let them be lit, great ascetic.” At once, the five hundred fires blazed up. Then this thought occurred to Uruvelā Kassapa the matted-hair ascetic: “The great ascetic is truly of great psychic power and might, since even the fires blaze up. Yet he is not an arahant like me.”

Tena [M 2.0284] kho pana samayena te jaṭilā aggiṃ paricaritvā na sakkonti aggiṃ vijjhāpetuṃ. Atha kho tesaṃ jaṭilānaṃ etadahosi – “nissaṃsayaṃ kho mahāsamaṇassa iddhānubhāvo yathā mayaṃ na sakkoma aggiṃ vijjhāpetu”nti. Atha kho bhagavā uruvelakassapaṃ jaṭilaṃ etadavoca – “vijjhāyantu, kassapa, aggī”ti. “Vijjhāyantu, mahāsamaṇā”ti. Sakideva pañca aggisatāni vijjhāyiṃsu. Atha kho uruvelakassapassa jaṭilassa etadahosi – “mahiddhiko kho mahāsamaṇo mahānubhāvo, yatra hi nāma aggīpi vijjhāyissanti, na tveva ca kho arahā yathā aha”nti.

At that time, those matted-hair ascetics, having tended their fires, were unable to extinguish them. Then this thought occurred to those matted-hair ascetics: “Without a doubt, it is by the great ascetic’s psychic power that we are unable to extinguish the fires.” Then the Blessed One said to Uruvelā Kassapa the matted-hair ascetic: “Let the fires be extinguished, Kassapa.” “Let them be extinguished, great ascetic.” At once, the five hundred fires were extinguished. Then this thought occurred to Uruvelā Kassapa the matted-hair ascetic: “The great ascetic is truly of great psychic power and might, since even the fires are extinguished. Yet he is not an arahant like me.”

Tena kho pana samayena te jaṭilā sītāsu hemantikāsu rattīsu antaraṭṭhakāsu himapātasamaye [V 2.0278] najjā nerañjarāya ummujjantipi nimujjantipi ummujjananimujjanampi karonti. Atha kho bhagavā pañcamattāni mandāmukhisatāni abhinimmini yattha te jaṭilā uttaritvā visibbesuṃ. Atha kho tesaṃ jaṭilānaṃ etadahosi – “nissaṃsayaṃ kho mahāsamaṇassa iddhānubhāvo yathayimā mandāmukhiyo nimmitā”ti. Atha kho uruvelakassapassa jaṭilassa etadahosi – “mahiddhiko kho mahāsamaṇo mahānubhāvo, yatra hi nāma tāva bahū mandāmukhiyopi abhinimminissati, na tveva ca kho arahā yathā aha”nti.

At that time, during the cold winter nights of the ‘between-the-eights’ period, at the time of snowfall, those matted-hair ascetics were plunging into and emerging from the Nerañjarā River, performing the rite of plunging and emerging. Then the Blessed One created five hundred braziers, where those matted-hair ascetics, having come out of the water, could warm themselves. Then this thought occurred to those matted-hair ascetics: “Without a doubt, it is by the great ascetic’s psychic power that these braziers have been created.” Then this thought occurred to Uruvelā Kassapa the matted-hair ascetic: “The great ascetic is truly of great psychic power and might, in that he can create so many braziers. Yet he is not an arahant like me.”

Tena kho pana samayena mahā akālamegho pāvassi, mahā udakavāhako sañjāyi, yasmiṃ padese bhagavā viharati so padeso udakena na otthaṭo hoti. Atha kho bhagavato etadahosi – “yaṃnūnāhaṃ samantā udakaṃ ussāretvā majjhe reṇuhatāya bhūmiyā caṅkameyya”nti. Atha kho bhagavā samantā udakaṃ ussāretvā majjhe reṇuhatāya bhūmiyā caṅkami. Atha kho uruvelakassapo jaṭilo “māheva kho mahāsamaṇo udakena vūḷho ahosī”ti nāvāya sambahulehi jaṭilehi saddhiṃ yasmiṃ padese bhagavā viharati, taṃ padesaṃ agamāsi. Addasā kho uruvelakassapo jaṭilo bhagavantaṃ [P 0.0556] samantā udakaṃ ussāretvā majjhe reṇuhatāya bhūmiyā caṅkamantaṃ, disvāna bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “idaṃ nu tvaṃ, mahāsamaṇā”ti. “Ayamahamasmi, kassapā”ti bhagavā vehāsaṃ abbhuggantvā nāvāya paccuṭṭhāsi. Atha kho uruvelakassapassa jaṭilassa etadahosi – “mahiddhiko kho mahāsamaṇo mahānubhāvo[M 2.0285], yatra hi nāma udakampi na pavāhissati, na tveva ca kho arahā yathā aha”nti.

Now at that time, a great untimely rain cloud poured down, and a great flood arose. Yet the place where the Blessed One was dwelling was not inundated by the water. Then it occurred to the Blessed One: 'What if I were to push back the water all around and walk back and forth on the dust-cleared ground in the middle?' So the Blessed One pushed back the water all around and walked back and forth on the dust-cleared ground in the middle. Then Uruvela Kassapa, the matted-hair ascetic, thought: 'Lest the great ascetic has been swept away by the water!' So he took a boat and, accompanied by many matted-hair ascetics, went to the place where the Blessed One was staying. Uruvela Kassapa saw the Blessed One pushing back the water all around and walking back and forth on the dust-cleared ground in the middle. Upon seeing him, he said to the Blessed One: 'Is that you, great ascetic?' 'It is I, Kassapa,' replied the Blessed One, and rising into the air, he alighted in the boat. Then it occurred to Uruvela Kassapa, the matted-hair ascetic: 'The great ascetic is indeed of great psychic power and great might, in that the water did not sweep him away. Yet he is not an arahant like me.'

Atha kho bhagavato etadahosi – “cirampi kho imassa moghapurisassa evaṃ bhavissati ‘mahiddhiko kho mahāsamaṇo mahānubhāvo, na tveva ca kho arahā yathā aha’nti, yaṃnūnāhaṃ imaṃ jaṭilaṃ saṃvejeyya”nti. Atha kho bhagavā uruvelakassapaṃ jaṭilaṃ etadavoca – “neva ca kho tvaṃ, kassapa, arahā, nāpi arahattamaggasamāpanno, sāpi te paṭipadā natthi, yāya tvaṃ arahā vā assasi arahattamaggaṃ vā samāpanno”ti. Atha kho uruvelakassapo jaṭilo bhagavato pādesu sirasā nipatitvā bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “labheyyāhaṃ, bhante, bhagavato santike pabbajjaṃ, labheyyaṃ upasampada”nti. “Tvaṃ khosi, kassapa, pañcannaṃ jaṭilasatānaṃ nāyako vināyako aggo pamukho pāmokkho, tepi tāva apalokehi, yathā te maññissanti, tathā te karissantī”ti. Atha kho uruvelakassapo jaṭilo yena te jaṭilā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā te jaṭile etadavoca – “icchāmahaṃ, bho, mahāsamaṇe brahmacariyaṃ carituṃ, yathā bhavanto maññanti tathā karontū”ti. “Cirapaṭikā mayaṃ, bho, mahāsamaṇe abhippasannā, sace bhavaṃ [V 2.0279] mahāsamaṇe brahmacariyaṃ carissati, sabbeva mayaṃ mahāsamaṇe brahmacariyaṃ carissāmā”ti. Atha kho te jaṭilā kesamissaṃ jaṭāmissaṃ khārikājamissaṃ aggihutamissaṃ udake pavāhetvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavato pādesu sirasā nipatitvā bhagavantaṃ etadavocuṃ – “labheyyāma mayaṃ, bhante, bhagavato santike pabbajjaṃ, labheyyāma upasampada”nti. “Etha, bhikkhavo”ti bhagavā avoca – “svākkhāto dhammo, caratha brahmacariyaṃ sammā dukkhassa antakiriyāyā”ti. Sāva tesaṃ āyasmantānaṃ upasampadā ahosi.

Then it occurred to the Blessed One: “For a long time this foolish man will think: ‘The great ascetic is of great psychic power and great might, but he is not an arahant like me.’ What if I were to stir this matted-hair ascetic?” Then the Blessed One said to Uruvela Kassapa the matted-hair ascetic: “You, Kassapa, are not an arahant, nor have you entered upon the path to arahantship. Nor do you have that practice by which you might become an arahant or enter upon the path to arahantship.” Then Uruvela Kassapa the matted-hair ascetic, having prostrated with his head at the Blessed One’s feet, said to the Blessed One: “May I receive the going forth in the Blessed One's presence, venerable sir, may I receive the full ordination?” “You, Kassapa, are the leader, guide, chief, foremost, and principal of five hundred matted-hair ascetics. First consult with them; they will do as they think fit.” Then Uruvela Kassapa the matted-hair ascetic went to those matted-hair ascetics and said to them: “Sirs, I wish to lead the holy life under the great ascetic. Do as you think fit.” “For a long time, sir, we have had faith in the great ascetic. If you, sir, will lead the holy life under the great ascetic, we will all lead the holy life under him.” Then those matted-hair ascetics let their hair, their matted locks, their carrying poles with belongings, and their fire-sacrifice implements float away on the water and went to the Blessed One. Having approached, they prostrated with their heads at the Blessed One’s feet and said to him: “May we receive the going forth in the Blessed One's presence, venerable sir, may we receive the full ordination?” “Come, bhikkhus,” the Blessed One said. “The Dhamma is well expounded. Live the holy life for the complete ending of suffering.” That itself was the full ordination for those venerable ones.

Addasā kho nadīkassapo jaṭilo kesamissaṃ jaṭāmissaṃ khārikājamissaṃ aggihutamissaṃ udake vuyhamāne, disvānassa etadahosi – “māheva me bhātuno upasaggo ahosī”ti, jaṭile pāhesi – “gacchatha me bhātaraṃ jānāthā”ti, sāmañca tīhi jaṭilasatehi saddhiṃ yenāyasmā uruvelakassapo tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ [P 0.0557] uruvelakassapaṃ etadavoca – “idaṃ nu kho, kassapa, seyyo”ti? “Āmāvuso, idaṃ seyyo”ti. Atha kho te jaṭilā kesamissaṃ jaṭāmissaṃ khārikājamissaṃ aggihutamissaṃ [M 2.0286] udake pavāhetvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavato pādesu sirasā nipatitvā bhagavantaṃ etadavocuṃ – “labheyyāma mayaṃ, bhante, bhagavato santike pabbajjaṃ, labheyyāma upasampada”nti. “Etha, bhikkhavo”ti bhagavā avoca – “svākkhāto dhammo, caratha brahmacariyaṃ sammā dukkhassa antakiriyāyā”ti. Sāva tesaṃ āyasmantānaṃ upasampadā ahosi.

Nadī Kassapa the matted-hair ascetic saw the hair, matted locks, carrying poles with belongings, and fire-sacrifice implements being carried along by the water. Having seen them, it occurred to him: “Lest some misfortune has befallen my brother!” He sent some matted-hair ascetics, saying: “Go and find out about my brother.” And he himself, along with three hundred matted-hair ascetics, went to the Venerable Uruvela Kassapa. Having approached, he said to the Venerable Uruvela Kassapa: “Is this better, Kassapa?” “Yes, friend, this is better.” Then those matted-hair ascetics let their hair, their matted locks, their carrying poles with belongings, and their fire-sacrifice implements float away on the water and went to the Blessed One. Having approached, they prostrated with their heads at the Blessed One’s feet and said to him: “May we receive the going forth in the Blessed One's presence, venerable sir, may we receive the full ordination?” “Come, bhikkhus,” the Blessed One said. “The Dhamma is well expounded. Live the holy life for the complete ending of suffering.” That itself was the full ordination for those venerable ones.

Addasā kho gayākassapo jaṭilo kesamissaṃ jaṭāmissaṃ khārikājamissaṃ aggihutamissaṃ udake vuyhamāne, disvānassa etadahosi – “māheva me bhātūnaṃ upasaggo ahosī”ti, jaṭile pāhesi – “gacchatha me bhātaro jānāthā”ti, sāmañca dvīhi jaṭilasatehi saddhiṃ yenāyasmā uruvelakassapo tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ uruvelakassapaṃ etadavoca – “idaṃ nu kho, kassapa, seyyo”ti? “Āmāvuso, idaṃ seyyo”ti. Atha kho te jaṭilā kesamissaṃ jaṭāmissaṃ khārikājamissaṃ aggihutamissaṃ udake pavāhetvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavato pādesu sirasā nipatitvā bhagavantaṃ etadavocuṃ – “labheyyāma mayaṃ, bhante, bhagavato santike pabbajjaṃ, labheyyāma upasampada”nti. “Etha, bhikkhavo”ti, bhagavā avoca – “svākkhāto dhammo, caratha brahmacariyaṃ sammā dukkhassa antakiriyāyā”ti. Sāva tesaṃ āyasmantānaṃ upasampadā ahosi.

Gayā Kassapa the matted-hair ascetic saw the hair, matted locks, carrying poles with belongings, and fire-sacrifice implements being carried along by the water. Having seen them, it occurred to him: “Lest some misfortune has befallen my brothers!” He sent some matted-hair ascetics, saying: “Go and find out about my brothers.” And he himself, along with two hundred matted-hair ascetics, went to the Venerable Uruvela Kassapa. Having approached, he said to the Venerable Uruvela Kassapa: “Is this better, Kassapa?” “Yes, friend, this is better.” Then those matted-hair ascetics let their hair, their matted locks, their carrying poles with belongings, and their fire-sacrifice implements float away on the water and went to the Blessed One. Having approached, they prostrated with their heads at the Blessed One’s feet and said to him: “Venerable sir, may we receive the going forth under the Blessed One, may we receive the full ordination?” “Come, bhikkhus,” the Blessed One said. “The Dhamma is well expounded. Live the holy life for the complete ending of suffering.” That itself was the full ordination for those venerable ones.

“Bhagavato [V 2.0280] adhiṭṭhānena pañca kaṭṭhasatāni na phāliyiṃsu, phāliyiṃsu, aggī na ujjaliyiṃsu, ujjaliyiṃsu, na vijjhāyiṃsu, vijjhāyiṃsu, pañca mandāmukhisatāni abhinimmini, etena nayena aḍḍhuḍḍhapāṭihāriyasahassāni honti.

By the Blessed One's determination, five hundred pieces of firewood would not split, then they split; the fires would not blaze, then they blazed; they would not be extinguished, then they were extinguished. He manifested five hundred braziers. In this way, there were one and a half thousand miracles.

“Atha kho bhagavā uruvelāyaṃ yathābhirantaṃ viharitvā yena gayāsīsaṃ tena cārikaṃ pakkāmi mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṃ sahassena sabbeheva purāṇajaṭilehi. Tatra sudaṃ bhagavā gayāyaṃ viharati gayāsīse saddhiṃ bhikkhusahassena. Tatra kho bhagavā bhikkhu āmantesi (saṃ. ni. 4.28) – ‘sabbaṃ, bhikkhave, ādittaṃ, kiñca, bhikkhave, sabbaṃ ādittaṃ, cakkhu, bhikkhave, ādittaṃ, rūpā ādittā, cakkhuviññāṇaṃ [M 2.0287] ādittaṃ, cakkhusamphasso āditto, yamidaṃ cakkhusamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṃ sukhaṃ vā dukkhaṃ vā adukkhamasukhaṃ vā tampi [P 0.0558] ādittaṃ. Kena ādittaṃ, rāgagginā dosagginā mohagginā ādittaṃ, jātiyā jarāya maraṇena sokehi paridevehi dukkhehi domanassehi upāyāsehi ādittanti vadāmi? Sotaṃ ādittaṃ, saddā ādittā…pe… ghānaṃ ādittaṃ, gandhā ādittā…pe… jivhā ādittā, rasā ādittā…pe… kāyo āditto, phoṭṭhabbā ādittā…pe… mano āditto, dhammā ādittā, manoviññāṇaṃ ādittaṃ, manosamphasso āditto, yamidaṃ manosamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṃ sukhaṃ vā dukkhaṃ vā adukkhamasukhaṃ vā tampi ādittaṃ. Kena ādittaṃ, rāgagginā dosagginā mohagginā ādittaṃ, jātiyā jarāya maraṇena sokehi paridevehi dukkhehi domanassehi upāyāsehi āditta’”nti vadāmi.

Then the Blessed One, having stayed at Uruvelā as long as he pleased, set out on a journey to Gayāsīsa with a great Saṅgha of bhikkhus—a thousand in all, all former matted-hair ascetics. There the Blessed One stayed at Gayā, at Gayāsīsa, together with the thousand bhikkhus. There the Blessed One addressed the bhikkhus: “Bhikkhus, all is burning. And what, bhikkhus, is the all that is burning? The eye, bhikkhus, is burning, forms are burning, eye-consciousness is burning, eye-contact is burning, and whatever feeling arises conditioned by eye-contact—whether pleasant, painful, or neither-painful-nor-pleasant—that too is burning.
